Acute muscle or musculotendinous strain: protect, restore pain-free movement, progressively load, then speed and sport demands.
Direct-blow muscle or soft-tissue bruise: protect early, restore range, then progressive loading.
Joint hyperextension trauma: structural injury screened first, then protected range and end-range control before loading.
Ligament sprain and symptomatic joint instability: protected movement, control and balance, progressive loading, then reactive and sport demands.
Painful joint irritation or impingement: settle symptoms, restore range and control, then load through tolerated range.
Symptom reports without a tissue diagnosis (pain, soreness, tightness, stiffness, swelling): symptom-led, conservative, no diagnosis implied.
Tendon pain and tendinopathy: load management through isometric, then heavier slow, then energy-storage loading.

Adjust provoking activity and avoid staying in one position for long periods. Soreness does not establish DOMS; do not use forceful neck self-testing. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.
Advise athlete to elevate the area above heart and wrap with compression sleeve. → SPP: remove if bruising fades, switch to pump/flush circuits.
Advise light compression wrap and elevation above heart for 10–15 min post-training. → SPP: if pain subsides, begin reintroducing low RPE movement.

After the acute period, only if your treating clinician has advised self-massage, gently roll comfortable quadriceps tissue. Avoid bruised or painful tissue and stop for pain. Do not roll an acute strain or treat rolling as readiness for loading. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

After the acute period, only if your treating clinician has advised self-massage, use gentle superficial pressure over comfortable hamstring tissue. Avoid the injured or bruised area. Stop for pain. Do not use a massage gun on an acute strain or treat massage as clearance to run or kick. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Air squats, light swings, or open chain movement to keep blood moving without stress. → SPP: increase ROM and tempo gradually as pain subsides.
Apply compression bandage, then perform gentle mobility drills to reduce swelling without provoking flare-up.
Apply localized heat for 10 min, then transition into controlled movement or CARs to expand usable range.
Apply slow lowering to regain ROM (e.g. leg lowers, tempo dips, etc). 3x6 reps. → SPP: layer in anti-extension isometrics (e.g. plank drag).

Avoid positions or activities in which the joint feels unsafe or gives way. Keep it comfortably supported and follow any clinician-directed restrictions. Arrange assessment for new or repeated giving way. Suspected dislocation, subluxation, severe pain, deformity or loss of sensation needs medical assessment; do not test the joint with hops, end-range stretches or perturbations.

Balance on the affected leg on a fixed foam pad beside stable support with eyes open. Keep the surface and position fixed; do not add perturbations or fatigue work. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Band retraction, extension, rotation drills. 3 sets light resistance.

Begin only once pain has settled, you no longer need crutches and you can stand on your toes without pain. Hold a stable chair, share your weight equally over both feet and gently rise onto your toes, then lower slowly. Work at your own pace and stop if painful. Keep both feet on level ground; do not add weight, single-leg work, a step or fatigue progressions.

Beside stable support on firm level ground, raise both heels, then transfer weight to the affected leg and slowly lower its heel only to the floor. Do not use a step, lower into deep dorsiflexion, increase depth or add speed or weight. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Change position rather than holding the neck still for long periods. Keep gentle ordinary movement; do not force range or remove prescribed protection. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Change positions and keep comfortable ordinary activity. Avoid prolonged bed rest and forced range; no diagnosis or measured mobility deficit is inferred. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Change positions and keep gentle ordinary neck movement. Tightness does not prove shortened tissue; avoid forceful stretching, traction or pressure on the neck. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.
Contract opposing muscles near end range to protect joint integrity.
Contract-relax against resistance (e.g. doorway press, glute bridge hold). 3x20s. → SPP: build into controlled eccentrics or flowing mobility reps.
Controlled lengthening under band tension to stimulate tendon healing without overload.
Elevate the limb above heart level. Perform light squeezes or quad/glute sets to stimulate fluid return.
Engage large muscle groups without load; avoid pain. Hold 15–30s x 3 rounds.
Focus on 3–4 joint circles or controlled articulations paired with slow nasal breathing. → SPP: convert to low-load tempo exercises for the affected region.

From hands and knees on firm ground, gently shift weight back and return while the wrists stay comfortable. Keep the knees down; no full plank, speed work or forced extension. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

From hands and knees on firm ground, gently shift weight between the hands through a small comfortable range. Keep both hands down; no arm reaches or instability challenge. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Hold a kettlebell upside down with the elbow bent close to the side and walk slowly on level ground over one fixed short distance. Use an individually selected fixed weight; no overhead carry or perturbations. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Hold positions just short of lockout to train tissue safety and reinforce control at terminal ranges.
Hold split stance, tall plank, or single leg positions on foam pad or BOSU. 3x20–30s. → SPP: Add light perturbation (e.g. partner taps, ball tosses).

Hold stable support and move the affected leg slowly inward against a fixed light cable resistance through a comfortable range. Keep the trunk still. No speed, resistance increase or fatigue progression within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Hold static contractions near the range of irritation to reinforce tendon capacity and reduce pain sensitivity.
Ice/heat alternated 3–5x per area, then slow joint circles or band ROM drills. → SPP: remove passive input, use self-mobilizing drills only.
Include inchworms, world’s greatest stretch, deep lunge opens. 2–3 rounds. → SPP: add mild loaded mobility (e.g. goblet squat hold, elevated Cossack stretch).
Isometric tension at pain-free end ranges, hold 30s. 3–4 sets daily.

Keep both feet on level ground. Lean into a stable wall and gently press through the forefeet without moving the ankles. Hold only while comfortable, then relax. No band, single-leg variant or fatigue work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Keep comfortable daily activity and change position as needed. Reduce provoking tasks without prolonged bed rest; no cause of the back pain is inferred. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Keep comfortable ordinary elbow movement without forceful end-range work. Stiffness alone does not establish a movement restriction or its cause. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Keep gentle ordinary wrist movement and reduce clearly provoking tasks. Do not add resistance or force range merely because the wrist feels stiff. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Keep the affected upper arm comfortably by your side and slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a pain-free range with the hand empty. Do not force end range, squeeze a ball, perform wrist curls or add resistance. A red, hot or swollen elbow needs assessment before exercise. This baseline does not diagnose lateral, medial or posterior tendon involvement. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Keep the elbow comfortably bent by the side and gently press the back of the hand into a towel against a stable wall without movement, then relax. No forced range or added resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Keep the hand relaxed and gently bend and straighten the affected fingers through a small comfortable range. Do not make a forceful fist, pull the fingers with the other hand, tap a pad or grip an object. Follow individual protection and movement restrictions and stop if the movement provokes the bruised fingers. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Keep the upper arm supported, palm facing up and elbow in comfortable mid-flexion. Resist gently with the other hand without movement, then relax. Keep pressure fixed; no added load or fatigue work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Lean forward with your uninjured hand on a stable support and let the affected arm hang relaxed. Allow small gentle forward-and-back and side-to-side swings within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force overhead movement, add weights or perform presses. Follow any individual restrictions given by your clinician. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Lean forward with your uninjured hand on a stable support and let the affected arm hang relaxed. Gently allow small, comfortable forward-and-back and side-to-side swings. Keep the movement pain-free. Do not add weights, force the range or perform presses. Stop if symptoms worsen. Follow any individual movement restrictions given by your treating clinician.
Lie down and elevate the bruised limb. Perform light flexion/extension to improve circulation and reduce pooling.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet resting on the floor. Gently tilt the pelvis to flatten the lower back slightly, then return slowly to neutral. Keep movement small and comfortable, breathe normally, and do not force an arch or hold tension. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Lie on your back with the affected knee comfortably bent and the foot resting on the surface. Slowly let the knee move a small amount outwards, then return to the starting position within a pain-free range. Keep the pelvis supported. Do not cross the knee inward, pull it towards the chest, force a deep rotation position or add a band. This replaces the extreme seated hip-switch positions with protected rotation. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

Lie supported on your back and hold a fixed individually selected kettlebell with both hands. Slowly press and lower through a comfortable range while maintaining a gentle inward grip. No load increase or fatigue work; demand depends on the selected weight. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Low RPE movement with mobility and breath pacing. 3–4 rounds.
Massage gun or lacrosse ball across the stuck tissue pre-movement. → SPP: replace with movement-based mobility under low load.
Mid-range holds for joint stiffness without movement. Build neuromuscular confidence.
Mobility tied to exhale. Repeat sequence x3 rounds full body.
Mobilize through dynamic movement. Emphasize rhythmic motion, not static stretching.
Move through safe ranges under tension. Avoid painful arcs, build capsule space.

On firm level ground, perform small two-foot pogo jumps with a fixed low height. No single-leg work, added weight, increased speed or fatigue progression. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand and slowly bend and straighten it within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force straightening, carry weights or push through the arm. Follow any clinician-directed movement restrictions. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand. Slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force straightening, carry weights or add curl resistance. Stop if pain or swelling increases. This is gentle movement for an uncomplicated muscle strain, not a tendon tear or repair protocol.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand. Slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force the elbow straight, push against a wall or add resistance. Stop if pain or swelling increases. This is gentle movement for an uncomplicated muscle strain, not a tendon tear or repair protocol.

Once symptoms have settled enough for comfortable movement, lie on the affected side with the upper leg supported out of the way. Slowly lift and lower the lower leg through a small comfortable range. Keep the work pain-free and self-paced. Stop if groin pain increases during or after the work. Do not add ankle weights, cables, fast repetitions or fatigue work.

Once the ankle is less painful, sit with the foot supported and gently move it up and down or trace the alphabet. Start with a small comfortable amount and build gradually. Keep within a comfortable range; do not force movement.

Only if individually advised to use an overhead position, hold a fixed light band overhead and walk slowly over a fixed short distance. No oscillations, range increase or fatigue work. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if individually advised, perform small quick finger taps onto a firm surface with clinician-directed tape. Keep speed and force fixed. Tape does not establish readiness or protect against every injury. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly bend and straighten the elbow against a fixed light band. Do not force straightening, increase resistance or work to fatigue. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly pull a fixed light band apart through a small range and return under control. No increased tension, end-range stretch or faster movement. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly straighten and bend the elbow against a fixed light resistance band. Do not force end range, increase band resistance or work to fatigue. This is resisted loading, not early movement. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the shoulder-height position is comfortable, hold the elbow bent at a right angle and gently resist external rotation with the other hand without movement. No forced position or fatigue hold. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only when standing and weight bearing are comfortable, stand beside a stable counter and gently balance on the affected leg on firm, level ground with support available and eyes open. Stop if the ankle gives way or feels unsafe. Do not hop, use a cushion, close your eyes or work to fatigue. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Passive recovery aid to flush DOMS. 15–20 mins soak or 5 cycles of hot/cold shower. → SPP: reserve for high soreness or poor sleep.

Perform a small two-foot jump onto a fixed foam pad and settle the landing. Keep the height and surface fixed; no repeated bouncing or perturbation. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Perform one small lateral hop on firm level ground and settle the landing before the next attempt. Keep distance fixed; no fast repeated hops or contact. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place both hands against a stable wall at chest height and gently press without moving the shoulders. Release between comfortable holds. Do not increase force, extend the hold to fatigue or add resisted movement within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place both hands on a stable raised table and perform a slow supported incline push-up through a comfortable elbow range, then return. Keep the support height fixed. Do not transition to floor work, a reverse tabletop or speed work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the affected hand against a stable wall at a comfortable height and hold gently without moving. No climbing higher, forced overhead position or added resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the affected hand lightly on a stable wall with the elbow comfortably straight. Slowly slide the hand through a small comfortable range; do not lock or force the elbow, press hard or add resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the forearms on a foam roller against a wall. Slowly slide only through a comfortable range and return under control. Use no additional band or weight; do not force overhead range. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Protect the affected toe from being bent backwards again. Pause provoking push-off, tiptoe work, running and jumping. Rest the foot in a comfortable supported position. Follow any individually prescribed footwear, walking support or weight-bearing restriction without changing it. The affected toe, joint stability and injury grade need assessment before toe curls, stretching or loaded forefoot work; this guidance does not diagnose turf toe. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

Protect the bruised back of the upper arm from contact, heavy pressing and resisted elbow straightening. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow individual movement/support restrictions. Do not apply vibration balls, force an overhead stretch or increase arm-circle range to test recovery. Automatic stretching or resistance work needs an assessed injury and is not prescribed here. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised elbow from contact, leaning on the injured area, heavy carrying and forceful pressing. Support the arm comfortably without pressure on the bruise and follow any individual sling or movement restriction. Do not apply a massage gun or push the elbow against a wall to build contact tolerance. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised fingers from catching impacts, punching, heavy grip and direct pressure. Rest the hand comfortably supported and follow any prescribed finger protection or movement restriction. Do not tap the fingers on a pad, grip a cold ball or roll the injured tissue to test contact tolerance. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised forearm from contact, heavy grip work and resisted wrist movement. Support the arm comfortably without pressing on the bruise and follow any prescribed support or movement restriction. Do not roll a ball over the injured tissue or use a band as a recovery flush. Increasing tight swelling, abnormal sensation or circulation needs assessment rather than further loading. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised front of the upper arm from contact, heavy pulling and repeated resisted elbow bending. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow individual movement/support restrictions. Avoid direct massage or percussion, forceful stretching and faster arm swings to test tolerance. A muscle bruise label does not exclude deeper muscle or tendon injury; automatic resistance or stretching is not prescribed. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised hand from heavy gripping, carrying, punching and direct pressure. Rest it comfortably supported and follow any individually prescribed hand protection. Do not use contrast heat, ball pressure or a resisted grip squeeze as automatic treatment. New loss of movement or grip, excessive or increasing swelling, or altered sensation needs assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Stay seated; no weights, band, pressure on the knees, step, forced range or automatic increase. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit or lie with the affected leg supported on a smooth surface. Gently slide the heel towards you to bend the knee, then slide back to straighten within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force movement, stand on an unstable surface or add resistance. Stop and seek assessment if the knee locks, repeatedly gives way or cannot bear weight. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit supported with the affected arm relaxed by your side. Gently draw the shoulder blade back and down without forcing the shoulder into end range, then relax. Keep the movement small and comfortable. Stop if the joint feels as though it is slipping. Do not add weights, overhead work or stretching. Suspected dislocation or subluxation needs medical assessment. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit upright with shoulders relaxed. Slowly turn the head a small comfortable amount to one side, then return to the middle. Use unassisted movement only; no neck circles, forced range, resistance, traction or sustained stretch. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Sit upright with the affected elbow comfortably bent and tucked by your side. Gently turn the forearm outwards within a small comfortable pain-free range, then return. Keep the upper arm by your side; do not force rotation, raise the arm overhead or add a weight or band. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit upright with the upper arm by your side and one fixed clinician-selected dumbbell. Bend the elbow and lower under control within the individually advised range. Do not use an incline stretch position, increase weight or work to fatigue. The selected weight and tendon site require individual assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the affected elbow by your side and the forearm comfortably supported. With the hand empty and wrist relaxed, slowly turn the palm upwards and downwards within a small pain-free range. Do not force twisting, hold a weight, add a band or use rapid pulses. Follow any clinician-directed splint or movement restriction. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected foot flat on the floor and the knee bent. Slowly lift the heel within a comfortable pain-free range, then lower it to floor level with the forefoot resting on the floor. Do not add weight, stand on a step, drop below floor level or bounce. This is seated movement, not a strength test or a required isometric-first protocol. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected forearm supported on a table and the hand relaxed. Gently bend and straighten the wrist within a small comfortable pain-free range. Do not grip tightly, force a stretch or add a weight or band. This maintains comfortable movement without choosing a flexor or extensor strengthening protocol. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected lower leg supported and the foot free to move. Slowly move the ankle a small amount upwards and downwards around a comfortable middle range. Sit with the affected upper arm by your side and the forearm comfortably supported. With the hand empty, slowly bend and straighten the elbow through a small comfortable range. Sit with the leg supported and a resistance band around the forefoot. Slowly point and release the foot within a comfortable range against a fixed light band. No increase in band tension or speed within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the leg supported. Move the ankle slowly in a small comfortable circle against one fixed light resistance band; do not increase tension or speed. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the upper arm relaxed by your side and the hand empty. Slowly bend and straighten the affected elbow through a small comfortable range, stopping short of pain. Stand beside a stable support and lean slightly forwards with the uninjured hand supporting you. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. Keep the hand empty and do not grip, stretch with the other hand, press on the bruise or add resistance. Follow individual splint and movement restrictions. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. When comfortable movement is possible, lie on your back with both knees bent and feet supported close to your hips. Gently lift into a double-leg bridge and hold briefly at a comfortable height, then lower. Keep the work pain-free and self-paced. Do not walk the feet out, straighten the knees, add resistance or work to fatigue.

When pain no longer prevents comfortable movement, sit with your foot supported on a towel on a smooth floor. Gently slide the foot to bend and straighten the affected knee within a pain-free range. Keep the movement slow and self-paced. Do not force knee flexion, add resistance or increase speed. Stop if movement becomes painful or symptoms worsen.

When pain no longer stops comfortable movement, sit with the foot supported and gently bend and straighten the affected toe within a small pain-free range. Do not pull the toe into a stretch, push off through it, hop or add resistance. Follow any clinician-directed protection; a deformed toe or inability to move it needs assessment. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

When pain no longer stops movement, gently move your shoulder and arm through a comfortable range. Go at your own pace and stop before pain prevents movement. Avoid forced chest stretches, resisted chest flies and surgical-repair routines.

When standing and weight bearing are comfortable, practise balancing on the affected leg on firm ground, close to a stable counter for support. Start with a short comfortable attempt and build gradually. Keep support available; do not use a cushion or close your eyes.

When weight bearing and gentle calf movement are comfortable, use a stable support and practise controlled heel lowering as shown in the linked ankle rehabilitation guidance. Work at your own pace, up to 2 sets on alternate days. The source gives no repetition target; stop before symptoms worsen.

With the forearm comfortably supported without pressure on the bruise, gently open and close the affected hand through a small comfortable range. Keep the hand empty; do not squeeze a ball, clench tightly, push fingers with the other hand or massage the bruised tissue. Stop if movement worsens symptoms and follow individual movement restrictions. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

With the forearm supported and wrist comfortable, gently open the affected hand and bend the fingers into a loose fist, then straighten them within a pain-free range. Do not squeeze tightly, use a ball or band, force stiff joints or add impact. Follow any splint or tendon-protection instructions from your clinician. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With the upper arm comfortably by your side, gently bend and straighten the affected elbow within a pain-free range. Keep the shoulder relaxed and the hand empty. Do not stretch the arm behind the body, force forearm rotation, use an incline bench or add resistance. raw.name: Seated controlled ankle heel raises
raw.notes: Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Stay seated; no weights, band, pressure on the knees, step, forced range or automatic increase. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

proposed.evidence_notes: OUH NHS ankle-sprain guidance supports seated heel raises with feet flat and slow lowering. Bexley NHS ankle-sprain guidance provides 10 repetitions in a comfortable range. One set, maximum once daily, no added resistance and mild clinician-described uncomplicated lateral presentation are conservative product limits, not validated LOAD thresholds or injury grades. This seated strengthening option does not certify standing weight-bearing tolerance, ROM, strength, stability or sport readiness. Existing RESTORE includes standing tasks; LOAD here is a bounded permission stage, not a claim this movement imposes greater force than every RESTORE task. raw.name: Toe hyperextension protection guidance
raw.notes: Protect the affected toe from being bent backwards again. Pause provoking push-off, tiptoe work, running and jumping. Rest the foot in a comfortable supported position. Follow any individually prescribed footwear, walking support or weight-bearing restriction without changing it. The affected toe, joint stability and injury grade need assessment before toe curls, stretching or loaded forefoot work; this guidance does not diagnose turf toe. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

raw.name: Heel contusion protection guidance
raw.notes: Protect the bruised heel from repeated hard landings, running and direct pressure. Rest the foot comfortably supported and reduce provoking standing or walking. Follow any clinician-advised footwear, heel support or weight-bearing restriction. Do not tap or roll the bruised heel to desensitize it, start barefoot loading or assume that heel tenderness rules out a bone injury. The app does not distinguish heel-pad from deeper heel injury, so automatic exercises remain unavailable. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

raw.name: Achilles tendon load-management guidance
raw.notes: Reduce activities that aggravate the affected tendon and keep the area comfortably supported. Avoid heavy lifting, strong gripping or twisting that worsens symptoms; do not repeatedly test the painful tendon. Keep ordinary comfortable movement as symptoms allow rather than applying a universal prolonged-rest timetable. Follow any clinician-directed restrictions. Sudden severe pain, a snap or pop with loss of function, suspected rupture, a hot red swollen area, fever or altered sensation needs medical assessment. Reduce provocative running, hopping and forceful push-off; do not stretch into deep dorsiflexion or use heel drops below floor level when insertional status is unknown.

raw.name: Quads contusion protection guidance
raw.notes: Protect the bruised thigh from further blows, deep squatting, kicking and provoking knee loading. Rest the leg comfortably supported and follow any clinician-prescribed position, wrap, walking support or movement restriction. Do not massage, use a percussion gun, force a thigh stretch or deepen a wall sit. Do not set or remove a bent-knee brace yourself; the extent of the contusion and safe knee movement need individual assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

raw.name: Hand contusion protection guidance
raw.notes: Protect the bruised hand from heavy gripping, carrying, punching and direct pressure. Rest it comfortably supported and follow any individually prescribed hand protection. Do not use contrast heat, ball pressure or a resisted grip squeeze as automatic treatment. New loss of movement or grip, excessive or increasing swelling, or altered sensation needs assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

families.description: Acute muscle or musculotendinous strain: protect, restore pain-free movement, progressively load, then speed and sport demands.
Ligament sprain and symptomatic joint instability: protected movement, control and balance, progressive loading, then reactive and sport demands.
Tendon pain and tendinopathy: load management through isometric, then heavier slow, then energy-storage loading.
Painful joint irritation or impingement: settle symptoms, restore range and control, then load through tolerated range.
Joint hyperextension trauma: structural injury screened first, then protected range and end-range control before loading.
Direct-blow muscle or soft-tissue bruise: protect early, restore range, then progressive loading.
Symptom reports without a tissue diagnosis (pain, soreness, tightness, stiffness, swelling): symptom-led, conservative, no diagnosis implied.

functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report: can you walk at a normal stride without pain? (yes / no / not sure)

functional_checkpoints.description: Jogs at very low speed without pain.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report after an optional, explicitly offered low-speed jog: pain during / after (better / same / worse / not tried)

functional_checkpoints.description: A submaximal resisted isometric contraction of the injured tissue is pain-free.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report captured with a reviewed isometric exposure: was the hold pain-free? (yes / no / not sure)

functional_checkpoints.description: Reported Achilles heel-rise observation; no readiness cutoff.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Actual mode, quality, repetitions and assessor usability

functional_checkpoints.description: Reported loading and delayed symptoms; no pain cutoff.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Actual loading task/time, during and delayed numeric symptoms/time

functional_checkpoints.description: Reported permitted range and selected load; no readiness cutoff.

functional_checkpoints.description: Self-reported loading permission and confirmed midportion applicability of the reviewed floor option; no medical verification or readiness claim.

prescriptions.instructions: Protect the strained area and avoid movements that aggravate it. During the first 2 to 3 days, rest from exercise that loads it. Use comfortable everyday movement; do not force a stretch or add resisted chest work.
stop_when: Stop if pain prevents comfortable movement or symptoms worsen.
Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

prescriptions.instructions: When pain no longer stops movement, gently move your shoulder and arm through a comfortable range. Go at your own pace and stop before pain prevents movement. Avoid forced chest stretches, resisted chest flies and surgical-repair routines.

Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

prescriptions.instructions: Once the ankle is less painful, sit with the foot supported and gently move it up and down or trace the alphabet. Start with a small comfortable amount and build gradually. Keep within a comfortable range; do not force movement.
stop_when: Stop if pain prevents comfortable movement or symptoms worsen.
Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

stop_when: Stop if pain prevents comfortable movement or symptoms worsen.
Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

stop_when: Stop if pain prevents comfortable movement or symptoms worsen.
Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

Use only a comfortable range within clinician restrictions; stop for pain or worsening during or delayed symptoms.
Seek assessment for loss of function, inability to bear weight, bony tenderness, deformity, altered sensation, severe swelling or instability.

raw.cue: Move the hips first; knees and feet recover the frame after.
raw.name: Guard Retention Direction Call
raw.why: Coordinate hips and legs to follow changing passing direction.

raw.cue: Win the contact first, step to the angle, then snap.
raw.name: Hand-Fight to Snapdown Reaction
raw.why: Link a hand-fighting cue to a controlled snap and foot reposition.

raw.cue: Post strong, clear the hips, finish with a stable base.
raw.name: Hip-Heist to Base
raw.why: Coordinate opposite hand-foot support through a common scramble transition.

raw.cue: Every pass step ends with a base you could stop in.
raw.name: Pass-Recover-Base Flow
raw.why: Build smooth transitions between passing movement and a stable base.

raw.cue: Frame creates space; hips move through it; knees recover last.
raw.name: Shrimp-Recover-Frame
raw.why: Coordinate hip escape with frame recovery instead of treating them as separate actions.

raw.cue: Feel the grip pressure, clear or replace it, then settle position.
raw.name: Tactile Grip-Fighting Reaction
raw.why: Improve hand-fighting responses from contact rather than visual guessing.

raw.cue: Protect space with the post, bring the foot under, stand facing the cue.
raw.name: Technical Stand-Up on Cue
raw.why: Connect a directional cue to a safe, organised return to standing.

raw.cue: Check first; read the second cue before choosing hand or kick return.
raw.name: Kick-Check-Return Choice
raw.why: Train the athlete to choose the correct return after a checking cue.

raw.cue: Set the checking foot before the cross leaves.
raw.name: Check-Return-Cross
raw.why: Connect the check to a fast but organised return.

raw.cue: Let the cross load the switch without jumping the feet together.
raw.name: Cross-Lead Kick Switch
raw.why: Improve upper-to-lower sequencing when the strike changes sides.

raw.cue: Jab finds range; low kick turns through; feet reset before the next action.
raw.name: Jab-Low Kick Reset
raw.why: Link hand entry, lower-body rotation and stance recovery.

raw.cue: Kick, recover the leg, own the stance for one beat.
raw.name: Kick-and-Stick
raw.why: Teach every kick to finish in a stable stance rather than a loose landing.

raw.cue: Secure position, keep chest tall, then place the foot down under control.
raw.name: Kick-Catch Balance Reset
raw.why: Improve posture and hand-foot organisation after catching a light kick cue.

raw.cue: Drive the knee from posture and recover the foot under the hip.
raw.name: Knee-Step-Recover
raw.why: Coordinate the knee action with a stable return step.

raw.cue: Keep the frame organised while the kicking leg leaves and returns.
raw.name: Long Guard-Teep Reset
raw.why: Coordinate upper-body frame position with a long-range lower-body action.

raw.cue: Do not pivot until the kicking foot has recovered.
raw.name: Punch-Kick-Pivot Chain
raw.why: Coordinate a mixed striking chain that finishes in a new lane.

raw.cue: Recover square enough to punch, then leave on the angle.
raw.name: Rear Kick-Punch Exit
raw.why: Turn kick recovery into a usable punching and exit position.

raw.cue: The switch changes feet; it should not change posture.
raw.name: Switch-Kick Stance Recovery
raw.why: Make the switch step and kick return to an organised stance.

raw.cue: Bring the kicking leg home before the jab steps in.
raw.name: Teep-Recover-Jab
raw.why: Coordinate long-range kicking with immediate hand readiness.

raw.cue: Close the exit first, then react to the partner's final direction.
raw.name: Cage Cut-to-Entry Choice
raw.why: Coordinate cage positioning with the correct striking or grappling entry.

raw.cue: Jab hides the step; level change happens after range is won.
raw.name: Jab-to-Double-Leg Entry Pattern
raw.why: Link a simple striking entry to wrestling footwork.

raw.cue: Bring the kicking foot home before dropping levels.
raw.name: Kick-to-Level-Change Reset
raw.why: Train the athlete to recover from a kick into wrestling-ready posture.

raw.cue: Recover base before changing direction for the second entry.
raw.name: Shot-Reshot Direction Change
raw.why: Improve left-right reorganisation after the first entry is stopped.

raw.cue: Hips back, hands active, then rebuild stance before the next cue.
raw.name: Sprawl-to-Stance-Recover
raw.why: Coordinate defence to immediate fighting stance recovery.

raw.cue: Build base, stand with eyes up, recover guard immediately.
raw.name: Stand-Up-to-Guard Reset
raw.why: Make the ground-to-standing transition finish in a protected fighting stance.

raw.cue: Finish the strike in stance, then change level with the chest up.
raw.name: Strike-to-Level-Change
raw.why: Connect striking posture to a clean level change without a pause or collapse.

raw.cue: Do not pull with the arms; step the body to the underhook.
raw.name: Underhook Pummel to Angle Step
raw.why: Link upper-body position to the foot angle that makes it useful.

raw.cue: Win inside position, step the hips free, then turn.
raw.name: Wall Pummel to Exit
raw.why: Coordinate hand fighting and foot position to leave the wall with balance.

raw.cue: Catch, return, then leave. Do not move all three at once.
raw.name: Catch-Return-Step Out
raw.why: Build a clean defence-counter-exit chain.

raw.cue: Hook first, turn second, land facing the opponent.
raw.name: Check Hook Exit
raw.why: Coordinate the scoring hook with the exit rather than spinning away from stance.

raw.cue: Create the angle before accelerating away.
raw.name: Corner Exit Sequence
raw.why: Coordinate defence, turn and exit when space is restricted.

raw.cue: Take away the exit before throwing; do not chase the shoulders.
raw.name: Cut-Off Step to Combination
raw.why: Coordinate ring cutting with a short scoring sequence.

raw.cue: Second jab finishes before the exit step starts.
raw.name: Double Jab to Exit Angle
raw.why: Link forward scoring actions to a balanced angle exit.

raw.cue: Touch the entry as it starts; do not reach after it.
raw.name: Intercepting Jab on Cue
raw.why: Train the athlete to connect an opponent entry cue to a balanced intercept.

raw.cue: Foot and jab land together; head stays over the stance.
raw.name: Jab-Step Sync
raw.why: Synchronise the lead hand with the lead step so range is gained without reaching.

raw.cue: React only to the real cue; keep the response compact.
raw.name: Lead-Hand Feint Reaction
raw.why: Improve the link between seeing a lead-hand cue and choosing the correct small response.

raw.cue: Win the outside lane with small steps while keeping both hands available.
raw.name: Open-Stance Lead-Foot Battle
raw.why: Improve lead-foot positioning when athletes are in opposite stances.

raw.cue: Parry small, cross straight, pivot after the punch lands.
raw.name: Parry-Cross-Pivot
raw.why: Coordinate hand defence, counter timing and the exit angle as one sequence.

raw.cue: Turn on the ball of the lead foot and finish ready to fire.
raw.name: Pivot-Reset Shadowboxing
raw.why: Make the pivot end in a usable fighting stance instead of a loose spin.

raw.cue: Roll under the cue, settle, then return one clean shot.
raw.name: Pocket Roll-Return
raw.why: Improve close-range timing without turning the drill into a high-output exchange.

raw.cue: Step under control; slip from the legs, then hook from stance.
raw.name: Pressure Step-Slip-Hook
raw.why: Link forward pressure, head movement and a compact return.

raw.cue: Move the head just outside range; do not lean past the rear hip.
raw.name: Pull-Counter Reset
raw.why: Improve distance judgement and posture through a pull-counter sequence.

raw.cue: Finish the rear hand with both feet still able to move.
raw.name: Rear-Hand Weight Transfer Reset
raw.why: Coordinate rear-side force transfer without falling over the front leg.

raw.cue: Move under the line, rebuild posture, then punch.
raw.name: Rope-Line Head Movement to Counter
raw.why: Link head movement to stance recovery and a controlled counter.

raw.cue: Defend first, find stance, then return.
raw.name: Slip-Catch-Return
raw.why: Connect a defensive read to a clean return without rushing the counter.

raw.cue: Keep each beat distinct; speed comes after the sequence is clean.
raw.name: Three-Beat Combination Rhythm
raw.why: Develop clean sequencing across a short three-action combination.

raw.cue: React to the cue, not a guess. Keep the first step small.
raw.name: Call-and-Response Direction Change
raw.why: Link an external cue to clean movement without losing posture.

raw.cue: Keep the trunk quiet while opposite arm and leg move together.
raw.name: Cross-Body Pattern Reset
raw.why: Improve opposite-side coordination used in striking, hand fighting and level changes.

raw.cue: Track two or three coloured objects from slow to fast; stop when visual accuracy drops.
raw.name: Dynamic Visual Tracking Drills
raw.why: Train visual tracking and response quality without turning the work into conditioning.

raw.cue: Do not pre-load. Read the cue and take the shortest clean step.
raw.name: Lateral-or-Forward Choice
raw.why: Connect a simple choice cue to the correct first movement.

raw.cue: One decisive step, then rebuild stance.

raw.cue: Reset the angle, not the pace.
instructions: Picture getting caught while entering.
Do not rush back in. Exhale, rebuild your stance and restart your pressure from position.
Then picture the opponent escaping your trap.
Reset the angle instead of chasing.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse restarting pressure from position after being caught or escaped.

raw.cue: Read before you chase.
instructions: Picture the opponent retreating straight, covering high or planting to counter.
Recognise the reaction before choosing your response.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Finish each exchange balanced and reset your pressure.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise how the opponent reacts to pressure before committing to the next attack.

raw.cue: Take the space, do not chase it.
instructions: Visualise them giving ground.
See yourself taking space without following them blindly.
Cut their preferred exit, enter behind your trained setup and finish the exchange balanced.
Run it again with them changing direction and adjust instead of chasing.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse taking space and finishing exchanges in position rather than chasing.

raw.cue: Patience is still the plan.
instructions: Picture your counter being anticipated and answered.
Do not start hunting. Exhale, rebuild your guard and re-establish distance.
Then picture the opponent refusing to lead at all.
Give them one trained lead of your own to react to, and go back to reading.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse staying patient after a counter is read and beaten.

raw.cue: Only answer what is real.
instructions: Picture a feint, a half-step and a fully committed lead.
Answer only the committed one; let the other two pass.
Use the counter you have already drilled for that lead.
Reset your guard and read again before anything else.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Separate a real committed lead from a feint meant to draw your counter.

raw.cue: Wait for the commitment.
instructions: See the opponent step into range.
Read the first committed cue before reacting.
Make the attack miss or fall short, answer with your trained counter, then leave safely.
Run it again with a different entry and wait for the real cue.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse waiting for a real committed cue before answering.

raw.cue: Get your feet back, then your range.
instructions: Picture your back finding the ropes with the opponent in your chest.
Do not trade to escape. Exhale, frame, and pivot off the ropes.
Rebuild your range and restart your jab from the centre.
Then picture them timing your exit. Change the exit side and continue working.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering range after it has been taken from you.

raw.cue: See the step before the shot.
instructions: Picture the opponent beginning to close distance.
Notice the first committed step, rhythm change or reach.
Use your trained intercept or exit.
Rebuild your preferred range immediately and repeat with a different entry.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise the moment the opponent commits to closing distance.

raw.cue: Score, move, see again.
instructions: See the opponent starting to shorten the distance.
Score on the way in with your trained lead, then move off line before they set.
Rebuild your range immediately and see the picture clearly again.
Run it again with them entering from the other side.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse building and rebuilding your range against a fighter who wants to close it.

raw.cue: See it, trust it, go.
instructions: See the ring and feel your feet underneath you.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
raw.name: Trust → Compete
raw.pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.
raw.why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.

raw.cue: Same routine, same stance.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
Feel yourself getting sharper as the warm-up progresses.
See the opening bell and settle into your normal stance.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.
raw.name: Familiar & Ready
raw.why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.

raw.cue: Breathe, rebuild, continue.
instructions: Picture being caught clean in an exchange.
Exhale, cover, move your feet and rebuild your stance.
Then picture your best shot being blocked twice in a row.
Change the setup rather than the intensity and continue working.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering composure and position after a bad moment.

raw.cue: Recognise, then respond.
instructions: Picture three reactions you expect from this opponent.
See the reaction clearly before you decide what to throw.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Reset your stance after each exchange and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Rehearse recognising the opponent's action before choosing a response.

raw.cue: Same problem, trained answer.
instructions: Pick the exchange you expect to repeat most in this fight.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same situation with the opponent reacting differently.
Finish every repetition balanced and back on guard.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse the two or three situations this fight is most likely to be decided in.

raw.cue: See it, trust it, go.
instructions: See the competition area and feel your feet underneath you.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your trusted cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
raw.name: Trust → Compete
raw.pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, cue up, go.
raw.why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the bout to your trained reactions.

raw.cue: Same routine, same start.
instructions: Picture arriving, getting ready and warming up in your normal order.
Hear the room and your corner.
See the start of the bout and settle into your normal position.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.
raw.name: Familiar & Ready
raw.why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.

raw.cue: Problem, reset, next decision.
instructions: Picture the moment in this fight that would rattle you most.
Exhale, protect, and rebuild your position.
Reconnect to your next useful task and continue working.
Run it once more and finish it the same way.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse adversity that ends with a decision, not with dwelling.

raw.cue: Recognise, then respond.
instructions: Picture three familiar actions from this opponent.
See the action clearly before you decide what to do.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Reset your position after each exchange and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Rehearse recognising the opponent's action before choosing a response.

raw.cue: One situation, trained answer.
instructions: Pick the situation you expect to repeat most in this bout.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same situation again with the opponent reacting differently.
Finish each repetition balanced and ready to continue.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse the main situation of this fight before the taper takes your sharpness elsewhere.

raw.cue: Lose the grip, keep the position.
instructions: Picture your grip being stripped and being turned out of the clinch.
Do not reach after it. Recover your posture and re-establish striking range.
Then picture being kneed on the way in.
Reset your entry, change the level of your grip and work again.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse losing the clinch without losing the round.

raw.cue: Take the real opening only.
instructions: Picture them catching a kick, framing you off, or leaning in after a combination.
See which of those actually offers you the clinch.
Take your trained grip only on the real opening.
When the grip is denied, break cleanly and reset rather than wrestling for it.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise the moment the clinch is available and the moment it is gone.

raw.cue: Position first, then score.
instructions: See the entry that gets you inside: after their kick, or behind your own hands.
Take your trained grip and win the head or inside position first.
Score with knees or off-balancing before the referee breaks it.
Run it again with them framing and turning out early.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse earning the clinch on your terms and scoring before the break.

raw.cue: Late once, not twice.
instructions: Picture countering late and taking the shot instead.
Exhale, cover, check, and re-establish your distance.
Then picture an opponent who will not commit to anything.
Offer one trained lead to draw a reaction, then return to reading.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse staying composed when your reads stop paying.

raw.cue: Let the feint go.
instructions: Picture a hand feint, a low kick and a committed head kick.
Answer only the committed weapon; let the feints pass.
Use the check or catch you have drilled, then your trained return.
Reset and read again without leaning forward.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Tell a committed kick from a feint before you counter.

raw.cue: Read the weapon, then answer.
instructions: See the opponent load a kick or step in behind their hands.
Read which one it is before you move.
Check, catch or make it fall short, then answer with your trained return.
Reset your stance and run it again with the other weapon.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse reading a committed kick or entry and answering it cleanly.

raw.cue: Recover the leg, then the range.
instructions: Picture your kick being caught and your balance taken.
Recover your leg, post your stance and step out to a new angle.
Then picture them walking through your teep into punching range.
Frame, pivot off, and rebuild your range before you throw again.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering after your long weapons are caught or walked through.

raw.cue: Identify the entry first.
instructions: Picture the opponent stepping in, switching stance or loading a kick.
Identify which one it is before you commit.
Answer with your trained teep, check or lateral exit.
Rebuild your range and repeat with a different entry.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise the entry early enough to use your longest weapon.

raw.cue: Long weapon first, then move.
instructions: See the opponent closing to their punching range.
Meet the entry with your trained long weapon: teep, side kick or lead round kick.
Recover the leg, step off line and rebuild your range before they reset.
Run it again with them slipping under the kick and entering low.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse holding long range with kicks and leaving before the hands arrive.

raw.cue: See it, trust it, go.
instructions: See the ring and feel your feet and shins loose.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
raw.name: Trust → Compete
raw.pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.
raw.why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.

raw.cue: Same routine, same stance.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up, shins and pads on, and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
Feel yourself getting sharper as the warm-up progresses.
See the opening bell, settle into your normal stance and take the first look.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.
raw.name: Familiar & Ready
raw.why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.

raw.cue: Breathe, rebuild, continue.
instructions: Picture being caught clean or having a kick checked hard.
Exhale, cover, move your feet and rebuild your stance.
Then picture your main weapon being read twice.
Change the setup rather than the intensity and continue working.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering composure and stance after adversity.

raw.cue: Hands or legs, decide early.
instructions: Picture three familiar attacks from this opponent, at least one with the legs.
Recognise which weapon is coming before you move.
Answer with the block, check or exit already trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Rehearse recognising hand or leg attacks early enough to answer them.

raw.cue: Own the range you chose.
instructions: Pick the range this fight will mostly be fought at.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same exchange once with hands and once with legs.
Finish each repetition balanced with both feet under you.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse the main exchanges of this fight across both punching and kicking range.

raw.cue: Re-enter behind a setup.
instructions: Picture your entry meeting a hard check or a clean counter.
Do not rush the next entry. Exhale, reset your stance and re-enter behind a setup.
Then picture them circling out of your trap.
Cut the new exit instead of chasing the old one.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse restarting pressure after being checked or countered on the way in.

raw.cue: Their reaction chooses your shot.
instructions: Picture them retreating straight, checking your kicks or planting to fire back.
See the reaction before choosing your response.
Use only the entries and finishes trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again after each exchange.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise how the opponent answers pressure before you commit to the next attack.

raw.cue: Cut the exit, then commit.
instructions: See them giving ground and picking an exit side.
Cut that exit with your feet before you throw.
Enter behind your trained setup and finish with the kick or knee you have drilled.
Run it again with them circling the other way and adjust your cut.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse walking them onto your shots instead of following them around the ring.

raw.cue: Get your hips back first.
instructions: Picture being turned and pinned to the cage yourself.
Frame, get your hips free and switch to your trained escape grip.
Then picture your entry being sprawled on.
Recover your posture, return to your feet and re-enter behind a strike.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering when the clinch is reversed against you.

raw.cue: Their defence picks your grip.
instructions: Picture them framing on your hips, underhooking, or turning to face you.
See which defence appears before you choose your grip.
Use the trained answer to that defence and keep them on the cage.
If you lose the grip, reset your posture and re-enter.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise how the opponent defends the clinch so you pick the right grip.

raw.cue: Grip, pin, then work.
instructions: See your entry into the clinch behind a strike or on their exit.
Take your trained grip and pin them to the cage before you try to score.
Work your knees, elbows or trips from that position without giving up the grip.
Run it again with them turning out and re-clinch instead of chasing.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse closing to the clinch and making the cage do the work.

raw.cue: Get up, then read again.
instructions: Picture your counter drawing a level change and ending on the mat.
Protect, frame, build your base and return to your feet.
Then picture them refusing to lead while the clock runs.
Give one trained lead to create the read, then go back to waiting.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse composure when your counter is baited into a takedown.

raw.cue: Feint, punch or shot.
instructions: Picture a feint, a real punch entry and a real shot.
Let the feint go; answer the punch with your trained counter.
Meet the shot with hips and frames, not with a punch.
Reset your stance and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Answer only genuine commitment, in striking and in grappling.

raw.cue: Head high or head low.
instructions: See the opponent commit to an entry.
Read whether the head stays high or drops before you answer.
Counter the high entry with your trained return; meet the low entry with your frame and hips.
Reset your stance and run both versions again.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse answering a committed entry without being drawn onto a level change.

raw.cue: Feet first, range second.
instructions: Picture your back hitting the cage with the opponent tied up on you.
Frame, get your hips out and circle back to open space.
Then picture being taken down cleanly.
Protect first, build your frames, get back to your feet and rebuild your range.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse getting back to open space after being taken out of it.

raw.cue: Watch the level, not the hands.
instructions: Picture the opponent stepping in with hands high, then stepping in with a level change.
Read the head position before you choose.
Strike and angle off the high entry; frame and sprawl on the low one.
Rebuild your range and repeat with the two mixed.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Separate a striking entry from a takedown entry before you commit.

raw.cue: Strike, then get your angle back.
instructions: See the opponent closing distance with their hands or a level change.
Decide which it is before you commit your weight.
Score on the entry, then circle off the cage and rebuild your range.
Run it again with the entry becoming a real shot and defend without freezing.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse striking at range while staying honest about the takedown.

raw.cue: See it, trust it, go.
instructions: See the cage and feel your feet underneath you.
Feel the gloves and see the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read the opening range and trust your reactions.
raw.name: Trust → Compete
raw.pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.
raw.why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.

raw.cue: Same routine, same stance.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up, gloves on and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
See yourself walking to the cage and stepping through the door.
Settle into your normal stance and take the first look at the opening range.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.
raw.name: Familiar & Ready
raw.why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.

raw.cue: Protect, rebuild, continue.
instructions: Picture being caught clean or taken down.
Protect first, then build your frames and your base.
Recover position, reconnect to your next task and continue working.
Then run it again from a different bad position and finish the same way.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse recovering composure and position after a bad moment.

raw.cue: Read the intent, then move.
instructions: Picture three familiar actions from this opponent, at least one a level change.
Recognise which it is before you move.
Use only the response already trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Rehearse reading strike or grappling intent before responding.

raw.cue: Know where you want the fight.
instructions: Pick the phase you expect to spend most of the fight in: range, clinch or ground.
See your entry into that phase and the first thing you do once you arrive.
See how you get back out if it is not working.
Run it again with the opponent starting the phase instead of you.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse the phases this fight is most likely to be decided in.

raw.cue: Protect, rebuild, continue.
instructions: Picture your first takedown being defended.
Stay composed. Recover position, reconnect to your next control option and continue working.
Then picture losing a dominant position.
Protect first, rebuild position and return to your next task.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse continuing to work after a defended entry or a lost position.

raw.cue: Take the entry they give you.
instructions: Picture them square, bladed, and backing toward the cage.
See which of your trained entries each stance opens.
Enter on the one that is available rather than the one you prefer.
Reset to your stance and read the position again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise which takedown entry the opponent's stance is actually giving you.

raw.cue: Earn the entry, then hold it.
instructions: See the strike or feint that sets up your trained entry.
Change levels on your own timing, not theirs, and finish to your control position.
See the first pass or advance you want once you are on top.
Run it again from the cage instead of open space.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse getting to your entry and converting the first control position.

raw.cue: Survive, exit, restart.
instructions: Picture the fight dragged into the phase you least want.
Stay composed, survive the first thirty seconds and work your trained exit.
Return to the phase you chose and restart from there.
Then run it once more where you stay and solve it instead of leaving.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse being forced into your weaker phase and getting back out.

raw.cue: Name the phase, then act.
instructions: Picture them striking at range, then backing to the cage, then reaching for the clinch.
Name the phase each one offers before you act.
Take the phase you are better in, using a trained entry.
Reset to your stance and read the next one.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise which phase the opponent is offering and take it deliberately.

raw.cue: You choose the phase.
instructions: See the striking exchange you want to start with.
Pick the moment you convert it into your trained takedown or clinch entry.
If the entry stalls, see yourself returning to striking rather than forcing it.
Run it again starting from grappling and exiting into strikes.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse moving between striking and grappling on your own decision, not theirs.

raw.cue: Rebuild position, then pressure.
instructions: Picture them escaping the fence and turning you into it.
Do not panic-swing. Frame, circle out and re-establish your forward position.
Then picture being caught coming in.
Exhale, reset your stance and re-enter behind a setup rather than a rush.
raw.name: Pressure → Reset
raw.why: Rehearse restarting pressure after it is broken or reversed.

raw.cue: See the escape before it happens.
instructions: Picture them circling out, framing off, or shooting to escape the fence.
See which escape they choose before you commit your next attack.
Answer with the trained cut, the trained frame-break or the trained sprawl.
Re-establish the fence and read again.
raw.name: Read → React
raw.why: Recognise how the opponent escapes your pressure at the cage.

raw.cue: Fence first, then work.
instructions: See them backing up and choosing an exit along the fence.
Cut that exit with your feet and put their back to the cage.
Enter behind your trained setup and finish the exchange or take the body lock.
Run it again with them circling out and adjust your angle instead of chasing.
raw.name: Tactical Picture
raw.why: Rehearse using the cage to take space rather than chasing in open ground.

raw.name: Achilles tendon load-management guidance
raw.notes: Reduce activities that aggravate the affected tendon and keep the area comfortably supported. Avoid heavy lifting, strong gripping or twisting that worsens symptoms; do not repeatedly test the painful tendon. Keep ordinary comfortable movement as symptoms allow rather than applying a universal prolonged-rest timetable. Follow any clinician-directed restrictions. Sudden severe pain, a snap or pop with loss of function, suspected rupture, a hot red swollen area, fever or altered sensation needs medical assessment. Reduce provocative running, hopping and forceful push-off; do not stretch into deep dorsiflexion or use heel drops below floor level when insertional status is unknown.

raw.name: Seated Achilles heel movement
raw.notes: Sit with the affected foot flat on the floor and the knee bent. Slowly lift the heel within a comfortable pain-free range, then lower it to floor level with the forefoot resting on the floor. Do not add weight, stand on a step, drop below floor level or bounce. This is seated movement, not a strength test or a required isometric-first protocol. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.
