raw.modality: standing clinch recovery after a level-change threat
raw.name: Level-Change Stuff-and-Recover Burst
raw.notes: From standing connection, recognise the partner’s controlled level-change or takedown-entry cue, stuff the entry, regain useful head and inside position, stabilise the clinch, then reset. Success means standing clinch control is recovered; do not sprawl for conditioning or finish a takedown.

raw.equipment_note: Partner gives light positional resistance. Use controlled contact and no neck cranks.
raw.name: MMA Clinch Position Flow
raw.notes: Connect at low intensity against light live resistance. Pummel for useful underhook or overhook position, establish head position and posture, then stabilise. As the partner changes position, recover useful standing connection without completing a takedown.

raw.name: Parry-Return Intervals
raw.notes: Holder feeds repeated straight-punch cues at a controlled pace. Parry, return a straight immediately, then regain guard and range before the next feed. Accuracy and clean defence come before volume.

raw.equipment_note: Use a wall as the practical cage substitute; partner controls pressure and pad contact.
raw.name: Cage Defend-Counter-Escape
raw.notes: Partner applies controlled pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete reads the pressure, frames, uses an underhook or angle where appropriate, creates safe separation, lands one short counter to the pads, then exits into open space and restores stance. Avoid static clinch grinding; reduce pressure when posture or escape footwork fails.

raw.equipment_note: Partner gives a safe low-kick feed and presents Thai pads for the immediate pocket answer.
raw.name: Check-Return Pocket Burst
raw.notes: Partner feeds a controlled low kick during a close exchange. Check, return aggressively inside the pocket with a compact punch-kick answer, recoil the kick, and restore stance and guard.

raw.name: Clinch Fighter's Neck Endurance
raw.notes: Maintain plum position against light resistance.

raw.name: Flicker’s Endurance
raw.notes: 1-2s only, reset stance after each combo. (Fast twitch focus)

raw.name: Cage-Space Kick Flow
raw.notes: Use an open-space lane with one edge marked as the limited-space boundary. The partner changes distance and position. Kick only when posture and space allow, then recoil; reposition instead when a kick would weaken stance. Reduce output if stance recovery or decisions fade.

raw.name: Teep Intercept Burst
raw.notes: The holder advances unpredictably. Intercept only when the entry is genuinely there, recover stance, and take a short angle. Stop if recoil or balance slows.

raw.equipment_note: Partner gives sustainable live resistance and holds a Thai pad for controlled strikes. No live knees or elbows to the head.
raw.name: Reactive MMA Clinch Rounds
raw.notes: The partner unpredictably pummels, frames, changes level, turns, separates, pressures towards the cage, circles away or shows a short-strike opening. Choose to pummel, frame, gain an underhook and head position, stuff the level change, turn, separate, make one controlled pad strike or reconnect. Keep decisions sustainable and recover standing control; responses are not pre-called.

raw.equipment_note: Use a wall as the practical cage substitute and pads for all hard counter targets.
raw.name: MMA Counter Decision Rounds
raw.notes: Partner unpredictably provides controlled strikes, kicks, level changes, takedown entries or pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete cannot freely initiate: read, defend or intercept, counter briefly to the pads, recover stance or open space, then wait for the next problem. Lower cue density when choices, mechanics or defensive recovery deteriorate.

raw.name: Rear-Kick Reposition Burst
raw.notes: Score with the rear kick, recoil into stance, then reposition outside the return line. Reset fully if the bag swing pulls posture forward.

raw.name: Scrambler's Hip Escape Marathon
raw.notes: Continuous hip escapes down mat length.

raw.name: Guillotine Shot Reactions
raw.notes: Partner signals shot direction; shooter reacts with guillotine grip.

raw.name: Turtle to Guard Scramble
raw.notes: Partner starts in top turtle – you must recover guard or stand. (Explosive hips)

raw.name: Pressure Fighter's Cutoff Circuit
raw.notes: Mirror imaginary opponent while cutting off space.

raw.name: Range-Recovery Intervals
raw.notes: Check or long-guard the imagined attack, reset the feet, and restore kicking range without repeated straight-line retreat. Reduce output if stance widens.

raw.name: Teep Volume & Position
raw.notes: Repeat measured teeps while holding preferred range and changing angle after each score. Reduce output if stance recovery or target selection breaks down.

raw.equipment_note: Use gi lapel for no-gi grip variations
raw.name: Stranglehold
raw.notes: Partner resists first 5 sec, then taps. (90% squeeze)

raw.name: Punch-Clinch Reentry
raw.notes: Score a short punch entry, connect to a safe clinch and settle balanced pressure. Regain stance before re-entering; stop if head position or clinch posture fails.

raw.description: Enter only on the range cue, score once, then immediately restore preferred distance.
raw.name: Range Gate-Score-Exit

raw.description: A cue triggers one intercepting step and straight on the way in, then immediate recovery to range.
raw.name: Intercept-Step-Straight

raw.description: One snapdown into a go-behind touch on the back position, then release and reset to neutral.
raw.name: Snapdown-Go-Behind Touch

raw.description: One solo hip heist to a squared base, then stop - no partner and no scramble volume.
raw.name: Hip-Heist-Base Snap

raw.description: Single teep to manage range, fast recoil of the kicking leg, then re-square to stance.
raw.name: Teep-Recoil-Re-square

raw.description: Snap to front-headlock control, establish the position for one beat, then release without squeezing.
raw.name: Front-Headlock-Capture-Release

raw.description: Snap solo through one back-exposure path to a controlled finish shape, then reset to base.
raw.name: Solo Back-Exposure Snap

raw.description: Check one cooperative kick cue and answer with a single return kick, then re-square.
raw.name: Check-Return-Kick

raw.description: Shadow the clinch frame, turn the corner and exit, with no partner load and no sustained tie.
raw.name: Solo Frame-Turn Exit Cue

raw.description: Draw one attack, take a small pull off the end of it, return once, then restore stance.
raw.name: Pull-Counter-Reset

raw.description: One crisp sit-out from a bottom touch, then re-square to a balanced base and stop.
raw.name: Sit-Out-Re-square

raw.description: From turtle, execute one technical stand to a squared base, then reset down - single repetition per burst.
raw.name: Turtle-Technical-Stand

raw.description: One short hand entry into a single kick, then recoil and re-square with no follow-up volume.
raw.name: Hand-Entry-Single-Kick Reset

raw.description: Partner shows one of two openings; take the matching control position, confirm it, then release.
raw.name: Position-Read Control Touch

raw.description: One solo level change into a short penetration step, then stand and stop - no partner, no finish.
raw.name: Level-Change-Penetration Snap

raw.description: From a relaxed standing stance, respond to a visual or self cue with one small stance adjustment and freeze in balance. No strikes, jumps, level changes or contact; fully relax between cues.
raw.name: Standing Stance-Set Cue

raw.description: Rehearse posture, frame placement and exit footwork against an imagined clinch without partner contact.
raw.name: Clinch Frame-Exit Shadow

raw.description: Use brief cadence touches and easy pedalling to retain machine rhythm without creating an aerobic workload.
raw.name: Assault Bike Rhythm Primer

raw.description: One snapping lead kick with an immediate controlled recovery to a balanced stance.
raw.name: Lead-Kick Snap-Recover

raw.description: Coach gives a visual cue; rehearse the response without impact, then settle.
raw.name: Visual Counter Shadow

raw.description: Move through the athlete's preferred base, hip-line and re-square positions solo with no partner resistance.
raw.name: Grappling Base-Position Shadow

raw.description: Shadow one arm-drag path with the feet only, then reset to base - no partner and no grip load.
raw.name: Solo Arm-Drag Footwork Cue

raw.description: Respond to a visual cue with one unloaded kick motion, then return to a quiet stance.
raw.name: Kick Timing Shadow Cue

raw.description: Partner shows one hand cue; answer with a single low kick, recover the leg, then stop.
raw.name: Punch-Cue-Low-Kick Counter

raw.description: Smooth ring or cage cutting against visualised exits with no sustained flurry.
raw.name: Pressure Lane Shadow

raw.description: Read a light cue, cover or parry, return briefly, then exit cleanly.
raw.name: Cover-Return-Exit

raw.description: Absorb one cooperative pressure touch, frame, return two crisp pocket shots, then reset stance.
raw.name: Pocket Frame-Burst Touch

raw.description: Brief long-range hand-speed action from a pendulum step, then settle back to guard.
raw.name: Pendulum Jab-Cross Reset

raw.description: Shadow one cut-off step and set the stance, then hold still - zero contact, zero impact.
raw.name: Cutoff Step-Set Cue

raw.description: Snap solo into one submission-entry shape, hold it for a beat, then release - no partner, no squeeze.
raw.name: Solo Entry-Position Snap

raw.description: Slip one telegraphed cue, answer with a single straight, then pivot out to a new angle.
raw.name: Slip-Cross-Pivot

raw.description: Rehearse light striking cadence and stance organisation without a sustained flurry or conditioning demand.
raw.name: Shadowboxing Technical Rhythm

raw.description: Shadow one kick and its recoil to stance, with no pad, no partner and no impact.
raw.name: Shadow Kick-Recoil Cue

raw.description: One crisp guard-pass entry to a control touch, then release the position and reset.
raw.name: Pass-Entry-Control Touch

raw.description: Take the guillotine position from a front-headlock touch, confirm the grip, then release with no squeeze.
raw.name: Guillotine Position-Catch-Release

raw.description: Partner shows one of two openings; take the matching submission entry to the catch, then release.
raw.name: Entry-Read Catch-Release

raw.description: Explosive first pressure step behind a jab, seal the angle, then settle - no follow-up flurry.
raw.name: Step-Jab-Cutoff Cue

raw.description: One partner cue, one parry, one straight return, then immediate exit and guard reset.
raw.name: Parry-Cross-Exit

raw.description: Enter the clinch, place one light knee touch, then break the tie - early taper only, never a knee volume set.
raw.name: Clinch Knee-Touch Entry

raw.description: Shadow two compact pocket shots, freeze the guard, then settle - zero contact, zero impact.
raw.name: Shadow Pocket Burst-Freeze

raw.description: One feint at range, one rapid entry, one shot, then clean exit - no second entry.
raw.name: Range Feint-Entry-Exit

raw.description: Rehearse one quiet scramble-to-base pathway on the mat, settle posture, then reset without speed chasing or resistance.
raw.name: Scramble Base Reset Shadow

raw.description: Enter to a body lock, confirm the position for one beat, then release - no lift and no finish.
raw.name: Body-Lock Entry-Position Touch

raw.description: One light tie touch to set the level, then a single explosive entry and immediate stance recovery.
raw.name: Touch-and-Go Entry

raw.description: Perform one controlled hip-heist recovery and immediately establish a stable square position.
raw.name: Hip-Heist-Re-square

raw.description: Acquire the armbar entry configuration quickly, stop at the catch, then release - no loaded joint finish.
raw.name: Armbar Entry-Catch-Release

raw.description: Sprawl on one cooperative entry cue, recover posture, then answer with a single re-shot touch.
raw.name: Sprawl-Re-shot Touch

raw.description: Snap solo into one submission-entry shape at speed, hold one beat, then release and reset.
raw.name: Solo Submission Entry Snap

raw.description: Pure hand-speed burst: rapid straight punches in the air at maximal crispness, then full recovery.
raw.name: Explosive Straight Burst

raw.description: Rehearse the preferred submission-entry pathway solo on the mat, stopping before any squeeze or loaded finish.
raw.name: Submission Entry Map Shadow

raw.description: Two to three crisp close-range strikes followed immediately by guard and stance restoration.
raw.name: Pocket Burst-Reset

raw.description: Show one convincing fake, read the reaction, then commit to a single entry and recover stance.
raw.name: Fake-Shot-Go

raw.description: One compact body shot into one head shot, then a single clean exit step and guard reset.
raw.name: Body-Head Burst-Exit

raw.description: Co-operative pummel to frame and clean exit with no sustained clinch battle.
raw.name: Pummel-Frame-Exit Flow

raw.description: Partner circles; reposition, show the re-shot entry, then reset without finishing hard.
raw.name: Circle-Re-shot Cue

raw.description: Pure acceleration cue: one maximal-intent first step from fighting stance, then stop and reset.
raw.name: Explosive First-Step Cue

raw.description: Explosive shuffle to close range, one clean score, then an angled exit back to long range.
raw.name: Shuffle-In-Score-Angle-Out

raw.description: Rehearse two or three compact pocket actions in shadow, restore guard, then settle with no impact or sustained flurry.
raw.name: Pocket Rhythm Shadow

raw.description: Close the escape lane with one step and answer with a single low kick, then re-square and stop.
raw.name: Cutoff-Low-Kick Touch

raw.description: Partner gives an escape cue; seal the lane and answer with a two-shot burst, then reset to neutral range.
raw.name: Herd-Corner-Burst-Reset

raw.description: Partner shows one escape lane; cut it off with a single explosive step, land one crisp score, stop.
raw.name: Cut-Off-Step-Score

raw.description: Shadow one shuffle and one angle change, then set the stance - zero contact, zero impact.
raw.name: Shuffle-Angle-Set Cue

raw.description: One arm drag to back exposure, catch the position, then release immediately - no finishing squeeze.
raw.name: Arm-Drag-Back-Catch-Release

raw.description: Deliver one crisp kick to a light pad and restore stance immediately without combination volume.
raw.name: Single-Kick Recoil Primer

raw.description: Shadow one clinch frame and corner turn, then set posture - no partner, no tie, no load.
raw.name: Shadow Frame-Turn-Set

raw.description: Quiet stance and range rhythm with occasional single intercepts and no bouncing contest.
raw.name: Long-Range Rhythm Shadow

raw.description: Rehearse re-position, level-change and re-shot rhythm solo, then recover stance without a finish.
raw.name: Re-shot Rhythm Shadow

raw.description: Short rotational hook-cross pair followed immediately by a pivot off the line and guard restoration.
raw.name: Hook-Cross-Pivot Burst

raw.description: Enter a preferred grappling position against light resistance, establish briefly, then disengage before fatigue.
raw.name: Position Touch-Reset

raw.description: One penetration step to depth, then stand back to a squared stance - single rep, no finish.
raw.name: Penetration-Step-Recover

raw.description: Snap to an inside tie from neutral posture, hold the position for a beat, then release cleanly.
raw.name: Inside-Tie Snap-Reset

raw.description: Perform one clean level change and initial penetration action without a hard finish, then recover stance.
raw.name: Level-Change-Entry-Recover

raw.description: Shadow one slip and one return, then restore guard and stop - zero contact, zero impact.
raw.name: Slip-Return Shadow Cue

raw.description: Two crisp pummels to a dominant underhook, then release the tie and reset to neutral posture.
raw.name: Pummel-Underhook-Reset

raw.description: Enter the preferred submission configuration, establish mechanics briefly, release before maximal squeeze, then reset.
raw.name: Position-Attack Entry-Release

instructions: Find one sign that your pressure has become rushed.
Choose the safe action that pauses the chase without giving up position.
Choose the setup that starts your next entry.
Write one pressure rule that keeps your feet organised.

mindset.anchor: Pressure is position, not speed.
mindset.context: Early-camp pressure discipline for a brawler.
mindset.focus: Spot the moment your feet begin following instead of cutting.
mindset.intent: Stay dangerous without becoming hurried.
mindset.reset: Pause the chase, square the stance and rebuild the entry.

raw.name: Pressure Reset
raw.progress: Use the reset whenever you notice yourself following during technical work.
raw.why: Keep pressure controlled so forward intent does not turn into reckless chasing.

instructions: Identify the opponent's preferred retreat direction.
Choose the direction you should step to cut that route.
Identify the cue that tells you pressure should start.
Choose the area of the ring you want to trap them in.

mindset.anchor: Cut the ring, do not chase it.
mindset.context: Early-camp pressure route study for a brawler.
mindset.focus: Watch the first direction they choose when space disappears.
mindset.intent: Guide the opponent toward the space you want.
mindset.reset: If you start following, pause and rebuild the angle.

raw.name: Pressure Route Scan
raw.progress: Use one technical round to steer toward the chosen trap instead of following.
raw.why: Learn where opponents naturally retreat so pressure can steer instead of chase.

instructions: Choose the setup that hides your forward step.
Choose the guard position you need while crossing range.
Choose the first punch that establishes the pocket.
Define where your head should finish after the entry.

mindset.anchor: Earn the pocket.
mindset.context: Early-camp entry quality for a brawler.
mindset.focus: Watch what the opponent throws as someone closes distance.
mindset.intent: Arrive protected before trying to win the exchange.
mindset.reset: If the entry is naked, leave and rebuild the setup.

raw.name: Safe Entry Builder
raw.progress: Rehearse the same setup and head position before adding longer combinations.
raw.why: Build a repeatable way into the pocket without walking onto clean shots.

instructions: Identify the clearest body opening the opponent gives away.
Choose the punch or feint that creates that opening.
Choose the body target you will attack.
Choose the head follow-up that punishes their reaction.

mindset.anchor: Open it before you take it.
mindset.context: SPP body-attack selection for a brawler.
mindset.focus: Watch for high guards, separated elbows and upright posture.
mindset.intent: Attack the body when the position earns it.
mindset.reset: If the body line closes, go back upstairs rather than forcing it.

raw.name: Body Attack Opportunity
raw.progress: Use the body attack only after the chosen setup appears in technical work.
raw.why: Find safe body attacks that reward pressure without making the entry predictable.

instructions: Identify the opponent's most common pocket sequence.
Choose your answer to that sequence.
Choose the finishing shot that best fits the opening.
Decide whether that exchange should end with an exit or a smother.

mindset.anchor: Know the next beat.
mindset.context: SPP pocket planning for a brawler.
mindset.focus: Watch the opponent's response after the first two punches.
mindset.intent: Win the second decision inside the pocket.
mindset.reset: If the exchange loses shape, smother or leave instead of trading blindly.

raw.name: Pocket Exchange Map
raw.progress: Rehearse the chosen exchange ending, not just the opening combination.
raw.why: Know what happens after the first punches so pocket exchanges stay planned rather than chaotic.

instructions: Choose where your body should finish after the combination.
Choose your response if the opponent fires back immediately.
Define the smother or control position you can reach safely.
Choose the action that resets you for the next pressure sequence.

mindset.anchor: Finish safe before restarting.
mindset.context: SPP post-combination control for a brawler.

instructions: Identify the first thing you normally do after an exchange ends.
Find the part of your stance, guard or vision that is slowest to recover.
Choose the order you want your reset to happen in.
Write one short reset routine.

mindset.anchor: Reset before restart.
mindset.context: General early-camp reset quality.
mindset.focus: Watch feet, guard and eyes during the reset.
mindset.intent: Finish each exchange ready for the next one.
mindset.reset: If one piece is missing, rebuild it before re-engaging.

raw.name: Reset Habit Review
raw.progress: Use the reset routine after every exchange in the next technical session.
raw.why: Make the reset between exchanges deliberate instead of letting the next exchange start from disorder.

instructions: Mark one period where the pace is slow and controlled.
Mark one period where the pace suddenly rises.
Identify what usually causes the change in tempo.
Choose one rhythm you want to impose in training.

mindset.anchor: Tempo tells you what is next.
mindset.context: General early-camp rhythm study.
mindset.focus: Notice what happens just before the pace changes.
mindset.intent: See the tempo changes that organise the fight.
mindset.reset: If the rhythm becomes unclear, watch one full minute without making notes.

raw.name: Rhythm Map
raw.progress: Use one technical round to deliberately create the chosen rhythm.
raw.why: Recognise when exchanges speed up, slow down or become predictable before adding tactics.

instructions: Identify the direction you circle in most often.
Identify the direction you almost never use.
Find the moment your stance stops being usable while you move.
Write one movement rule that forces you to use the neglected direction.

mindset.anchor: Pick the angle before it picks you.
mindset.context: Early-camp movement-habit study from your own footage.
mindset.focus: Track which way your feet take you after every exchange.
mindset.intent: Move on purpose rather than out of habit.
mindset.reset: If you drift, square up and re-choose the direction before moving again.

raw.name: Stance and Angle Audit
raw.progress: Apply the movement rule in shadow and footwork work; keep it only if your stance stays usable.
raw.why: Expose the movement direction you default to and the side of the ring or cage you keep giving away.

instructions: List the three threats that affect exchanges most often.
Rank them from highest to lowest priority.
Choose the first answer you will train for the top threat.

mindset.anchor: One priority first.
mindset.context: General early-camp threat ranking.
mindset.focus: Rank threats by how often and how badly they change exchanges.
mindset.intent: Solve the highest-value problem first.
mindset.reset: If everything looks dangerous, return to frequency and consequence.

raw.name: Threat Priority
raw.progress: Build the next tactical rehearsal around the top-ranked threat only.
raw.why: Separate the biggest tactical problem from smaller threats so training attention stays clear.

instructions: Name the part of your first plan most likely to fail.
Choose the part that should stay unchanged.
Choose one tactical change that addresses the failure.
Define the sign that tells you the adjustment is working.

mindset.anchor: Adjust, do not panic-rewrite.
mindset.context: General SPP plan-B preparation.
mindset.focus: Identify exactly what is failing before choosing the adjustment.
mindset.intent: Change one variable instead of abandoning the whole plan.
mindset.reset: Keep the parts of the plan that are still working.

raw.name: Adjustment Tree
raw.progress: Run one technical round where the first option is deliberately removed and use the adjustment.
raw.why: Prepare one clear adjustment when the first tactical plan stops working.

instructions: Choose the immediate defensive action you use first after trouble.
Choose one short reset phrase.
Choose the next safe action that restarts your offence or position.
Choose the route that brings you back to control.

mindset.anchor: First get safe, then regain control.
mindset.context: General SPP adversity planning.
mindset.focus: Watch what successful fighters do in the first few seconds after trouble.
mindset.intent: Make the first action after adversity predictable and safe.
mindset.reset: Use the same short reset instead of solving everything at once.

raw.name: Adversity Reset
raw.progress: Start one technical drill from a disadvantaged position and use the same reset sequence.
raw.why: Prepare a simple route back to control after being hit, trapped, tired or frustrated.

instructions: Write the full tactical instruction you want to remember.
Identify the thing you must notice before acting.
Choose the single action that follows that read.
Compress the instruction to three words.

mindset.anchor: One instruction, one action.
mindset.context: General SPP corner-message rehearsal.
mindset.focus: Separate what you need to notice from what you need to do.
mindset.intent: Make the instruction observable and executable.
mindset.reset: If the instruction feels crowded, reduce it to the first action only.

raw.name: Corner Instruction Translation
raw.progress: Use only the three-word version during the next hard technical round.
raw.why: Turn a complicated tactical instruction into one action you can execute under fatigue.

instructions: Identify the safest scoring action late in the round.
Choose the position you want before the final exchange.
Choose the mistake you must avoid when urgency rises.
Write one final-minute instruction.

mindset.anchor: Close clearly.
mindset.context: General SPP final-minute management.
mindset.focus: Watch what changes in the final minute when both fighters know time is short.
mindset.intent: Finish the round with clear control rather than random volume.
mindset.reset: If the finish becomes reckless, return to the safest scoring action.

raw.name: Last-Minute Control
raw.progress: Finish one technical round using the same final-minute instruction.
raw.why: Plan how to close a round clearly when fatigue and urgency make decision-making noisier.

instructions: Find the moment the round clearly changed direction.
Identify what caused the change.
Identify what the fighter gaining control noticed or exploited.
Choose the response you would use to stop the same shift.

mindset.anchor: Catch the shift early.
mindset.context: General SPP momentum management.
mindset.focus: Find the exchange or positional change that altered the round.
mindset.intent: Notice momentum early enough to act on it.
mindset.reset: Return to the last action that gave you control.

raw.name: Momentum Shift Review
raw.progress: Rehearse the chosen response immediately after a deliberately difficult exchange.
raw.why: Recognise the moment control changes so you can respond before a bad spell becomes a lost round.

instructions: Choose the first tactical question you need answered.
Choose the safe action that tests that question.
Define the response that confirms your read.
Choose what you will do next if the read is confirmed.

mindset.anchor: Test, read, then decide.
mindset.context: General SPP opening-information plan.
mindset.focus: Choose what you need to learn first about the opponent.
mindset.intent: Make the opening exchange answer one question.
mindset.reset: After the test, return to your base position before changing anything.

raw.name: Opening Exchange Test
raw.progress: Start a technical round with the same test and act only on the observed response.
raw.why: Use the first exchanges to gather specific information instead of trying to prove the whole game plan immediately.

instructions: Describe the opponent's behaviour in the first minute.
Describe what changes in the middle of the round.
Describe what changes in the final minute.
Choose the part of the round where you should take the most control.

mindset.anchor: The round has phases too.
mindset.context: General SPP round-management study.
mindset.focus: Compare the first, middle and final minute.
mindset.intent: Match your tactical decisions to the part of the round you are in.
mindset.reset: If the pattern changes, update the map rather than forcing the first read.

raw.name: Round Flow Map
raw.progress: Plan one technical round around the chosen control window.
raw.why: Understand how the opponent's behaviour changes through the round instead of treating every minute the same.

instructions: Choose the position you most want to avoid staying in.
Choose the position where you perform best.
Identify the movement or action that links the two.
Choose one cue that starts that transition.

mindset.anchor: Move toward control.
mindset.context: General SPP positional transition planning.
mindset.focus: Watch the movement that changes a bad position into a useful one.
mindset.intent: Know the route back to your best fighting position.
mindset.reset: If the first route is blocked, protect position before trying again.

raw.name: Route to Control
raw.progress: Begin one technical drill in the difficult position and earn the route back to control.
raw.why: Link one difficult position to the position where your decisions and scoring are strongest.

instructions: Choose the cleanest scoring action you can repeat.
Choose the position you want to control while scoring.
Choose one combination worth repeating.
Identify one busy but low-value action to reduce.

mindset.anchor: Repeat what scores cleanly.
mindset.context: General SPP scoring efficiency.
mindset.focus: Watch which actions land cleanly without costing position.
mindset.intent: Build around actions that score clearly and leave you organised.
mindset.reset: If an action creates noise but no clean score, move on from it.

raw.name: Scoring Map
raw.progress: Track how often the selected scoring action lands cleanly in technical work.
raw.why: Separate clean, repeatable scoring actions from busy work that looks active but gives little return.

instructions: Choose one reliable visual or positional trigger.
Choose the action you will take when it appears.
Choose how you leave after the action.
Choose what you use to reset before the next exchange.

mindset.anchor: See it, do it.
mindset.context: General SPP trigger-response work.
mindset.focus: Choose a trigger you can genuinely see in real time.
mindset.intent: Make one read immediately actionable.
mindset.reset: If the trigger is absent, stay neutral rather than forcing the response.

raw.name: Trigger-Response Builder
raw.progress: Rehearse the full trigger-response-exit-reset chain in technical work.
raw.why: Turn one reliable opponent signal into a trained action instead of a vague tactical idea.

instructions: Choose the first familiar action you will show.
Choose the response you already trust if the opponent disrupts it.
Choose the position you want after the opening exchange.
Say the sequence once in plain language.

mindset.anchor: Familiar first.
mindset.context: General fight-week opening rehearsal.
mindset.focus: Use only confirmed actions and responses.
mindset.intent: Start with what has already worked in camp.
mindset.reset: If the opening changes, return to the safest familiar action.

raw.name: Familiar Round-One Rehearsal
raw.progress: Rehearse the sequence once at low intensity, then stop analysing it.
raw.why: Confirm a familiar opening sequence without adding new decisions during taper.

instructions: Name the one danger you have prepared for most in this camp.
Name the trained answer that goes with it.
Confirm the position you want to be in immediately after using it.
Rehearse the answer slowly until it needs no thought.

mindset.anchor: Known danger, known answer.
mindset.context: Fight-week rehearsal of an already-prepared threat.
mindset.focus: Watch only footage of the threat you have already prepared for.
mindset.intent: Meet the known danger with a known answer.
mindset.reset: If the answer feels unclear, use the simpler version you have trained more.

raw.name: Familiar Threat Rehearsal
raw.progress: Rehearse it once more at low intensity before fight day and leave the rest alone.
raw.why: Rehearse the answer you have already trained for the danger you already know about, without adding new theory.

instructions: Choose one familiar entry cue.
Choose one familiar scoring cue.
Choose one danger cue and one reset phrase.
Condense them into one final sentence you can recall under pressure.

mindset.anchor: Simple survives pressure.
mindset.context: Final fight-week tactical compression.
mindset.focus: Use cues already rehearsed successfully.
mindset.intent: Carry only the most useful information into fight day.
mindset.reset: If thoughts multiply, return to the single final sentence.

raw.name: Final Tactical Cue Card
raw.progress: Read the final sentence before the last light rehearsal; add nothing new.
raw.why: Reduce the trained game plan to a few familiar cues that remain usable under pressure.

instructions: List the two responses you have repeated most often this camp.
Confirm the situation each one belongs to.
Remove any response you have not trained enough to trust.
Say both responses out loud in the situation they belong to.

mindset.anchor: Trained beats clever.
mindset.context: Fight-week confirmation of already-trained responses.
mindset.focus: Look only at work you have repeated successfully in camp.
mindset.intent: Go in with the answers you already own.
mindset.reset: If you start weighing options, go back to the response with the most repetitions.

raw.name: Trained Response Confirmation
raw.progress: Confirm both in light shadow work only; add no new response this week.
raw.why: Confirm the two responses you have the most repetitions in and drop everything you have not trained.

instructions: Pause examples at the instant contact releases and mark both stances.
Identify the opponent's fastest legal return from that separation position.
Choose the guard and step that remove the return before re-entry.

mindset.anchor: The break creates a new first exchange.
mindset.context: Finish at protected punching range with an exit lane visible.
mindset.focus: Opponent lead shoulder and kicking-side hip as separation begins.
mindset.intent: Recover guard and angle before restarting offence.
mindset.reset: If the break leaves the athlete square, take one guarded step out before attacking.

raw.name: Break-and-Reset Position (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Review close-range rounds for clean break position, not only inside scoring.
raw.why: Learn where to stand after the referee break or natural release from close range.

instructions: Review brief close-range exchanges and classify the opponent's torso posture.
Identify which posture gives a legal knee line without pulling or prolonged control.
Choose the release direction that avoids their immediate punch return.

mindset.anchor: See the posture, knee once, release.
mindset.context: Finish separated with guard high and both feet ready.
mindset.focus: Opponent torso folding, elbows widening or weight settling as distance collapses.
mindset.intent: Knee only from balanced contact and release without extending the tie-up.
mindset.reset: If the target line or balance is poor, frame away and reset punching range.

raw.name: Knee Opportunity Recognition (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Count only knees followed by prompt balanced separation.
raw.why: Recognise when close-range posture creates an immediate legal knee opportunity.

instructions: Compare tie-up entries after blocks, punches and opponent kick recovery.
Identify which entry protects the head and arrives with hips under the torso.
Mark the loaded-knee cue that cancels contact before the hands reach.

mindset.anchor: Earn the tie-up, act immediately.
mindset.context: Finish with one legal close-range action and prompt separation in stance.
mindset.focus: Opponent elbows closing, kick recovery or forward posture after punching.
mindset.intent: Reach close range behind a guard reaction or completed opponent attack.
mindset.reset: If their posture and knees remain loaded, stay in guard and exit rather than reaching for the neck.

raw.name: Safe Tie-Up Entry (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Drill entry, one action and release without prolonged holding.
raw.why: Identify how to enter a brief legal tie-up without absorbing clean punches, kicks or knees.

instructions: Study how the expected opponent resets after referee and natural breaks.
Identify the consistent step or guard opening that creates the re-entry.
Choose one scoring action and the square-stance cue that delays it.

mindset.anchor: Own the reset before the re-entry.
mindset.context: Finish after one clean score at an angle, outside return fire.
mindset.focus: The direction the expected opponent steps and the hand they drop while resetting.
mindset.intent: Re-enter only after guard and stance are restored on separation.
mindset.reset: If separation leaves the athlete square, cover and take space before attacking again.

raw.name: Clinch Break Re-Entry (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Rehearse release, stance recovery and one re-entry as separate beats.
raw.why: Prepare the opponent-specific scoring action after a brief clinch breaks.

instructions: Identify the exact entry that produces the opponent's vulnerable posture.
Choose the legal knee line available before they rebuild stance.
Define the recovered-posture cue that cancels the knee and triggers release.

mindset.anchor: Contact, posture cue, one knee.
mindset.context: Finish separated on the safe side of the opponent's rear hand.
mindset.focus: Their elbows flare, torso bends or weight plants after the matchup's chosen entry.
mindset.intent: Deliver the knee on contact before the tie-up becomes static.
mindset.reset: If posture recovers before contact, release and return to guarded striking.

raw.name: Immediate Knee Opportunity (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Drill the opportunity at full decision speed with only one knee per held contact.
raw.why: Exploit the expected opponent's specific posture cue for a single immediate knee.

instructions: Catalogue the expected opponent's first reaction to upper-body contact.
Match open torso, hard frame and turning escape to distinct rule-appropriate responses.
Define the static-contact cue that ends the exchange immediately.

mindset.anchor: First response decides the one legal action.
mindset.context: Finish after a prompt score or clean separation with guard restored.
mindset.focus: Whether they stiff-arm, cover, turn, posture tall or drive chest-to-chest.
mindset.intent: Choose immediate knee, frame-and-strike or release from their first response.
mindset.reset: If contact becomes static, obey the break and return to stance without fighting for prolonged control.

raw.name: Opponent Tie-Up Response (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Rehearse random responses with one action maximum before release.
raw.why: Prepare for how the expected opponent reacts when brief close-range contact is made.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's response to the planned close-range combination.
Assign forward fold or chest collision to the brief-clinch branch.
Assign pivot or loaded-counter posture to the striking exit branch.

mindset.anchor: Strike the opening; tie up the collision.
mindset.context: Finish with one immediate legal action and balanced release.
mindset.focus: Their shell, forward fold or collision after the selected hand combination.
mindset.intent: Connect only on the matchup reaction that safely closes distance.
mindset.reset: If they pivot or remain upright with counters loaded, angle out instead of grabbing.

raw.name: Strike-to-Brief-Clinch Decision (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Rehearse the decision with immediate release after the legal close-range action.
raw.why: Decide when the expected opponent's reaction to strikes makes a brief tie-up and knee superior to another punch.

instructions: Name the one posture cue carried into the fight.
Visualise the trusted entry, legal action and immediate release.
Rehearse the loaded-knee danger cue followed by the familiar exit.

mindset.anchor: One cue, one close action, out.
mindset.context: Finish separated in stance with head protected.
mindset.focus: The single elbow or torso cue repeatedly confirmed in camp.
mindset.intent: Enter, score once and release on the rehearsed posture picture.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent's knee line stays loaded; guard and exit without tie-up.

raw.name: First Close-Range Cue (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Keep this as a short close-range reminder.
raw.why: Retain one familiar cue for the first safe close-range action.

instructions: Recall the single contact position used successfully in preparation.
Pair it with the one legal knee and practiced release direction.
Close on the poor-position danger cue and the known guard reset.

mindset.anchor: Immediate knee or immediate release.
mindset.context: Finish outside close range with both feet under the hips.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed body position that requires no prolonged holding or adjustment.
mindset.intent: Use the familiar knee only when balance and legal target are already present.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: grip or posture needs rebuilding; release immediately and reset guard.

raw.name: Knee-and-Release Rule (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Do not add another close-range option in fight week.
raw.why: Compress brief-clinch work to one rule-compliant knee-and-release sequence.

instructions: Compare the same counter against short, correct and overextended opponent entries.
Mark where the return lands with full form and where it becomes crowded.
Choose the range adjustment used before the next counter attempt.

mindset.anchor: Right counter, right distance.
mindset.context: Finish at the counter's ideal range with room to defend the next weapon.
mindset.focus: Opponent step depth and where their attack finishes relative to the athlete's lead foot.
mindset.intent: Hold the distance where defence and return fit inside one balanced exchange.
mindset.reset: If distance collapses too far, tie up briefly or angle out before trying to counter.

raw.name: Counter Range Audit (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Audit technical rounds for clean distance rather than total counter attempts.
raw.why: Learn which ranges make the athlete's preferred counters score cleanly and which make them jam or miss.

instructions: Separate cues for low, body and head kick lines in repeated clips.
Match each clear line to check, block, withdraw or evade before naming a counter.
Select the legal return available during the opponent's kicking-leg recovery.

mindset.anchor: See the hip, own the recovery beat.
mindset.context: Finish in stance after the return, outside the opponent's follow-up hands.
mindset.focus: Hip turn, chamber, supporting-foot pivot and weight transfer before the kick releases.
mindset.intent: Choose the defensive action from the kick line before selecting the legal counter.
mindset.reset: If the line is unclear, use the safest cover or distance defence and reset stance.

raw.name: Kick Counter Trigger Map (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Validate that the counter lands without delaying stance recovery.
raw.why: Recognise kick preparation early enough to defend and return in balance.

instructions: Rewind repeated punch entries to the first visible foot or shoulder cue.
Name the punch pattern and the defensive opening it creates.
Choose one counter and the post-counter position that avoids the remaining punches.

mindset.anchor: Read the entry, counter the opening.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the final punch line with guard restored.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot step, shoulder turn, guard opening and the first two punches of the pattern.
mindset.intent: Select a legal punch counter before the combination reaches full speed.
mindset.reset: If the pattern changes, cover and angle away instead of guessing the return.

raw.name: Punch Counter Trigger Map (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Call the pattern correctly from the cue in three new examples.
raw.why: Identify the earliest cue and pattern in the opponent's punch entries.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's preferred hand or feint setup for the body kick.
Select the block, evade or distance response that preserves stance against that line.
Locate the return opportunity during their leg landing and define the no-window exit.

mindset.anchor: Protect the body; score on the landing.
mindset.context: Finish after the return at an angle beyond the opponent's follow-up punch.
mindset.focus: Their hand setup, hip line and guard position while the kicking leg travels to the body.
mindset.intent: Complete the chosen defence before returning into the scoring window.
mindset.reset: If the kick leaves them balanced and covered, exit rather than reaching for a late return.

raw.name: Body-Kick Counter Decision (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Drill the defence-return-exit sequence against the matchup setup.
raw.why: Exploit the expected opponent's body-kick setup without surrendering body protection.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's immediate answer after the selected counter lands.
Map the side their feet and shoulders need to turn for that answer.
Choose the angle that forces the extra turn and the blocked-lane defensive contingency.

mindset.anchor: Counter once, disappear from the return line.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's lead shoulder or beyond their kicking-side hip.
mindset.focus: Their rear shoulder, lead foot and preferred second attack after absorbing a counter.
mindset.intent: Complete the return and leave along the side their follow-up cannot track.
mindset.reset: If the angle is blocked, cover in place briefly and exit after their follow-up finishes.

raw.name: Counter-and-Angle Exit (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Review whether the exit beats the opponent's second attack in live rounds.
raw.why: Choose the exit angle that prevents the expected opponent from countering the counter.

instructions: Separate the expected opponent's inside and outside low-kick setups.
Choose check, withdraw or intercept from the athlete's weight position at release.
Match the opponent's slow or fast stance recovery to a legal counter or disciplined reset.

mindset.anchor: Solve the low kick, then take the recovery.
mindset.context: Finish balanced after a check, withdrawal, intercept or counter with both feet ready.
mindset.focus: Supporting-leg load, kick side and how quickly the opponent replaces their stance.
mindset.intent: Defend or intercept according to weight placement, then score during stance recovery.
mindset.reset: If the opponent recovers square and guarded, reset instead of forcing the return.

raw.name: Low-Kick Counter Decision (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Rehearse the decision with varied low-kick lines and require balanced finishes.
raw.why: Build an opponent-specific answer to inside and outside low kicks.

instructions: Name the one opponent cue carried into the opening exchange.
Visualise the familiar defence, counter and finishing position.
Rehearse one changed-pattern danger cue followed by the practiced exit.

mindset.anchor: One signal, one clean return.
mindset.context: Finish balanced outside the next punch or kick line.
mindset.focus: The single foot, shoulder or hip cue confirmed throughout camp.
mindset.intent: Fire only when the rehearsed punch or kick launch signal appears.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the attack pattern changes; cover, angle out and resume reading.

raw.name: First Counter Trigger (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Keep the final review to this trusted trigger.
raw.why: Retain one familiar opening cue for the trusted counter.

instructions: Recall the single kick line prepared most often in camp.
Pair it with the trusted defence and legal return already drilled.
Close on the heavy-stance danger cue and the familiar withdrawal reset.

mindset.anchor: Read the hip, defend, return, recover.
mindset.context: Finish in full stance with guard protecting the opponent's hands.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed hip turn that identifies the selected kick line.
mindset.intent: Use the familiar response against the opponent's best-known kick.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: stance is too heavy to defend cleanly; withdraw and restore balance.

raw.name: One Trusted Kick Counter (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Use one short mental repetition and stop.
raw.why: Compress kick defence to one reliable counter sequence.

instructions: Plot the athlete's exit after each successful long-range score.
Mark whether the lane returns to centre or drifts toward the boundary.
Choose the pivot that avoids the opponent's fastest tracking side.

mindset.anchor: Exit into space that keeps the weapons long.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre at the athlete's preferred kick range.
mindset.focus: Opponent lead foot, boundary position and the side their shoulders can turn fastest.
mindset.intent: Leave through open floor instead of backing toward the ring boundary.
mindset.reset: If both lateral lanes close, cover forward briefly and pivot out after contact.

raw.name: Exit Lane Audit (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Audit the next technical round for exits that preserve long range.
raw.why: Identify the exits that preserve kicking space after the athlete scores.

instructions: Mark the clean contact range for the athlete's primary low, body and head kicks.
Compare the opponent's nearest legal return at each distance.
Select the stance recovery needed after every kick line.

mindset.anchor: Reach with the weapon, not the posture.
mindset.context: Finish with the kicking foot recovered outside immediate punching range.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot gap, hip reach and whether the opponent can punch during recovery.
mindset.intent: Choose the kick whose line and recovery fit the available range.
mindset.reset: If the kick would reach only by leaning, step out and rebuild distance.

raw.name: Kick Range Map (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Confirm range in technical work using clean form as the scoring standard.
raw.why: Map the exact distances for low, body and head kicks without sacrificing balance.

instructions: Compare which long weapon stops straight movement, lateral movement and planted pressure.
Identify the recovery position each weapon leaves against punches and kicks.
Choose a simple weapon-to-entry-line rule for the next session.

mindset.anchor: Choose the long tool for the line.
mindset.context: Finish at range with the opponent forced to reset their feet.
mindset.focus: Straight entry, outside step or planted stance at the edge of range.
mindset.intent: Match the long weapon to the opponent's direction rather than repeating one tool.
mindset.reset: If the opponent crosses beneath the weapon, guard and angle away before firing again.

raw.name: Long-Weapon Range Control (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Track whether the chosen tool controls movement without repeated retreats.
raw.why: Use the jab, front kick and long round kick to control different entry lines.

instructions: Collect examples of straight, angled and kick-led entries.
Assign a long weapon, defensive step or guarded exit to each entry type.
Name the ambiguous cue that requires movement without a counter.

mindset.anchor: Classify the entry before choosing the answer.
mindset.context: Finish at long range with the opponent's forward line broken.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot direction, hip load and whether hands or kicks initiate the approach.
mindset.intent: Differentiate straight pressure, lateral entry and kick-led entry before acting.
mindset.reset: When the entry type is unclear, guard and move to open space before countering.

raw.name: Opponent Entry Reaction (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Call the entry type correctly during the next range drill.
raw.why: Learn the athlete's first safe response to different ways an opponent enters long range.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's primary pressure entry and identify its committed step.
Choose the jab, front kick, low kick or knee that reaches that step safely.
Add a stopped-pressure exit and a continued-pressure defensive branch.

mindset.anchor: Touch the step, then take the angle.
mindset.context: Finish at long range with the opponent needing to turn before advancing again.
mindset.focus: The expected opponent's lead-foot landing and guard shape during pressure entry.
mindset.intent: Intercept before their punching range is established, then leave the follow-up line.
mindset.reset: If the intercept fails to halt them, cover and angle rather than repeating at close range.

raw.name: Intercept Forward Pressure (Kickboxing)
raw.progress: Rehearse the intercept against the opponent's actual entry rhythm.
raw.why: Select the matchup-specific weapon that interrupts the opponent's committed forward step.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's first response to the selected scoring kick.
Match straight pursuit, return kick and lateral chase to distinct exits.
Identify the blocked-lane cue that replaces movement with guarded recovery.

mindset.anchor: The kick is finished when the exit is finished.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the opponent's counter line with both feet under the hips.
