mindset.context: Finish with effective offence or a clean reset away from dead position.
mindset.focus: The familiar head-and-hand position that makes the chosen offence available.
mindset.intent: Maintain the trusted control only while it creates a strike, takedown or advance.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: control becomes static or inside position disappears; release and re-square.

raw.name: One Fence Control Rule (MMA)
raw.progress: Use the rule as a short reminder, with no new fence sequence.
raw.why: Compress fence work to one rule that turns control into meaningful offence.

instructions: Find three attacks and rewind to the earliest repeatable movement before each one.
Separate cues for punches, kicks, entries and level changes.
Rank the cues by reliability and choose only the clearest for training.

mindset.anchor: Counter the launch, not the noise.
mindset.context: Finish outside the attacking line with vision and stance preserved.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot load, shoulder twitch, hand drop, level dip or stance switch that precedes offence.
mindset.intent: Read the start of the attack rather than reacting to impact.
mindset.reset: If the cue is ambiguous, keep the guard and angle away instead of guessing a counter.

raw.name: Attack Trigger Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Call the attack correctly from the cue in three fresh clips before progressing.
raw.why: Build a library of the opponent's initiating cues before choosing any counter.

instructions: Compare counters that halt the opponent with counters they absorb while still advancing.
For a stopped opponent, name the safe exit lane; for continued drive, name the connection.
Reject any follow-up that leaves the athlete square with no answer to the next phase.

mindset.anchor: Exit stopped pressure; connect through continuing pressure.
mindset.context: Finish at a clean outside angle or with secure head-and-hand contact.
mindset.focus: Whether their feet stop, posture folds forward or hips continue driving into range.
mindset.intent: Choose the finish from the opponent's forward momentum after the counter.
mindset.reset: If balance is unclear, post and circle to open space before adding offence.

raw.name: Counter Exit or Connection (MMA)
raw.progress: Review the next counter round for correct finishes after both reactions.
raw.why: Recognise when a landed counter should end with an angle and when it should become grappling contact.

instructions: Pause examples at the moment the first attack enters range and mark both athletes' feet.
Decide which counters retain space and which invite immediate body contact.
Assign an exit or connection response to each range before reviewing the result.

mindset.anchor: Score with room for the next phase.
mindset.context: Finish beyond their follow-up strike or in deliberate inside control.
mindset.focus: The opponent's step depth and whether their hips or shoulders enter after the strike.
mindset.intent: Counter only from a range that leaves a defendable second beat.
mindset.reset: If they crash through the counter line, frame, pummel or angle clear instead of admiring the shot.

raw.name: Safe Counter Range (MMA)
raw.progress: Confirm in technical work that the counter leaves a reliable defensive second action.
raw.why: Distinguish counter range from the distance where a counter becomes a clinch or takedown risk.

instructions: Identify the opponent's preferred level-change setup and the first defensive contact it requires.
Locate the brief window when their head rises or hands separate after the defence.
Choose one legal return and the angle that avoids their immediate re-shot.

mindset.anchor: Stop the entry, find the head, leave the line.
mindset.context: Finish upright at an angle after a legal strike or with dominant front-head position.
mindset.focus: Head position, lead knee and reaching hands as they change level from striking range.
mindset.intent: Defend the entry first, then strike during their posture recovery.
mindset.reset: If hip control is not secure, frame and circle before attempting the return strike.

raw.name: Counter After Level Change (MMA)
raw.progress: Score the drill only when defence is complete before the counter begins.
raw.why: Punish the expected opponent's level-change entry without confusing it with a failed-shot scramble.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's recovery after the exact counter selected for camp.
Mark the recovery that creates hip access and the recovery that removes it.
Build a two-branch rule: connect on the exposed stance, exit on the recovered stance.

mindset.anchor: The counter earns the entry; the feet confirm it.
mindset.context: Finish connected below the hips or safely outside the return attack.
mindset.focus: A high guard, squared feet or forward recovery step after the chosen counter.
mindset.intent: Change levels only when the counter fixes posture or stance in the planned direction.
mindset.reset: If the opponent retracts hips or regains angle, take the strike and exit rather than forcing the shot.

raw.name: Counter-to-Takedown Decision (MMA)
raw.progress: Test both opponent reactions in constrained drilling without adding a third option.
raw.why: Identify which expected striking reaction exposes a takedown after the counter lands.

instructions: Separate footage of fully cleared shots from attempts that still retain meaningful control.
Choose the opponent-specific rise or retreat cue that confirms the shot is over.
Match that cue to one high-percentage strike or positional takeover and its safe finish.

mindset.anchor: Failed means cleared; then punish.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean strike, a dominant spin behind or separation on the athlete's terms.
mindset.focus: Their knees, hands and head position as they abandon the finish or rise.
mindset.intent: Turn a defended shot into immediate effective offence without surrendering hip safety.
mindset.reset: If they retain a leg or body lock, keep defending and improve position before striking.

raw.name: Punish Failed Shot (MMA)
raw.progress: Review whether the follow-up begins only after the legs and hips are free.
raw.why: Exploit the moment after the expected opponent's takedown attempt has clearly failed.

instructions: Recall the single counter already selected for the matchup.
Attach the exact familiar exit step used after it in camp.
End with the square-stance danger cue and the known angle reset.

mindset.anchor: Counter complete means position restored.
mindset.context: Finish seeing both hands and the opponent's hips from a stable base.
mindset.focus: The familiar impact or posture cue confirming the response has finished.
mindset.intent: Complete the exit before looking for another counter.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: staying square for a second exchange; step to the trained outside angle and reframe.

raw.name: Counter-and-Reset Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Use this as a brief completion reminder, not a new combination study.
raw.why: Keep the counter plan disciplined by attaching one reset to the trusted response.

instructions: Name the one opening cue retained from camp analysis.
Visualise the familiar counter and its exact post-counter angle.
Rehearse one false read followed by the practiced defensive reset.

mindset.anchor: One launch signal, one answer.
mindset.context: Finish outside the return line with stance ready.
mindset.focus: The single shoulder, foot or level cue repeatedly seen in preparation.
mindset.intent: Wait for the rehearsed launch signal and fire the trusted counter.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the attack shape changes; cover, angle out and return to observation.

raw.name: First Counter Trigger (MMA)
raw.progress: Take only this trigger into the final review.
raw.why: Reduce the opening counter plan to the opponent's most familiar initiating cue.

instructions: Find entries where the opponent covers distance with a second committed step.
Freeze the last frame where a lateral exit remains available without crossing feet.
Assign a frame-and-pummel response for every example where that frame has passed.

mindset.anchor: Beat the hands or win the contact.
mindset.context: Finish at an outside angle before connection, or in a stable clinch if the exit was late.
mindset.focus: The opponent's chest crossing over the lead knee while the rear foot drives forward.
mindset.intent: Leave on the entry step rather than after hands reach the torso.
mindset.reset: If contact is already made, establish frames and inside position instead of retreating upright.

raw.name: Exit Before Connection (MMA)
raw.progress: In technical rounds, grade the timing of the exit rather than total distance travelled.
raw.why: Recognise the final beat available to exit before the opponent secures body contact.

instructions: Compare how the opponent closes distance after each primary long-range weapon.
Note whether they retreat, parry and return, catch timing or change level underneath.
Choose the weapon whose recovery best answers the most common reaction.

mindset.anchor: Long offence must return to a defendable stance.
mindset.context: Finish with both hips under control and an exit lane visible.
mindset.focus: Opponent reactions to the lead kick, straight strike and feint from outside range.
mindset.intent: Select long attacks that preserve balance and hide the next defensive read.
mindset.reset: If the weapon leaves the stance square or leg available, recover before repeating it.

raw.name: Long-Range Threat Scan (MMA)
raw.progress: Carry the selected weapon and recovery into one low-volume range round.
raw.why: Identify which long-range weapons deter entry and which invite a level change or catch.

instructions: Mark the distance for the athlete's longest reliable strike in three exchanges.
Mark where the opponent can enter punches, kicks, clinch contact or a shot from one movement.
Define the foot-position cue that keeps the athlete in the useful gap between those zones.

mindset.anchor: Own the gap between strike and connection.
mindset.context: Finish at long striking range with the centreline and hips protected.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot distance plus the opponent's ability to touch the hips without an extra step.
mindset.intent: Hold the range that scores while keeping enough space to read phase changes.
mindset.reset: When ranges collapse, frame or pivot back to the chosen long-range marker.

raw.name: MMA Range Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Check the range marker during drilling without adding volume.
raw.why: Separate clean striking range from the distances where kicks, punches, clinches and shots overlap.

instructions: Trace the opponent's pressure route and identify the step that removes the final open lane.
Choose the opponent-specific pivot or lateral step that beats their steering shoulder.
Define the fence-contact contingency when the early angle is missed.

mindset.anchor: Angle on step two; do not donate the fence.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre with the opponent forced to turn before attacking again.
mindset.focus: The second retreating step and the opponent's shoulder line steering the approach.
mindset.intent: Turn while open space remains, not after the back foot meets the boundary.
mindset.reset: If the fence is already reached, plant, frame and exit through a rehearsed side rather than circling blindly.

raw.name: Angle Off Before Fence (MMA)
raw.progress: Grade the next pressure drill on exits completed before boundary contact.
raw.why: Prevent the expected pressure pattern from carrying the athlete to the cage before the angle is taken.

instructions: Study the exact entry pattern expected in the matchup and identify its committed first step.
Select one intercept that lands before their hands or hips establish control.
Add a branch for stopped momentum and a branch for continued forward drive.

mindset.anchor: Intercept, assess momentum, leave.
mindset.context: Finish outside their second step or in deliberate contact with head position.
mindset.focus: The expected opponent's lead-foot landing and head line during their preferred entry.
mindset.intent: Damage or disrupt the entry while preserving the exit from the follow-up phase.
mindset.reset: If the intercept does not stop momentum, frame and angle rather than throwing in place.

raw.name: Intercept the Entry (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the MMA intercept against the opponent's actual entry rhythm and transition threat.
raw.why: Choose an opponent-specific intercept for the first committed step into range.

instructions: Measure the expected opponent's level-change distance from their preferred setup.
Compare it with the recovery position after the athlete's chosen long strikes.
Remove or modify the strike that repeatedly leaves both feet inside the launch window.

mindset.anchor: Know the shot line before opening the strike line.
mindset.context: Finish every long attack beyond hip contact or prepared to defend it.
mindset.focus: Their penetration-step reach after the setup they are most likely to use.
mindset.intent: Score without placing both feet inside the opponent's best shot window.
mindset.reset: When both feet enter that window, recover one step or present a planned anti-entry frame.

raw.name: Takedown-Threat Distance (MMA)
raw.progress: Validate the chosen range against live entry attempts at controlled pace.
raw.why: Calibrate striking choices around the expected opponent's true takedown launch distance.

instructions: Name the single familiar action used to establish distance.
Visualise the expected first-step reaction and the trained range response.
Rehearse the two-beat danger cue followed by the known lateral reset.

mindset.anchor: Touch range, read the step, recover.
mindset.context: Finish the opening exchange in open space with stance intact.
mindset.focus: The opponent's first step after the known range-finding action.
mindset.intent: Establish distance with the trusted long weapon and recover immediately.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: they cover two beats at once; angle out and restore the long-range marker.

raw.name: First-Round Range Script (MMA)
raw.progress: Keep the script to this one opening read.
raw.why: Carry one familiar opening range check into the first exchange.

instructions: Recall the one foot-position cue used successfully in camp.
Pair it with the familiar pivot or lateral step, without adding strikes.
End on the boundary danger cue and the opposite-side reset.

mindset.anchor: See the foot, take the lane.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre with the opponent outside the athlete's lead shoulder.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed lead-foot crossing that signals the outside lane is available.
mindset.intent: Leave as soon as the opponent's pressure step closes the chosen buffer.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the lane closes toward the fence; frame, re-square and use the practiced opposite exit.

raw.name: Preferred Exit Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Use only this exit reminder in the final technical session.
raw.why: Lock in the safest familiar exit cue for the final preparation window.

instructions: Sample repeated exchanges from open space, contact and ground where available.
Record only the first reaction to the same stimulus in each sample.
Keep tendencies that recur and discard isolated actions.

mindset.anchor: Repeat before you rely.
mindset.context: Finish with one confirmed tendency for each relevant phase.
mindset.focus: Their first guard, footwork, clinch or get-up reaction under a familiar threat.
mindset.intent: Separate reliable tendencies from one-off responses.
mindset.reset: When reactions vary, return to observation rather than inventing a fixed rule.

raw.name: Opponent Reaction Scan (MMA)
raw.progress: Confirm one retained tendency during the next scheduled technical review.
raw.why: Build a clear picture of the opponent's recurring first reactions across MMA phases.

instructions: Label the start and end phase of five representative exchanges.
Mark the single cue that caused each transition rather than every action inside it.
Identify the route where the athlete most often arrives out of position.

mindset.anchor: Know which phase is arriving.
mindset.context: Finish each transition with stance, grips or base ready for effective offence.
mindset.focus: The contact or distance cue that ends one phase and starts the next.
mindset.intent: Recognise phase changes early enough to arrive organised.
mindset.reset: If the route becomes unclear, protect posture and return to the last stable position.

raw.name: Phase Route Review (MMA)
raw.progress: Review that route in the next technical session and confirm an organised arrival.
raw.why: See the routes that repeatedly move an exchange between striking, clinch, fence and ground.

instructions: Choose one common loss of structure in each phase relevant to the athlete.
Name the smallest reliable reset that restores safety in that phase.
Identify the familiar action used only after the reset is complete.

mindset.anchor: Structure is the route back to offence.
mindset.context: Finish in a known defensive position with vision and base restored.
mindset.focus: The first posture, grip or base failure that makes continuation unsafe.
mindset.intent: Return to structure before attempting to regain offence.
mindset.reset: Use the phase-specific reset: re-square standing, pummel in contact or rebuild frames underneath.

raw.name: Safe Reset Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Track whether technical rounds restore structure before restarting offence.
raw.why: Define safe resets for lost striking, clinch and ground positions.

instructions: Trace the opponent's danger sequence backward from its effective finish.
Identify the earliest visible gate where the route can be denied reliably.
Choose the denial and the late-read emergency response as separate decisions.

mindset.anchor: Stop the route at its first gate.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the opponent's preferred transition with position intact.
mindset.focus: The setup, foot position or grip that starts their highest-risk sequence.
mindset.intent: Remove the route's enabling position before counterattacking.
mindset.reset: If denial arrives late, protect the threatened position and exit the sequence safely.

raw.name: Danger Route Denial (MMA)
raw.progress: Review whether training stops the route at the gate rather than surviving its finish.
raw.why: Deny the expected opponent's most damaging route between phases.

instructions: Review the athlete's three most likely advantageous positions in the matchup.
Name the strike, submission threat or positional advance available from each.
Remove any route whose only outcome is holding without productive continuation.

mindset.anchor: Position is useful when offence follows.
mindset.context: Finish each planned route with a clear scoring or fight-ending action.
mindset.focus: What happens immediately after winning range, fence, top or back position.
mindset.intent: Keep routes that create impact, advancement or credible finishing threats.
mindset.reset: If a position stays static, advance, attack or reset rather than counting empty control.

raw.name: Effective Offence Check (MMA)
raw.progress: Evaluate the next simulation by effective outcomes after position is won.
raw.why: Judge whether the matchup plan converts position into meaningful MMA offence.

instructions: Select the transition most likely to define the matchup.
Study the expected opponent's first recovery action after that transition.
Assign one continuation and one unfamiliar-reaction reset.

mindset.anchor: Read the landing of the transition.
mindset.context: Finish with effective offence from the first stable position in phase two.
mindset.focus: Their posture immediately after the planned strike, clinch break, takedown or stand-up.
mindset.intent: Make the second action from the expected opponent's recovery position.
mindset.reset: If the recovery differs from the studied picture, stabilise and reassess before continuing.

raw.name: Second-Phase Decision (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the second decision from the realistic transition, not a static start.
raw.why: Prepare the next decision after the matchup's most likely phase transition.

instructions: Name the single opening cue retained from camp.
Pair it with the one familiar response already rehearsed.
Close on the changed-picture danger cue and the known centre reset.

mindset.anchor: Read the phase, then act once.
mindset.context: Finish the opening exchange in a stable, familiar position.
mindset.focus: The opponent's first stance, distance or posture signal from preparation.
mindset.intent: Begin in the trained response as soon as the known picture appears.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opening picture changes; protect stance and reset to centre.

raw.name: Opening Phase Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Use this as a brief opening reminder only.
raw.why: Retain one familiar cue that identifies the likely opening phase.

instructions: Recall the single loss-of-structure cue used throughout camp.
Visualise the one familiar positional reset attached to it.
Name the action that must wait until structure is restored.

mindset.anchor: Structure before the restart.
mindset.context: Finish re-square, framed or based in the phase-appropriate safe position.
mindset.focus: The familiar sign of lost base, posture or inside position.
mindset.intent: Interrupt disorder before trying to reclaim offence.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: continuing from the broken position; return immediately to the trained safe structure.

raw.name: Trusted Reset Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Keep the final review to this reset and no new analysis.
raw.why: Carry one known reset for the moment the first MMA exchange loses structure.

instructions: Compare level changes, clinch entries and reactive connections from open space.
Identify which setup moves the opponent's hands away from the intended contact point.
Mark the posture cue that makes each route unsafe before commitment.

mindset.anchor: Safe contact starts before the grip.
mindset.context: Finish connected with head position and feet able to drive or turn.
mindset.focus: The opponent's hand position and weight transfer after jabs, kicks or feints.
mindset.intent: Arrive at hips or upper-body control with posture protected.
mindset.reset: If the entry line is uncovered, return to range and rebuild behind a defensive reaction.

raw.name: Entry-to-Contact Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Drill the highest-quality route only to secure contact and stable base.
raw.why: Map how the athlete reaches meaningful grappling contact through striking danger.

instructions: Review where each primary takedown actually lands against common stance reactions.
Identify the grip and finishing direction that steer toward the preferred resulting position.
Define the first control needed when the opponent turns and the ideal destination is missed.

mindset.anchor: Name the landing before the entry.
mindset.context: Finish past the legs, in strong half guard or another preselected advantageous position.
mindset.focus: Opponent stance, fence proximity and likely turn or guard recovery during descent.
mindset.intent: Direct the takedown toward a stable landing that supports immediate offence.
mindset.reset: If the planned landing is lost, secure base and prioritise position before striking or submitting.

raw.name: Ground Destination Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Track successful takedowns by resulting position and offence, not by floor contact alone.
raw.why: Choose the position each takedown should produce instead of treating floor contact as the finish.

instructions: Select three familiar strikes or feints and observe the opponent's immediate response.
Choose the response that gives the cleanest head line and hip access.
Write one no-entry cue for the same setup when the opponent remains structurally ready.

mindset.anchor: The reaction opens the takedown.
mindset.context: Finish on connected hips or back at safe setup range.
mindset.focus: Feet squaring, weight rising, elbows lifting or a committed counter after the setup.
mindset.intent: Enter on changed stance or posture, not simply because a setup was thrown.
mindset.reset: If the reaction does not move stance or posture, reset behind guard without shooting.

raw.name: Takedown Setup Reaction (MMA)
raw.progress: Test whether the chosen reaction reliably precedes clean connection in drilling.
raw.why: Identify the specific opponent reaction that makes a takedown entry available.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's highest-frequency defence to the primary attempt.
Choose the secondary attack that uses the direction and weight of that defence.
Mark the connection-loss cue that ends the chain before position deteriorates.

mindset.anchor: Their defence names the next attack.
mindset.context: Finish on the secondary takedown or in a stable clinch reset.
mindset.focus: The opponent's sprawl, whizzer, step-out or hip turn after the primary entry.
mindset.intent: Change direction or level while connection and base remain useful.
mindset.reset: If both knees collapse or grips separate, recover posture instead of chaining blindly.

raw.name: Chain Attempt Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Drill the chain from a realistic defended first attempt, not a cooperative pause.
raw.why: Use the expected defence to the first takedown as the setup for the next attempt.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's preferred fence defence to the primary takedown.
Match their wide base, underhook or turn to the planned secondary finish.
Specify the head-position loss that pauses the chain and returns to clinch control.

mindset.anchor: Read the base, finish through its weak side.
mindset.context: Finish in an advantageous ground position with control ready for offence.
mindset.focus: Their near-side underhook, knee width, hip height and posting foot against the fence.
mindset.intent: Change finish when the opponent's base defeats the first direction.
mindset.reset: If head position or hand connection is lost, rebuild the clinch before driving again.

raw.name: Fence Finish Decision (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the first-to-second finish transition against the actual defensive shape.
raw.why: Select the best opponent-specific finish once a takedown entry reaches the fence.

instructions: Classify whether the opponent builds up by wall-walk, underhook, sit-out or technical stand-up.
Identify the first support point that makes that route possible.
Choose the denial and the moment to switch from retention into effective offence.

mindset.anchor: Break the first post; preserve top position.
mindset.context: Finish with their shoulders or hips returned to the mat and a stable attacking base.
mindset.focus: The first elbow, hand or knee they use to build height from bottom position.
mindset.intent: Remove the post or hip angle that their get-up depends on.
mindset.reset: If the opponent clears the hips and faces up, reconnect safely or accept the standing reset.

raw.name: Get-Up Denial (MMA)
raw.progress: Review whether the first support was removed before the get-up gathered momentum.
raw.why: Stop the expected opponent's preferred route back to standing before chasing secondary offence.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's preferred wall-walk or technical stand-up sequence.
Find the beat where one hand leaves support and their weight becomes returnable.
Choose the return direction and the grip-loss cue that cancels it.

mindset.anchor: Return the rising base, not a settled stance.
mindset.context: Finish above the hips in controlled top position ready to attack.
mindset.focus: Their posted hand leaving the floor, hips rising and weight committing to one foot.
mindset.intent: Return them only while connection, head position and balance remain secure.
mindset.reset: If grips slip or the opponent faces fully, release to stable clinch control rather than lifting from poor position.

raw.name: Mat Return Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Drill the return from the opponent's real get-up timing and confirm top position afterwards.
raw.why: Identify when the expected opponent's stand-up attempt exposes a safe mat return.

instructions: Study the scramble most likely to follow the primary takedown or escape exchange.
Rank the first objectives: protect submission danger, win head height, control hips, establish top.
Choose the opponent cue that changes the priority from control to disengagement.

mindset.anchor: Post, hips, position, then offence.
mindset.context: Finish on top, behind the hips or safely disengaged with stance restored.
mindset.focus: Head height, hip line and which athlete has the first stable post.
mindset.intent: Secure the highest-value control before attacking during the scramble.
mindset.reset: If no reliable post exists, protect the neck and hips while returning to base.

raw.name: Scramble Priority (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the priority order from an unscripted transition and review the first decision only.
raw.why: Choose the first positional objective when the expected transition becomes disordered.

instructions: Start from the likely post-takedown position against the expected opponent.
Identify the first escape reaction that exposes a strike, pass or submission route.
Choose the offensive continuation and the base cue that must remain intact while attacking.

mindset.anchor: Position earns value through attack.
mindset.context: Finish with clean ground strikes, a credible submission sequence or improved dominant position.
mindset.focus: The opponent's framing elbow, hip turn and hand commitment during their first escape.
mindset.intent: Use control as the platform for offence rather than the final objective.
mindset.reset: If posture or base breaks, re-secure position before forcing damage or a submission.

raw.name: Top Control to Effective Offense (MMA)
raw.progress: Review the round for productive attacks and advances, not static control time.
raw.why: Turn the expected top position into strikes, submission threat or meaningful advancement.

instructions: Recall the opponent reaction most often seen after the planned takedown.
Pair it with the one familiar strike, pass or submission continuation.
Close on the lost-base danger cue and the known stabilising reset.

mindset.anchor: Land, read, continue once.
mindset.context: Finish in the trained dominant position with effective offence available.
mindset.focus: The single frame, hip turn or get-up post expected on landing.
mindset.intent: Advance or strike from the opponent's known first ground reaction.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: base loosens during offence; settle position and rebuild control.

raw.name: First Ground Continuation Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Use one short continuation rehearsal and add nothing new.
raw.why: Preload one familiar continuation after the first successful takedown.

instructions: Name the one familiar setup retained for fight week.
Visualise the known reaction and the trusted entry behind it.
Rehearse the withdrawn-hips danger cue and the practiced abort once.

mindset.anchor: Create the reaction, then connect.
mindset.context: Finish on stable hip contact or safely back at range.
mindset.focus: The single weight shift or guard lift repeatedly created in camp.
mindset.intent: Enter only when the trained stance reaction appears.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent's hips withdraw; abandon the entry and return to the setup stance.

raw.name: First Takedown Setup (MMA)
raw.progress: Keep the review to this first-attempt picture.
raw.why: Retain one familiar setup for the first takedown attempt.

instructions: Review exchanges across open striking, clinch, fence and ground.
Separate activity from results by noting impact, advancement and real finishing threats.
Choose the two most reliable routes into the phase with the best results.

mindset.anchor: Transitions serve the winning phase.
mindset.context: Finish in the position that repeatedly produces meaningful offence.
mindset.focus: Where strikes land cleanly, positions advance or credible submissions develop.
mindset.intent: Use other phases to reach the strongest one rather than competing everywhere equally.
mindset.reset: When a phase produces only neutral control, return to the route that creates impact or advantage.

raw.name: Best Phase Identification (MMA)
raw.progress: Use the next technical session to confirm one route into the identified winning phase.
raw.why: Identify where the athlete consistently creates the most effective offence.

instructions: Review fence arrivals from striking and grappling entries separately.
Identify when the boundary opens a turn, takedown or safe striking lane.
Mark the neutral contact where leaving the cage is tactically superior.

mindset.anchor: Use the cage to create, not to pause.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean strike, advantageous connection or return to centre.
mindset.focus: Opponent foot position, underhook access and available striking angle at fence contact.
mindset.intent: Choose the phase that uses the boundary without settling for empty control.
mindset.reset: If the boundary removes the planned offence, disengage to open space and rebuild.

raw.name: Cage Transition Choice (MMA)
raw.progress: In situational work, require a productive decision within the first fence exchange.
raw.why: Recognise how the cage changes the value of striking, clinch and takedown options.

instructions: Mark long, punching, clinch and shot ranges in repeated exchanges.
Identify the cue that should trigger a deliberate phase change at each boundary.
Name the stable position used when the intended transition is unavailable.

mindset.anchor: Cross ranges with a purpose.
mindset.context: Finish in clean striking space, secure clinch contact or connected to the hips.
mindset.focus: The opponent's foot depth and hand position as long range collapses to body contact.
mindset.intent: Move between phases deliberately instead of drifting through the transition range.
mindset.reset: If the transition arrives without posture or hand position, exit to the last stable range.

raw.name: Range Transition Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Practice calling the phase before crossing its range line.
raw.why: Understand the distances where striking becomes clinch or takedown contact.

instructions: Choose one familiar initiating strike and list the three most common reactions to it.
Assign each distinct reaction to continued strikes, clinch entry or takedown entry.
Add the neutral read that sends the athlete back to range without commitment.

mindset.anchor: One reaction, one phase branch.
mindset.context: Finish with effective striking, secure upper-body control or connected hips.
mindset.focus: High guard with planted feet, forward collision or hips exposed beneath upright retreat.
mindset.intent: Let posture and distance select continued striking, clinch contact or a shot.
mindset.reset: If the reaction is neutral, exit on angle and restart the setup.

raw.name: Strike Clinch or Shot Tree (MMA)
raw.progress: Drill the tree with randomised reactions until phase choice precedes movement.
raw.why: Build a simple three-branch decision for the opponent's first defensive reaction.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's best answer to the athlete's primary phase.
Locate what that answer concedes in distance, hand position, hips or stance.
Build the exact phase switch and the balanced-defence cue that cancels it.

mindset.anchor: Committed defence opens the next phase.
mindset.context: Finish attacking where the opponent's recovery is weakest.
mindset.focus: The matchup-specific shell, sprawl, pummel or disengagement that overcommits posture.
mindset.intent: Switch on their committed defensive reaction rather than from impatience.
mindset.reset: If the defence remains balanced, complete the current action and exit without forcing transition.

raw.name: Opponent Reaction to Phase Switch (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the switch only against the correct opponent-specific reaction.
raw.why: Use the expected opponent's strongest defence in one phase to enter the phase they protect least well.

instructions: Map how the expected opponent exits the primary shot defence.
Choose the recovery beat that exposes a specific strike without abandoning control early.
Add the branch where their forward posture makes re-connection safer than striking.

mindset.anchor: Clear contact, then strike the recovery.
mindset.context: Finish on a legal strike at an angle or reconnect if their posture collapses forward.
mindset.focus: Their head rise, hand separation or square stance when they clear the entry.
mindset.intent: Return to offence as the opponent rebuilds posture after denying the shot.
mindset.reset: If a leg or body lock remains contested, keep positional responsibility before striking.

raw.name: Shot-to-Strike Branch (MMA)
raw.progress: Train the shot-to-strike switch only after a clearly resolved first phase.
raw.why: Use the expected takedown defence to create a clean striking continuation.

instructions: Study the exact strike selected to draw the expected opponent's defensive response.
Identify which response exposes the shot and which response demands a striking exit.
Define the second decision if the first takedown contact meets their preferred defence.

mindset.anchor: Strike creates posture; posture selects the shot.
mindset.context: Finish connected beneath the hips or beyond the opponent's return attack.
mindset.focus: Their hands rising, feet squaring or weight planting after the selected strike.
mindset.intent: Change level on the planned guard or stance shift, not by preset combination count.
mindset.reset: If the hips withdraw or the counter line stays open, finish the strike and angle away.

raw.name: Strike-to-Shot Branch (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the opponent-specific branch from the strike through first defensive contact.
raw.why: Exploit the expected opponent's defensive striking reaction as the entry to their hips.

instructions: Select the matchup's most likely first phase and the transition it usually creates.
Identify the opponent reaction that decides who owns the next stable position.
Choose the immediate second-phase action and the cue that delays it for positional safety.

mindset.anchor: The second phase completes the first attack.
mindset.context: Finish with impact, positional advancement or a credible finishing threat after transition.
mindset.focus: The first stable posture after strike-to-clinch, shot-to-scramble or clinch-to-break.
mindset.intent: Treat the transition result as the real scoring opportunity.
mindset.reset: If the second phase begins without base, secure position before forcing offence.

raw.name: Winning the Second Phase (MMA)
raw.progress: Review complete sequences for who wins after transition, not who initiates first.
raw.why: Plan the opponent-specific action that wins after the opening phase changes.

instructions: Recall the familiar route-A opening and its intended phase.
Name the one reaction that triggers the rehearsed route-B transition.
Close on the no-structure danger cue and the trusted centre reset.

mindset.anchor: A first; B only on cue.
mindset.context: Finish the opening exchange in the stronger phase or safely back at centre.
mindset.focus: The known stance or guard response that closes the first route and opens the second.
mindset.intent: Begin with route A and switch to route B only on the trained cue.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: neither route has structure; reset to centre behind the opening feint.

raw.name: A/B Opening Plan (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse only the two known routes during fight week.
raw.why: Keep two familiar opening routes tied to one clear opponent reaction.

instructions: Name the one reaction retained as the transition signal.
Visualise the familiar phase switch and its finishing position.
Rehearse one absent-cue example followed by the known stance reset.

mindset.anchor: No cue, no switch.
mindset.context: Finish stable in the new phase with the next offence available.
mindset.focus: The single posture or distance cue repeatedly used in camp.
mindset.intent: Switch once, decisively, when the trained reaction appears.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the reaction is incomplete; stay in the current phase and restore stance.

raw.name: First Transition Cue (MMA)
raw.progress: Carry this single transition rule into the final review.
raw.why: Lock in the first familiar signal for changing phase.

instructions: Record the direction of the opponent's first two exits as their back approaches the fence.
Identify whether footwork, a frame, a level change or a clinch creates each escape.
Choose the step and angle that blocks the preferred route while preserving stance and shot defence.

mindset.anchor: Close the door; do not chase the runner.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's lead shoulder with the fence still limiting their next exit.
mindset.focus: First circle, reversal, frame, level change or clinch as the fence nears.
mindset.intent: Deny the preferred cage exit without following it in a straight line.
mindset.reset: If the route is unreadable, square the stance at safe striking range and rebuild the cut.

raw.name: Cage Route Scan (MMA)
raw.progress: During the next technical round, verify whether the predicted first exit appears twice.
raw.why: Learn the opponent's first escape route when forward pressure closes open space.

instructions: Name the strike or feint that changes the opponent's stance or guard most reliably.
Match each reaction to level change, clinch connection or continued striking.
Mark one poor-position cue that cancels the entry before commitment.

mindset.anchor: Pressure creates the shot; position authorises it.
mindset.context: Finish chest-to-hip, on a secure body lock or back at organised striking pressure.
mindset.focus: A widened stance, raised guard, shell or upright retreat after a strike or feint.
mindset.intent: Connect only when the opponent's reaction improves the level change or clinch entry.
mindset.reset: If hips are back, feet are crossed or distance is stretched, stay upright and recover position.

raw.name: Level-Threat Pressure Map (MMA)
raw.progress: Test one mapped reaction in drilling and confirm that the chosen connection arrives balanced.
raw.why: Find the moments when striking pressure makes a wrestling threat believable.

instructions: Identify which opponent escape most often tempts the athlete to overrun the stance.
Freeze the footage at the first posture or foot-position error, not after the counter lands.
Select one two-step positional reset and the familiar action that restarts controlled pressure.

mindset.anchor: Base first, pressure second.
mindset.context: Finish square to the opponent with both defensive reactions available.
mindset.focus: Head over the lead knee, crossed feet, reaching posture or an opponent suddenly gaining a clean angle.
mindset.intent: Restore stance before trying to win the lost ground again.
mindset.reset: Plant under the hips, bring the rear foot back into base and restart behind a familiar feint.

raw.name: Pressure Reset (MMA)
raw.progress: Use the reset once in a pressure round before adding any new offence.
raw.why: Recognise the exact point where organised pressure turns into exposed chasing.

instructions: Track the expected opponent's exit direction from the first fence exchange.
Note their second movement once open space appears: continue, reverse or counter forward.
Place the second cut where that movement will arrive and name the shot or counter cue that cancels pursuit.

mindset.anchor: Win the second corner, not the foot race.
mindset.context: Finish intercepting the next escape lane with stance intact and the opponent still outside centre.
mindset.focus: Whether the opponent continues circling, reverses direction or attacks immediately after clearing the fence.
mindset.intent: Arrive at the next lane before their direction change rather than sprinting behind them.
mindset.reset: If the re-catch line exposes the hips or centreline, hold centre and restart the cut.

raw.name: Cage Re-Catch (MMA)
raw.progress: In situational work, score a re-catch only when the second cut happens without crossed feet.
raw.why: Map the second cut after the expected opponent escapes the first cage trap.

instructions: Classify the opponent's most common fence escape by hands, hips and head position.
Choose one denial specific to that escape and state which side must remain closed.
Define the strike, takedown or positional advance available only after control is restored.

mindset.anchor: Deny the escape that is actually happening.
mindset.context: Finish with restored head-and-hand position, a clean turn or effective offence from stable control.
mindset.focus: Their underhook or pummel, turn, frame, level change or disengagement attempt.
mindset.intent: Answer the escape mechanism before adding offence from the clinch.
mindset.reset: If inside position is lost completely, release safely and re-square instead of clinging to weak control.

raw.name: Fence Escape Denial (MMA)
raw.progress: Review the next fence round for successful denials, not total time spent holding position.
raw.why: Identify the expected opponent's preferred technical escape from fence control and its direct denial.

instructions: Identify which pressure combination makes the expected opponent stop moving their feet.
Mark the beat where their guard commitment hides the change of level.
Define the failed-entry cue that sends the athlete back to striking rather than driving from poor position.

mindset.anchor: Hands make the level; the reaction makes the shot.
mindset.context: Finish on connected hips with head position or return safely to striking range.
mindset.focus: The planned strike making the opponent plant, shell or punch back with hips available.
mindset.intent: Shoot beneath a committed defensive reaction, not beneath neutral posture.
mindset.reset: If their hips retreat or the entry line is visible, return to hands and recover the angle.

raw.name: Level Change Behind Pressure (MMA)
raw.progress: Drill the strike-to-level timing against the expected reaction before adding a finish.
raw.why: Choose the opponent-specific moment when forward striking hides the level change.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's response to the exact strike planned for closing distance.
Label one response for continued striking and a different response for clinch-to-fence connection.
Add the response that demands disengagement, including the safe exit direction.

mindset.anchor: Read the reaction, then choose the phase.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean second strike, connected fence position or a protected disengagement.
mindset.focus: Their guard return, hip position and exit line immediately after the selected entry strike.
mindset.intent: Take the branch that produces effective offence instead of forcing every exchange to the fence.
mindset.reset: If neither clean follow-up nor secure connection exists, angle out before the counter or shot.

raw.name: Strike-to-Fence Decision (MMA)
raw.progress: Rehearse the three-way branch until the correct finish can be called before the second action.
raw.why: Decide whether an opponent-specific strike reaction calls for more striking, fence connection or release.

instructions: State the one cue that permits another forward step.
Pair it with the single familiar response already rehearsed in camp.
Say the danger cue and positional reset aloud before ending the review.

mindset.anchor: Contained, balanced, dangerous.
mindset.context: Finish every pressure exchange able to strike, defend a shot or disengage.
mindset.focus: The familiar cue that confirms the opponent is still contained rather than escaping on an angle.
mindset.intent: Advance only while stance and defensive responsibility remain organised.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: reaching past the lead knee; stop, rebuild base and restart behind the trusted action.

raw.name: Final Pressure Rule (MMA)
raw.progress: Use the rule as the final corner reminder, without expanding the plan.
raw.why: Keep one final rule that prevents pressure from becoming reckless pursuit.

instructions: Recall the single reaction that calls for continued striking.
Recall the alternative reaction that calls for immediate clinch connection.
Close with the known danger cue and one practiced disengagement.

mindset.anchor: First fence touch, one clear branch.
mindset.context: Finish with effective offence or a clean reset, never passive fence holding.
mindset.focus: The opponent's known guard and hip reaction on first fence contact.
mindset.intent: Make the trained strike-or-connect decision without pausing at the boundary.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: head position is lost; release, frame away and re-square in open space.

raw.name: First Cage Decision (MMA)
raw.progress: Keep this as a short first-contact rehearsal only.
raw.why: Preload one familiar choice for the first time the opponent reaches the fence.

instructions: Name the single familiar cue that starts the planned pressure sequence.
Visualise the exact strike-and-cut response and its intended finishing position.
Rehearse the danger cue once, followed immediately by the trained stance reset.

mindset.anchor: See the first step. Take the first lane.
mindset.context: Finish the sequence balanced at the fence line or safely back in centre control.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed stance or first-step cue that exposes the opponent's preferred cage route.
mindset.intent: Start composed and let the familiar cue release the opening attack.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the feet narrow or the opponent changes level; re-square and return to the opening feint.

raw.name: First Pressure Sequence (MMA)
raw.progress: Carry only this opening sequence into fight week; add no new branch.
raw.why: Compress the opening pressure plan to one trained cue and one trusted sequence.

raw.cue: Follow a self-planned or random visual escape path and close the angle without crossing the feet or chasing.
raw.duration: 2 x 90 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Ring Cut-Off Walkdown
raw.notes: Control space and cut the ring by closing angles, not chasing. Low mechanical cost; a taper-safe pressure pattern.

raw.cue: On your own start or a random left/right visual cue, take the 45-degree angle and reset behind the jab.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: 45-Degree Angle Step to Jab Reset
raw.notes: Create a 45-degree attacking angle and reset behind the jab. Angle-creation quality, not a speed or conditioning effort.

raw.cue: Show the level change, then react to a partner response, coach direction call, or random left/right visual cue. Step to the new attack angle and reset.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean reactions each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Level-Change Feint to Angle
raw.notes: Sell the level change to draw a defensive reaction, then step off to improve the penetration or re-attack angle before the next shot. Wrestling-compatible angle creation; SPP only.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the feint no longer changes level cleanly or the angle step finishes outside a stable attack base.

raw.cue: React to a partner exit, coach direction call, or random left/right visual cue. Cut that lane and fully rebuild the base before the next rep.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean reactions each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Pressure Step-Cut Reset
raw.notes: Read the opponent's exit lane, cut it off, and reset the base before punching. Reactive read with a hard lateral brake; SPP only.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the lane read, braking control, or stance reset loses quality.

raw.cue: Track a self-planned path, light partner circle, or random left/right visual cue. Close the escape lane while keeping hips and stance oriented.
raw.duration: 2 x 90 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Cage Circle and Cut-Off
raw.notes: Use light cage-orientation steps. Keep the stance and hips oriented to the opponent while controlling the escape lane; do not chase into open space.

raw.cue: Start from a different scramble shape each rep, chosen before the rep or by a random visual cue. Stand, brake, and establish a balanced striking base.
raw.duration: 3 sets x 3 clean transitions, full base reset between reps
raw.name: Scramble-to-Strike Rebase
raw.notes: Return from a scramble shape into a balanced striking stance. Ground-to-stance transition with a hard brake into base; SPP only. High braking/transition cost carried in braking_demand, not in physiological intensity.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the stand-up slows, the brake becomes heavy, or the striking base is not immediately balanced.

raw.cue: Use a self-chosen or random left/right visual cue to exit laterally, settle the base, then re-enter.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Lateral Exit to Re-Enter
raw.notes: Exit laterally after an exchange, then re-enter with stance intact. Loads lateral knee and ankle more than straight-line resets.

raw.cue: Switch once, settle the new base, and confirm guard and balance before switching back.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Switch-Step Stance Recovery
raw.notes: Switch stance to reset lead-leg kicking options and recover a balanced base after a missed or thrown kick. Hip-rotation dominant.

raw.cue: React to a light partner shot, coach shot call, or random visual shot cue. Sprawl, clear the line, exit to the called side, and fully rebase.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 3 clean reactions each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Sprawl Exit to Ring Angle
raw.notes: Clear the shot line with a sprawl, then exit to an angle and regain striking range. Reactive level-change with high eccentric and trunk cost; SPP only. High braking/transition cost carried in braking_demand, not in physiological intensity.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the sprawl response, angle exit, or stance recovery loses timing or balance.

raw.cue: Start from a marked corner. On your own start or a random left/right visual cue, L-step to the open lane and reset.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Corner Escape L-Step
raw.notes: Escape the ropes or corner with an L-step and reset stance to a safe angle. Lateral knee load under a change of direction.

raw.cue: Use a floor line as the reference. Move on your own start, then recover stance without crossing the feet.
raw.duration: 2 x 60 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Stance Reset Line Drill
raw.notes: Reset base after movement without crossing feet or squaring stance. Lowest-cost base-restoration pattern; safe deep into the taper.

raw.cue: Throw the shadow check hook on your own start or a random pressure cue, then pivot clear and recover stance.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Check-Hook Pivot Out Shadow Drill
raw.notes: Turn the corner off a check-hook pattern and pivot out to an angle. Fight-specific pivot; single-leg pivot loading.

raw.cue: Move from wrestling stance on a self-planned path, mirror a light partner, or follow a random direction cue. Circle without crossing the feet, keep level and head position available, then settle into attack-ready base.
raw.duration: 2 x 60 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Wrestling Stance-Motion Circle Reset
raw.notes: Low-cost wrestling stance-and-motion rehearsal. Maintain base while circling and changing direction so penetration and contact setups stay available without turning the session into conditioning.

raw.cue: On a straight-pressure or shot-line cue, step laterally off the line before reaching the fence, reorient the hips to the opponent, and rebuild a striking and takedown-ready stance.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean exits each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Shot-Line Circle-Off Reset
raw.notes: MMA open-space exit pattern: circle off a straight-line blitz or takedown entry instead of retreating directly toward the fence. Preserve stance and hip orientation for the next defensive layer.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the first step goes straight back, the feet narrow or cross, or the hips turn away from the threat.

raw.cue: After one familiar kick motion, use a self-start or random shot/no-shot visual cue. Place the kicking leg under control, recover hip position, and finish in a stance that can immediately defend a level change.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean recoveries each side, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Kick-Recovery Anti-Shot Rebase
raw.notes: MMA kick-recovery footwork: regain balanced stance and takedown-ready hip position after a kick instead of admiring the strike or landing narrow and tall.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the kicking leg lands narrow or crossed, balance drifts, or the recovered posture is too tall to respond to a level change.

raw.cue: Use a rehearsed break or a light partner release. Disengage, square the base to the threat, then reset before re-entry.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Clinch Exit Square-Up Reset
raw.notes: Disengage, regain base, and reorient to the opponent before re-entry. Use a controlled stance reset off the break.

raw.cue: Use a rehearsed kick line, light partner feed, or random side cue. Check, plant, and angle out to the counter position.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Check and Return Step
raw.notes: Check the low or body kick, plant, and return to stance on an angle to counter. Single-leg balance with an elastic re-plant.

raw.cue: Complete one controlled teep pattern, retreat off the plant, and regain range and stance before the next repetition.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Teep Retreat and Re-Stance
raw.notes: Push-kick to manage distance, retreat off the plant, and rebase without falling backward square. Muay Thai range-control pattern.

raw.cue: Choose the same controlled grappling stand-up each rep, establish base and posture, then reset the connection or distance position.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Submission Hunter Stand-Up Reset
raw.notes: Stand up from a grappling exchange into a balanced grappling stance, regain base, and reset distance or connection position. Appropriate as a controlled BJJ/MMA stand-up transition rather than a striking reset.

raw.cue: On your own start or a random forward visual cue, step out of range, pivot off line, and reset before re-entry.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Step-Back Pivot Reset
raw.notes: Step out of range, pivot off line, then reset stance before re-entry. Moderate hip-rotation and single-side braking cost.

raw.cue: Start one step from a marked fence line. On a self-start, light partner pressure, or random left/right cue, circle along the boundary, turn the corner, and rebase facing center before resetting.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean exits each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Fence Exit to Center Rebase
raw.notes: Defensive MMA cage footwork: leave the fence laterally and recover center-facing stance instead of backing straight into the boundary or turning away from the opponent.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the exit becomes a straight retreat, the feet cross, or the athlete finishes with the hips turned away from center.

raw.cue: From a guarded jab, parry, or long-guard shape, step to the outside lane and close to clinch range. Use a light partner or random visual cue, establish base before the simulated tie, then reset.
raw.duration: 2 sets x 4 clean entries each direction, full stance reset between reps
raw.name: Long-Guard Clinch Entry Step
raw.notes: Rehearse the foot position that closes distance into a Muay Thai clinch without reaching with the upper body. The entry stays technical and no-contact unless a light partner cue is available.
raw.quality_stop_rule: Stop the set when the entry reaches with the upper body, the feet cross, or the base is not established before the simulated tie.

raw.cue: Track a self-planned path, light partner escape, or random left/right visual cue. Step across the escape lane, keep stance width, and herd rather than chase.
raw.duration: 2 x 90 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Thai Ring-Cut Pressure Walkdown
raw.notes: Muay Thai ring-control pattern: apply pressure with small angle cuts so the opponent is steered toward the ropes without crossing the feet or overcommitting into kicks or knees.

raw.cue: After each familiar round-kick pattern, place the kicking leg with control, exit, and rebuild stance before repeating.
raw.duration: 2 x 75 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Kick Exit and Re-Stance Walkthrough
raw.notes: Rehearse the exit position after a familiar round kick. Regain stance and range without repeated kicking or a hard push-off.

raw.cue: Use a floor marker as the guard line. Step around it with knees soft and feet under the hips, pause in a balanced standing passing base, then circle back without crossing the feet.
raw.duration: 2 x 60 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
raw.name: Standing Guard-Pass Base Circle
raw.notes: BJJ standing guard-passing footwork emphasizing balance, posture, and angle around the guard line without reaching, hopping, or turning the drill into speed work.

Battle repeatedly for the pin, underhook and head position as the partner contests turns, reversals, escapes and re-pins. Preserve posture, balance, inside position and decision quality. Reduce resistance if the work becomes sloppy wrestling. The partner may show a controlled takedown threat, but the athlete must keep and recover standing control.

Begin a short striking exchange. The partner may make a genuine committed shot. Read the attack, use appropriate takedown defence only when needed, create safe separation, return 1–2 compact strikes, and restore stance and base.

Begin at first contact. Explosively gain useful inside arm position against controlled resistance, stabilise posture and balance briefly, then release and reset in stance. Stop the rep if it becomes a body lock, throw, or wrestling exchange.

Begin one step from a marked boundary, not pinned to it. As the partner closes, use a strike, frame or angle and regain open space laterally. Reset if body contact becomes established. Stop when stance or defensive shape drops.

Begin only once pain has settled, you no longer need crutches and you can stand on your toes without pain. Hold a stable chair, share your weight equally over both feet and gently rise onto your toes, then lower slowly. Work at your own pace and stop if painful. Keep both feet on level ground; do not add weight, single-leg work, a step or fatigue progressions.

Beside stable support on firm level ground, raise both heels, then transfer weight to the affected leg and slowly lower its heel only to the floor. Do not use a step, lower into deep dorsiflexion, increase depth or add speed or weight. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Box height 12-18" based on experience. Stop the set when ground contact slows.
Box height 12-18". Absorb and stick the landing — no rebound.
Box height 24-30". Max height intent, full reset between reps.
Box height 50% max vertical jump. Absorb quietly, then drive straight up.
Brief hard efforts; excellent for power adaptation

Build credible low and body kicks from both stances without chasing switch-kick volume. Recoil and restore a defensively useful stance after each kick; reduce output if either side becomes square or unstable.
Build long combinations from jab or long guard and finish with an angled exit. Lower the pace if balance or clean target selection fades.
Builds aerobic power; zero joint impact
Builds output for finishing exchanges against the ropes/cage. Alternate between straight and diagonal knees. (95% effort)
Builds plumb-position endurance while striking. Alternate between single collar and double collar ties. (90% effort)
Builds structural neck strength to reduce KO risk - use 5-10lb weight

Change position rather than holding the neck still for long periods. Keep gentle ordinary movement; do not force range or remove prescribed protection. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Change positions and keep comfortable ordinary activity. Avoid prolonged bed rest and forced range; no diagnosis or measured mobility deficit is inferred. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Change positions and keep gentle ordinary neck movement. Tightness does not prove shortened tissue; avoid forceful stretching, traction or pressure on the neck. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. Check or long-guard the imagined attack, reset the feet, and restore kicking range without repeated straight-line retreat. Reduce output if stance widens.
Check the low or body kick, plant, and return to stance on an angle to counter. Single-leg balance with an elastic re-plant.
Chest: land soft with the elbows tracking back.
Choose jab, teep or long kick from the holder’s cue, then recover stance and exit. Reduce output when decisions, recoil or range control lose quality.
Circle in stance at a relaxed pace. Every 8-12 seconds, jab or feint, make an angle exit, then restore preferred range.

Clear the shot line with a sprawl, then exit to an angle and regain striking range. Reactive level-change with high eccentric and trunk cost; SPP only. High braking/transition cost carried in braking_demand, not in physiological intensity.
Close distance behind a safe entry, combine in the pocket, then recover stance without giving up useful pressure. Reduce output if punch quality or defensive head position collapses.
Close the escape route fast, score a short shadow combination and reset fully. Do not cross the feet or chase straight behind the opponent.
Coach signals shot after random strikes. (85% speed)
Coach-cued theme shadow at relaxed speed. Best D-1 fallback when no equipment is available.

Complete a short exchange, use a brief frame and separation, then take a valid Thai-pad knee opening and add one compact punch. Restore stance and guard immediately; release immediately after the knee. Stop if posture or stance recovery slows.
Complete a short pocket exchange, take a half-step reset, then use the holder's opening to re-enter with a compact combination. Recover stance. Do not chase at long range.

Connect at low intensity against light live resistance. Pummel for useful underhook or overhook position, establish head position and posture, then stabilise. As the partner changes position, recover useful standing connection without completing a takedown.

Contest inside hand position, forearm control, posture and balance repeatedly. Keep the feet underneath the body, the head stable and guard responsibility intact while regaining useful connection. Separate cleanly and restore guard at the end of each interval. Reduce resistance if either boxer starts wrestling or holding statically.
Continuous hip escapes down mat length.
Contract opposing muscles near end range to protect joint integrity.
Contract-relax against resistance (e.g. doorway press, glute bridge hold). 3x20s. → SPP: build into controlled eccentrics or flowing mobility reps.
Control space and cut the ring by closing angles, not chasing. Low mechanical cost; a taper-safe pressure pattern.

Control the connection, use foot position and upper-body contact to turn or reposition the partner, then separate cleanly and restore stance and guard in the better boxing position. No throws, trips, or prolonged body locks.
Controlled lengthening under band tension to stimulate tendon healing without overload.
Create a 45-degree attacking angle and reset behind the jab. Angle-creation quality, not a speed or conditioning effort.
Cue: sharp tuck, soft land. No max height intention.
Cut off the partner, hold a balanced trapping position and score two to four punches. Stop and reset if the feet cross or the stance becomes square.
Cycle through 3 submission attempts without pausing.
Cycle through named imagined cues: jab, rear straight, hook and forward entry. Use the matching defence, counter at light speed, then angle out and reset. Do not free-punch between cues.
DEADLIFT SUB: Use when axial loading contraindicated. WEIGHT: 24-32kg for athletes
Defensive MMA cage footwork: leave the fence laterally and recover center-facing stance instead of backing straight into the boundary or turning away from the opponent.
Deliver a five-second maximal-quality burst, then recover fully. Stop the burst if punch speed, shape or head position drops.
Develops Dutch-style combination striking from the clinch. (90% effort)
Develops late-round takedown defense from overhook positions. (90% effort)
Disengage, regain base, and reorient to the opponent before re-entry. Use a controlled stance reset off the break.
Double-leg takedown into standing knee strike. Reset.
Drill 3-step sub chains from guard. (85% effort)
ELBOW WARNING: Not for golfers elbow. HAMMER WEIGHT: 6-8lbs
ELBOW WARNING: Not for golfers elbow. SLEDGEHAMMER: 6-8lbs

Easy arm-leg rhythm. No sprinting, no EMOM, no hard calories. Best low-impact gas-tank option when the athlete needs conditioning but must protect joints and freshness. Can be used before or after hard sparring as a recovery flush.
Easy mobility and breathing reset; keep it restorative, not a workout.
Elevate the limb above heart level. Perform light squeezes or quad/glute sets to stimulate fluid return.
Emphasize footwork pivots and defensive slips between combos (60-70% effort)
Empty sled. No brakes at end (max effort)
Engage large muscle groups without load; avoid pain. Hold 15–30s x 3 rounds.
Enter behind a long jab, kick the called open target, regain stance, and leave on an angle. No target means no kick.
Enter behind two or three clean strikes, connect to balanced clinch position and settle before release. Stop if head position, stance or posture is lost.
Enter explosively, land two to four clean punches, then make a technical exit and regain stance. End the rep if the athlete becomes square.
Enter for one clean score and immediately take an angle before the partner can establish wrestling contact. Recover stance at safe range. Stop if the exit becomes upright or square.

Enter for short scoring exchanges, exit before wrestling contact and recover stance at long range. The partner may threaten a shot during either transition. Reduce output if the athlete stays extended or loses hip-back readiness.
Escape the ropes or corner with an L-step and reset stance to a safe angle. Lateral knee load under a change of direction.
Establish useful clinch control against light resistance, create one valid opening, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, restore stance and posture, then regain position before scoring again.
Establish useful clinch position against resistance, turn and off-balance without throwing, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, then restore position.

Exchange at close range, then deliver a compact 2–4 strike burst. Restore stance with hips underneath, balanced posture and hands ready for an appropriate takedown defence. Stop if the athlete becomes square, reaches, or cannot remain shot-ready.
Exhale fully before rounds; recover between (50% effort)
Exit laterally after an exchange, then re-enter with stance intact. Loads lateral knee and ankle more than straight-line resets.
Explosive hip-hinge option for repeated alactic power; end the set when snap speed slows.
Explosive push-off from pinned cage position.
Explosive step-in, land 1-3 straight shots, then exit immediately at an angle. Full-quality reset before the next rep.
Fast single shots only. Keep rhythm and accuracy high. Not for D-1: requires equipment.
Fire one explosive jab-cross or rear straight, retract cleanly, then make a 30-45 degree angle exit before resetting.

Flow between being pinned to the cage and holding favourable cage control. Against light live resistance, gain inside and head position, answer underhook battles, turn attempts, escapes and brief separation, then reverse or re-establish useful standing connection. Maintain awareness of controlled MMA level-change and takedown threats while keeping the exchange standing.
Focus on 3–4 joint circles or controlled articulations paired with slow nasal breathing. → SPP: convert to low-load tempo exercises for the affected region.
Focus on breathing/technique; no power output (zone 2 (50-60% effort))
Focus on crisp technique, not speed/power (light)
Focus on hip pop, not max speed (RPE 8)
Focus on hip snap, not power (light)
Focus on stability, not max distance (RPE 8)
Focused leg work; excellent for knee rehab
Forces reliance on grip/body feel over sight (30% effort)
Forward/backward alternating; no spikes in effort
From bottom position, explode to feet in one motion.
From bottom, stand up and immediately sprawl.
From butt-scoot position, walk up wall to standing.
From connection, gain useful inside arm and head position, keep posture, then recover and stabilise as the partner changes grips, angle and position with light resistance. No maximal pulling.
From connection, win safe posture control against resistance, briefly disrupt balance, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, then immediately regain a stable clinch position.

From hands and knees on firm ground, gently shift weight back and return while the wrists stay comfortable. Keep the knees down; no full plank, speed work or forced extension. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

From hands and knees on firm ground, gently shift weight between the hands through a small comfortable range. Keep both hands down; no arm reaches or instability challenge. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

From light partner connection, establish an appropriate forearm frame, create legal space, separate cleanly, and restore guard and boxing stance immediately. Reset only after balance and readiness return. Do not push the partner across the ring or hold statically.
From preferred range, enter explosively, make one clean scoring action, then exit to safe range and recover stance. Use maximal speed. Stop and reset if balance, speed or position deteriorates.
From quadruped, reach opposite arm and leg with trunk square. Stop on quality drop.

From standing connection, explosively win a useful underhook and head position against controlled resistance, stabilise posture and balance, then reset. Success is secure standing position, not takedown completion.

From standing connection, recognise the partner’s controlled level-change or takedown-entry cue, stuff the entry, regain useful head and inside position, stabilise the clinch, then reset. Success means standing clinch control is recovered; do not sprawl for conditioning or finish a takedown.
From turtle, stand up and circle out repeatedly.
Full-body conditioning; safe for most injuries

Holder applies a controlled forward-pressure cue. Land a check-hook counter, pivot off the line, then reset at safe range. Reduce speed if the athlete crosses their feet or loses defensive shape.
Holder attacks unpredictably with jab, rear straight, hook or forward entry. Read, defend or intercept, counter, then reposition. Slow the feeds if timing or stance recovery declines.
Holder feeds repeated straight-punch cues at a controlled pace. Parry, return a straight immediately, then regain guard and range before the next feed. Accuracy and clean defence come before volume.

Holder gives a controlled level-change cue and presents a mitt target. Athlete reads the cue, uses the uppercut as a specific interception option, fires once to the mitt, exits off line, then recovers stance and guard. This is not a universal takedown response; stop if the athlete guesses or loses defensive shape.

Holder gives either a forward-entry cue or a long straight cue. Read the action: teep the entry, or parry the straight and return a straight punch or kick. Make one explosive response, then recoil and recover stance, guard and range. The holder chooses the cue, not the athlete.

Holder gives one unpredictable jab, rear straight, hook or forward-entry cue. Select the correct defence or intercept, counter immediately, then reposition. Reduce cue choices if the athlete starts guessing.
Holder makes a clear forward-entry cue. Land an immediate straight stop-hit, exit off line, and reset. Use one full-quality response only; do not turn it into a combination sprint.

Holder repeats varied attack cues under a steady pace. Athlete defends or intercepts, counters accurately, then resets. Keep timing, accuracy and defensive shape intact; never chase uncontrolled punch volume.
Holder shows a jab cue. Slip outside, fire one immediate cross counter, then step to safe range and reset. Stop the set if timing slows, defence gets loose or stance recovery deteriorates.
Holder steps in with a straight-punch cue. Pull just out of range, return one straight immediately, then recover stance and distance. Every rep starts from the entry cue.

Keep comfortable daily activity and change position as needed. Reduce provoking tasks without prolonged bed rest; no cause of the back pain is inferred. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Keep comfortable ordinary elbow movement without forceful end-range work. Stiffness alone does not establish a movement restriction or its cause. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function.
