Keep ground contact <150ms. Prioritize rhythm and posture.

Keep the affected upper arm comfortably by your side and slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a pain-free range with the hand empty. Do not force end range, squeeze a ball, perform wrist curls or add resistance. A red, hot or swollen elbow needs assessment before exercise. This baseline does not diagnose lateral, medial or posterior tendon involvement. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Keep the elbow comfortably bent by the side and gently press the back of the hand into a towel against a stable wall without movement, then relax. No forced range or added resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Keep the hand relaxed and gently bend and straighten the affected fingers through a small comfortable range. Do not make a forceful fist, pull the fingers with the other hand, tap a pad or grip an object. Follow individual protection and movement restrictions and stop if the movement provokes the bruised fingers. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.
Keep the partner contained and score from a balanced stance rather than throwing nonstop. Maintain defensive head position; stop and reset whenever the athlete becomes square.

Keep the upper arm supported, palm facing up and elbow in comfortable mid-flexion. Resist gently with the other hand without movement, then relax. Keep pressure fixed; no added load or fatigue work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Kick at a controlled pace, step down in stance and take useful forward position before the next attack. Do not fall square or force a follow-up when balance is poor.
Kick only from long range, recover stance, then exit laterally before resetting. Reduce output if recoil slows or feet cross.

Kick the bag with controlled round kicks from both sides. Recoil and restore stance after every kick; do not chase volume. Reduce output if support-leg balance, accuracy or stance quality deteriorates.

Kick the held target and recoil. The partner gives an immediate forward response; exit or reposition, then restore a kick-ready defensive stance. No punch combination is required. Reduce or stop output if recoil, balance, accuracy or entry response fades.

Kick the held target, recoil and restore stance. The holder then shows either a normal striking reset or a controlled level-change threat; respond with sound defensive posture only. Do not complete a takedown.

Late-camp force-preservation pull from a fixed mid-thigh position; low-eccentric, low-soreness neural/max-force maintenance. Usable through D-7 at very low dose (2-3 x 3-5s, full rest, maximal intent). Keep total volume tiny. Not for D-6 or later.

Lean forward with your uninjured hand on a stable support and let the affected arm hang relaxed. Allow small gentle forward-and-back and side-to-side swings within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force overhead movement, add weights or perform presses. Follow any individual restrictions given by your clinician. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Lean forward with your uninjured hand on a stable support and let the affected arm hang relaxed. Gently allow small, comfortable forward-and-back and side-to-side swings. Keep the movement pain-free. Do not add weights, force the range or perform presses. Stop if symptoms worsen. Follow any individual movement restrictions given by your treating clinician.
Lie down and elevate the bruised limb. Perform light flexion/extension to improve circulation and reduce pooling.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet resting on the floor. Gently tilt the pelvis to flatten the lower back slightly, then return slowly to neutral. Keep movement small and comfortable, breathe normally, and do not force an arch or hold tension. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Lie on your back with the affected knee comfortably bent and the foot resting on the surface. Slowly let the knee move a small amount outwards, then return to the starting position within a pain-free range. Keep the pelvis supported. Do not cross the knee inward, pull it towards the chest, force a deep rotation position or add a band. This replaces the extreme seated hip-switch positions with protected rotation. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

Lie supported on your back and hold a fixed individually selected kettlebell with both hands. Slowly press and lower through a comfortable range while maintaining a gentle inward grip. No load increase or fatigue work; demand depends on the selected weight. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Light slips, rolls, parries, steps, and exits. Conversational pace only. No sharp cutting or high-output defensive bursts.
Link kicks to balanced step-down pressure and short punch combinations. Regain stance after every kick and reduce output if recoil, posture or target quality collapses.
Load 25% BW. Tall chest, steady turnover.
Load: 30% BW. No braking phase (max effort)
Load: 30% BW. Walk back = rest (max effort)
Low RPE movement with mobility and breath pacing. 3–4 rounds.
Low barrier to entry; rhythm & footwork focused
Low kick, read the partner’s escape and cut the route before scoring again. Do not follow straight behind; stop and reset if kick recoil or stance recovery breaks down.
Low load; good for mental reset and recovery flush (low (zone 2))
Low-amplitude ankle snaps for quickness. Keep contacts crisp and brief.
Low-cost anti-rotation trunk-stability support (overcoming isometric). Keep the dose tiny and intent moderate; not a maximal-strength anchor.

Low-cost grip/anti-rotation trunk support, not a maximal-strength anchor. Use only when grip/trunk work fits the athlete; keep totals tiny (2-3 short holds per side) and never chase grip or trunk fatigue. Shrink the dose from D-7 inward.
Low-cost wrestling stance-and-motion rehearsal. Maintain base while circling and changing direction so penetration and contact setups stay available without turning the session into conditioning.

Low-dose strength-retention touch, D-21 to D-8 only, and only for fighters who already train the trap-bar deadlift (familiarity_required): never introduce it cold in the final stretch. Keep it non-grinding, no failure, no back-off volume, no soreness target; stop on any bar-speed or quality loss. The taper dose caps thin sets/reps as the fight nears. Not for D-7 or later.
Low-volume punch throw from a fight stance. Keep it crisp, chest-height, and never chase fatigue.

Low-volume punch throw: 2-3 x 3 per side with full rest early, shrinking to 1-2 crisp throws as the fight nears. Micro-dose only on D-7, D-6/D-5, D-4 and D-2; med-ball throws are pulled entirely on D-3 and D-1 by the final-sharpening rules.
MMA kick-recovery footwork: regain balanced stance and takedown-ready hip position after a kick instead of admiring the strike or landing narrow and tall.
MMA open-space exit pattern: circle off a straight-line blitz or takedown entry instead of retreating directly toward the fence. Preserve stance and hip orientation for the next defensive layer.
Maintain frames against partner's forward pressure.
Maintain frequent jab output. Every jab or double jab must finish with balanced stance, defensive recovery and preferred range restored.
Maintain plum position against light resistance.

Maintain preferred range while adding a light score and reposition every 6-10 seconds. Use the fewest useful steps; no excessive bouncing, crossed feet or repeated straight retreat. Lower the pace if stance or distance control fades.
Maintain straight-shot accuracy with movement between exchanges. Speed may reduce slightly, but stance, accuracy and defensive recovery must stay clean.
Massage gun or lacrosse ball across the stuck tissue pre-movement. → SPP: replace with movement-based mobility under low load.
Max effort. Full reset between reps.
Max-effort hip toss from clinch position.
Max-power hip toss from double-collar tie.
Max-power knees to trapped bag. Full hip extension.

Maximal-strength maintenance / neural work: no eccentric, no landing, low soreness. D-13 to D-8: 2-3 x 3-5s per side with full rest; shrink to 1-2 short holds per side through D-7 and D-6/D-5. Keep out of D-4 to D-1. Not for D-1: requires equipment.
Med ball simulates opponent’s head pressure. (Explosive shots)
Micro-dose band primer for crisp jab-cross sequencing. Keep reps low, fast, and fully recovered.
Micro-support drill. Stop on quality drop.
Mid-range holds for joint stiffness without movement. Build neuromuscular confidence.
Mirror imaginary opponent while cutting off space.
Mirror partner movement at 30-40% speed. No chasing, no hard cuts, no wrestling, no competitive intensity.
Mobility tied to exhale. Repeat sequence x3 rounds full body.
Mobilize through dynamic movement. Emphasize rhythmic motion, not static stretching.
Monumental work capacity builder without impact
Move at long range behind the jab and long guard. Keep the stance narrow enough to kick, then exit laterally; lower the pace if balance changes.
Move economically in MMA stance. Enter to score, then leave before an imagined wrestling connection. Keep the centre and do not drift towards the marked boundary on consecutive exchanges.

Move economically in stance at preferred range. Every 10-15 seconds, score lightly, reposition off the return line and recover stance. Keep the pace low; reduce output if balance or foot position breaks down.
Move through safe ranges under tension. Avoid painful arcs, build capsule space.
Muay Thai ring-control pattern: apply pressure with small angle cuts so the opponent is steered toward the ropes without crossing the feet or overcommitting into kicks or knees.
Nasal breathing only. Light rhythm, footwork, relaxed punches, and easy movement. No power shots, no hard pivots, no fatigue chase. Best no-equipment gas-tank fallback.
Nasal breathing only; excellent recovery modality
Nasal-only walk. Keep shoulders relaxed and posture tall. Best after hard sparring or on recovery days when the athlete needs aerobic work without training noise.
No ground contact; bilateral stability work

No rest; focus on smooth transitions (low-moderate)

On firm level ground, perform small two-foot pogo jumps with a fixed low height. No single-leg work, added weight, increased speed or fatigue progression. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
On the advance cue, make a controlled backstep, fire a straight counter, then exit laterally and restore range.
On the holder’s advance, choose jab, teep or long kick and angle away after scoring. Stop if the choice, recoil or exit loses speed.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand and slowly bend and straighten it within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force straightening, carry weights or push through the arm. Follow any clinician-directed movement restrictions. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand. Slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force straightening, carry weights or add curl resistance. Stop if pain or swelling increases. This is gentle movement for an uncomplicated muscle strain, not a tendon tear or repair protocol.

Once pain begins to settle, support the affected elbow with your other hand. Slowly bend and straighten the elbow within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force the elbow straight, push against a wall or add resistance. Stop if pain or swelling increases. This is gentle movement for an uncomplicated muscle strain, not a tendon tear or repair protocol.

Once symptoms have settled enough for comfortable movement, lie on the affected side with the upper leg supported out of the way. Slowly lift and lower the lower leg through a small comfortable range. Keep the work pain-free and self-paced. Stop if groin pain increases during or after the work. Do not add ankle weights, cables, fast repetitions or fatigue work.

Once the ankle is less painful, sit with the foot supported and gently move it up and down or trace the alphabet. Start with a small comfortable amount and build gradually. Keep within a comfortable range; do not force movement.

Only if individually advised to use an overhead position, hold a fixed light band overhead and walk slowly over a fixed short distance. No oscillations, range increase or fatigue work. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if individually advised, perform small quick finger taps onto a firm surface with clinician-directed tape. Keep speed and force fixed. Tape does not establish readiness or protect against every injury. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly bend and straighten the elbow against a fixed light band. Do not force straightening, increase resistance or work to fatigue. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly pull a fixed light band apart through a small range and return under control. No increased tension, end-range stretch or faster movement. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the overhead position is comfortable, slowly straighten and bend the elbow against a fixed light resistance band. Do not force end range, increase band resistance or work to fatigue. This is resisted loading, not early movement. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only if the shoulder-height position is comfortable, hold the elbow bent at a right angle and gently resist external rotation with the other hand without movement. No forced position or fatigue hold. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Only when standing and weight bearing are comfortable, stand beside a stable counter and gently balance on the affected leg on firm, level ground with support available and eyes open. Stop if the ankle gives way or feels unsafe. Do not hop, use a cushion, close your eyes or work to fatigue. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
PARTNER REQUIRED: Switch attacker/defender every round
Pace like a fight, but lower output (50% effort)
Partner actively contests arm and inside position. Hand-fight to useful control, create a valid opening, score one controlled knee to Thai pads, then reset and solve the next contest. No free knee.
Partner advances intermittently. Use the jab, step-slide or backstep, then reset laterally to preferred range.

Partner alternates unpredictably between a controlled striking attack and a level-change or shot cue. Athlete reads which threat is present, uses striking defence or appropriate hip and takedown defence, makes one light counter to the pads after safe separation, then recovers stance and range. Keep shot feeds submaximal; this is not a repeated-sprawl circuit.

Partner applies controlled forward pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete reads the pressure, defends or frames, angles away, makes one light counter to the pads, regains open space, then resets in stance. Position restored is the success condition; lower pressure if footwork or defensive shape breaks down.

Partner applies controlled pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete reads the pressure, frames, uses an underhook or angle where appropriate, creates safe separation, lands one short counter to the pads, then exits into open space and restores stance. Avoid static clinch grinding; reduce pressure when posture or escape footwork fails.
Partner applies progressive resistance in all directions to simulate fight-level impacts
Partner attempts passes while you maintain guard. (low-moderate)
Partner claps to signal sprawl. Max-height jump after.
Partner contests inside position, posture, angle, turns and head or arm control. Repeatedly gain, lose or change, recover and stabilise. Reduce resistance before movement becomes wrestling.

Partner controls a committed forward or level-change cue and presents a Thai-pad target. Where technically appropriate, athlete reads the entry, intercepts the pad with one knee, recoils, then restores stance and defensive position. Never use uncontrolled live knee contact; stop if timing, balance or recoil deteriorates.
Partner counters takedown — you must immediately transition to back control. (90% explosiveness)

Partner cues a controlled forward punch or close-range entry. Read it, cover or frame to stop the entry, make an immediate knee counter, recoil and place the leg back in stance, then recover stance, frame, guard and position before the next feed. This is an entry counter, not a prolonged clinch exchange.

Partner cues a jab or rear straight. Read it, pull or slide just beyond the strike, make one immediate body- or low-kick return, recoil, then recover stance, guard and range. One clean response per effort; stop if the athlete guesses.
Partner drills only. No live sparring (RPE 8)
Partner drops ball → athlete catches + jumps. Use 2–4kg.
Partner feeds a controlled low kick during a close exchange. Check, return aggressively inside the pocket with a compact punch-kick answer, recoil the kick, and restore stance and guard.
Partner frames or creates brief separation. Maintain balance, work around the frame, reconnect, regain useful inside position and stabilise. Do not add a striking flurry.
Partner gently tugs band in random directions during single-leg stance
Partner gives a clear forward-entry cue. Read the step, intercept with a light teep, recoil the kicking leg, replace the foot, recover stance, guard and range, then accept the next feed.

Partner gives a controlled failed or defended takedown entry and presents pad targets. Athlete reads the failed entry, establishes safe position, delivers a one-to-three-strike counter, disengages, then restores stance and range before the next cue. Do not extend the exchange into grappling; lower feed density if defensive position fades.

Partner gives controlled jab, rear straight, hook or forward-entry cues. Defend or intercept, return a light counter, then regain stance and range. Keep the pace easy; reduce cue variety if the athlete guesses or loses shape.

Partner gives controlled low- and body-kick cues. Read the kick, check, make an immediate light return kick, recoil it, then recover stance and guard before the next feed. Alternate sides without chasing pace; balance and clean position end every repetition.
Partner gives controlled single attacks. Defend, counter with one to three punches, angle out, and reset before the next cue. The athlete cannot initiate freely.
Partner gives forward or lateral pressure cues. Move, pivot or L-step, regain open space, then reset stance and range.

Partner gives one clear, committed but controlled shot cue. Athlete reads it, sprawls or uses appropriate hip defence, creates safe striking separation, lands one immediate counter to the pad, then resets completely. Stop the set when reaction speed, hip position or stance recovery declines.

Partner gives one controlled short attack. Cover, answer with a compact hook and low or body kick, recoil the kick, then restore stance and guard. Fully reset; do not trade freely. Stop if stance recovery slows.

Partner gives one controlled takedown-entry cue. Athlete reads and stuffs or otherwise defends the entry, establishes safe separation, lands one short counter to the pad, exits laterally into open space, then resets completely. End the effort if it becomes prolonged wrestling or stance recovery slows.

Partner gives one low-kick cue. Read and check it, fire one explosive immediate return kick, recoil quickly, and recover stance and guard inside the effort. Stop if timing, balance, recoil or defensive shape drops.

Partner gives one unpredictable cue from a restricted set: jab, rear straight, kick, forward pressure, level change or controlled takedown entry. Athlete reads the threat, chooses a sound defence or interception, counters immediately to the pads, then repositions and recovers stance. Reduce the cue set if guessing begins and stop when reaction quality falls.
Partner gives unpredictable toss cue. Ball: 3–5kg. Emphasize snap.

Partner increases positional resistance and feeds frames, turns, posture battles, knee threats and brief separations at a high but controlled rate. Maintain decision quality: pummel, frame, re-posture, turn, off-balance, reconnect or score one controlled knee to Thai pads, then restore useful position before solving the next problem.
Partner initiates cage clinch – you must reverse or escape. (Fight pace)

Partner mixes controlled low-kick and body-kick cues. Read each feed, check, forearm-parry or step just outside range as appropriate, make one light kick return, recoil, then recover stance and defensive position. Do not preselect the defence.

Partner mixes straight-punch, low-kick, body-kick and forward-entry cues. Read and defend, evade or intercept, make a short immediate counter of no more than two strikes, then move laterally and recover stance, guard and range. The next feed waits for the reset.
Partner pins to cage – you must escape to center. (Fight pace)
Partner points direction; shooter explodes that way.

Partner repeatedly alternates unpredictably between controlled strike and takedown-entry cues. Athlete reads each threat, uses the appropriate defence, counters briefly to the pads, recovers guard and stance, then waits for the next cue without free initiation. Lower feed density if defensive shape or decision accuracy breaks down.
Partner resists – you must chain takedowns. (90% effort)
Partner resists first 5 sec, then taps. (90% squeeze)
Partner signals shot direction; shooter reacts with guillotine grip.
Partner signals shot randomly. React with sprawl then immediate takedown.
Partner starts in side control. (85% squeeze)
Partner starts in side control. (90% speed)
Partner starts in tight front headlock. (90% effort)
Partner starts in top turtle – you must recover guard or stand. (Explosive hips)
Partner tries to bench press escape. (85% control)

Partner unpredictably changes grips, frames, straightens, turns, separates or presents a knee opening. Choose to pummel, frame, re-posture, turn, reconnect, score one controlled knee or stabilise; no pre-called response.

Partner unpredictably chooses jab, rear straight, low kick or forward entry. Perceive the attack, select a suitable defence or interception, make one immediate punch, kick or teep counter, then recoil and recover stance and defensive position. Do not reveal the answer before the cue; stop if guessing begins.

Partner unpredictably feeds a controlled jab, rear straight, kick, forward entry or level-change cue. Athlete reads the threat, uses a suitable defence or interception, makes one light counter to the pads, then restores stance and range before the next feed. Keep the pace easy and reduce cue variety if the athlete starts guessing.

Partner unpredictably feeds a jab, rear straight, low kick, body kick or forward entry. Athlete cannot initiate: read the attack, choose a sound defence or interception, counter immediately, recoil kicks, then recover stance and defensive position with a lateral reset. Lower the feed rate when choices or shape deteriorate.

Partner unpredictably presents a short punch attack, low- or body-kick cue, brief close-range entry, or cover opening. Read the exchange; cover, check, catch, or parry as appropriate; answer compactly with punches or a kick, then recoil and restore stance and guard before resetting or re-engaging. Use a controlled Thai-pad knee only on a valid close-range opening.

Partner unpredictably provides controlled strikes, kicks, level changes, takedown entries or pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete cannot freely initiate: read, defend or intercept, counter briefly to the pads, recover stance or open space, then wait for the next problem. Lower cue density when choices, mechanics or defensive recovery deteriorate.

Partner varies controlled short punch attacks. Cover, catch, or roll as appropriate; answer with a short punch and low kick, recoil the kick, then restore stance and guard before the next cue. Win each exchange, then restore position.

Partner varies the timing and side of controlled low- and body-kick feeds. Read, check, make an immediate kick return, recoil, and recover stance and guard before every new cue. Reduce feed rate if balance, timing or defensive shape fades.
Passive recovery aid to flush DOMS. 15–20 mins soak or 5 cycles of hot/cold shower. → SPP: reserve for high soreness or poor sleep.

Perform a small two-foot jump onto a fixed foam pad and settle the landing. Keep the height and surface fixed; no repeated bouncing or perturbation. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Perform one small lateral hop on firm level ground and settle the landing before the next attempt. Keep distance fixed; no fast repeated hops or contact. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place both hands against a stable wall at chest height and gently press without moving the shoulders. Release between comfortable holds. Do not increase force, extend the hold to fatigue or add resisted movement within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place both hands on a stable raised table and perform a slow supported incline push-up through a comfortable elbow range, then return. Keep the support height fixed. Do not transition to floor work, a reverse tabletop or speed work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the affected hand against a stable wall at a comfortable height and hold gently without moving. No climbing higher, forced overhead position or added resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the affected hand lightly on a stable wall with the elbow comfortably straight. Slowly slide the hand through a small comfortable range; do not lock or force the elbow, press hard or add resistance. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Place the forearms on a foam roller against a wall. Slowly slide only through a comfortable range and return under control. Use no additional band or weight; do not force overhead range. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Posterior chain: hips low, fast stand-up. GPP: reduce to 5 sets.
Posterior chain: keep hips low on the sprawl. GPP: limit to 3 sets.

Protect the affected toe from being bent backwards again. Pause provoking push-off, tiptoe work, running and jumping. Rest the foot in a comfortable supported position. Follow any individually prescribed footwear, walking support or weight-bearing restriction without changing it. The affected toe, joint stability and injury grade need assessment before toe curls, stretching or loaded forefoot work; this guidance does not diagnose turf toe. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

Protect the bruised back of the upper arm from contact, heavy pressing and resisted elbow straightening. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow individual movement/support restrictions. Do not apply vibration balls, force an overhead stretch or increase arm-circle range to test recovery. Automatic stretching or resistance work needs an assessed injury and is not prescribed here. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised elbow from contact, leaning on the injured area, heavy carrying and forceful pressing. Support the arm comfortably without pressure on the bruise and follow any individual sling or movement restriction. Do not apply a massage gun or push the elbow against a wall to build contact tolerance. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised fingers from catching impacts, punching, heavy grip and direct pressure. Rest the hand comfortably supported and follow any prescribed finger protection or movement restriction. Do not tap the fingers on a pad, grip a cold ball or roll the injured tissue to test contact tolerance. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised forearm from contact, heavy grip work and resisted wrist movement. Support the arm comfortably without pressing on the bruise and follow any prescribed support or movement restriction. Do not roll a ball over the injured tissue or use a band as a recovery flush. Increasing tight swelling, abnormal sensation or circulation needs assessment rather than further loading. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised front of the upper arm from contact, heavy pulling and repeated resisted elbow bending. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow individual movement/support restrictions. Avoid direct massage or percussion, forceful stretching and faster arm swings to test tolerance. A muscle bruise label does not exclude deeper muscle or tendon injury; automatic resistance or stretching is not prescribed. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised hand from heavy gripping, carrying, punching and direct pressure. Rest it comfortably supported and follow any individually prescribed hand protection. Do not use contrast heat, ball pressure or a resisted grip squeeze as automatic treatment. New loss of movement or grip, excessive or increasing swelling, or altered sensation needs assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised heel from repeated hard landings, running and direct pressure. Rest the foot comfortably supported and reduce provoking standing or walking. Follow any clinician-advised footwear, heel support or weight-bearing restriction. Do not tap or roll the bruised heel to desensitize it, start barefoot loading or assume that heel tenderness rules out a bone injury. The app does not distinguish heel-pad from deeper heel injury, so automatic exercises remain unavailable. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Protect the bruised shin from kicks, pad contact and kneeling pressure. Rest the leg comfortably supported and reduce provoking prolonged standing or walking. Follow any clinician-prescribed support or weight-bearing restriction. Do not use sticks, percussion devices or rollers over the bruise, or test contact tolerance. The exact depth of the impact injury is not established, so direct shin loading and automatic exercises remain unavailable. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised shoulder from repeated contact, heavy lifting and provoking reaching. Support the arm comfortably when resting and follow any individual sling or movement restriction. Do not press a ball or percussion device into the bruise, hang from a trap bar or add band resistance. This protection guidance does not establish structural healing or readiness for contact. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the bruised thigh from further blows, deep squatting, kicking and provoking knee loading. Rest the leg comfortably supported and follow any clinician-prescribed position, wrap, walking support or movement restriction. Do not massage, use a percussion gun, force a thigh stretch or deepen a wall sit. Do not set or remove a bent-knee brace yourself; the extent of the contusion and safe knee movement need individual assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Protect the bruised wrist from contact, heavy grip, pushing through the hand and repeated provoking wrist loading. Rest the forearm and hand comfortably supported and follow prescribed splint or movement restrictions. Do not roll or tap the bruise, add glove impact or remove protection because its colour fades. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Protect the elbow from repeat over-straightening. Pause pressing, throwing, forceful lockout and resisted elbow work. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow any individually prescribed sling or movement restriction. Do not test stability, push into full extension or begin wall presses. The hospital movement advice assumes an assessed soft-tissue injury without broken bones; an app hyperextension label does not establish that assessment. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

Protect the injured finger from being pulled or bent backwards. Avoid gripping against resistance, catching impacts and contact work. Rest the hand comfortably supported. Follow any hand-therapist splint or strapping instructions exactly; do not change the finger position, undo the splint for app exercises or decide when to stop wearing it. Finger exercises need the assessed injury and individual protection plan; no automatic stretching or finger holds are prescribed. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

Protect the injured hand from repeated backward bending, forceful gripping and contact impacts. Support the hand comfortably at rest and avoid using it to bear body weight. Follow any individually prescribed hand protection and movement restrictions. The exact injured joint and safe movement range need assessment; do not pull fingers backwards, perform backhand wall crawls or follow a generic wrist or finger exercise protocol. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

Protect the injured joint and avoid exercise or activity that aggravates it. During the first few days of a new sprain, rest from loading it and avoid massage or forced stretching. Follow any clinician-directed support or movement restrictions. Seek assessment for severe or worsening pain, deformity, inability to use the joint or loss of sensation.

Protect the shoulder from repeat backward overstretching. Pause provoking reaching behind the body, bottom-range pressing, heavy lifting and contact work. Support the arm comfortably at rest and follow any individually prescribed sling or movement restriction without changing it. Do not test shoulder stability, force range or introduce band presses. Movement rehabilitation needs the assessed injury and individual restrictions; this guidance does not establish that the joint is stable. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. Sit on a stable chair with both feet flat on the floor. Keeping the front of both feet on the floor, slowly raise both heels within a comfortable range and slowly lower them to the floor. Sit or lie with the affected leg supported on a smooth surface. Gently slide the heel towards you to bend the knee, then slide back to straighten within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not force movement, stand on an unstable surface or add resistance. Stop and seek assessment if the knee locks, repeatedly gives way or cannot bear weight. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit supported with the affected arm relaxed by your side. Gently draw the shoulder blade back and down without forcing the shoulder into end range, then relax. Sit upright with shoulders relaxed. Slowly turn the head a small comfortable amount to one side, then return to the middle. Sit upright with the affected elbow comfortably bent and tucked by your side. Gently turn the forearm outwards within a small comfortable pain-free range, then return. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit upright with the upper arm by your side and one fixed clinician-selected dumbbell. Bend the elbow and lower under control within the individually advised range. Do not use an incline stretch position, increase weight or work to fatigue. The selected weight and tendon site require individual assessment. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the affected elbow by your side and the forearm comfortably supported. With the hand empty and wrist relaxed, slowly turn the palm upwards and downwards within a small pain-free range. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected foot flat on the floor and the knee bent. Slowly lift the heel within a comfortable pain-free range, then lower it to floor level with the forefoot resting on the floor. Do not add weight, stand on a step, drop below floor level or bounce. This is seated movement, not a strength test or a required isometric-first protocol. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected forearm supported on a table and the hand relaxed. Gently bend and straighten the wrist within a small comfortable pain-free range. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Sit with the affected lower leg supported and the foot free to move. Slowly move the ankle a small amount upwards and downwards around a comfortable middle range. Stop and seek assessment for catching, locking or a blocked movement. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

Sit with the leg supported and a resistance band around the forefoot. Slowly point and release the foot within a comfortable range against a fixed light band. No increase in band tension or speed within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the leg supported. Move the ankle slowly in a small comfortable circle against one fixed light resistance band; do not increase tension or speed. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Sit with the upper arm relaxed by your side and the hand empty. Slowly bend and straighten the affected elbow through a small comfortable range, stopping short of pain. Do not press on a wall, lean on the bruise, force straightening or add resistance. Follow any clinician movement restriction; this is movement only, not pushing or contact preparation. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.
Skill rhythm and timing with low impact
Slips, pivots, rolls at conversational pace
Slow stance switches, step-throughs, and angle exits. No explosive push-offs, no bouncing, no hard pivots.
Smooth nasal rowing with controlled stroke rate. No sprint pulls. Strong aerobic-base option when running impact is not suitable. Can sit before or after hard sparring if kept easy.
Spine: brace hard, no rounding under load. Weight 25-35% BW.
Spine: no flexion under load. Taper: reduce to 3/side.
Sprawl, then explode into double-leg shot. Full recovery between reps.
Sprawl, then spring up into 2 knees + 2 elbows.
Sprint 10m, drop to guillotine grip, reset. Repeat.
Stalk at a controlled pace while keeping stance width and head position. Do not cross the feet or chase straight behind an imagined opponent; reset stance after every entry.

Stand beside a stable support and lean slightly forwards with the uninjured hand supporting you. Let the affected arm hang relaxed, then gently allow a small slow forward-and-back pendulum movement within a comfortable range. Keep the hand empty; do not hang from a bar, pull the shoulder, swing forcefully, add weight or force range. Follow any clinician movement restriction and stop if this provokes the bruised shoulder. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Stand facing a smooth wall with a cloth under the affected hand. Gently slide the hand upwards only through a comfortable range no higher than shoulder level, then return. Do not lean body weight heavily into the arm, force a painful arc, add resistance or lift overhead. Keep the neck comfortable; no forced chin tuck or posture correction is required. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

Stand up from a grappling exchange into a balanced grappling stance, regain base, and reset distance or connection position. Appropriate as a controlled BJJ/MMA stand-up transition rather than a striking reset.

Stand with both feet on a fixed foam pad beside stable support and make small slow knee bends without bouncing or jumping. Keep depth fixed; no partner contact. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Start facing wall, coach gives go-cue. Jump straight up.

Start from a compressed distance cue. Restore preferred range, score once, reposition, then repeat at a demanding pace. Do not retreat straight back on consecutive actions. Reduce output if stance or balance breaks down.

Start from an already-secured mount, half-guard top, or stable postured guard-top position. Maintain base and posture through a compact 3–5 second punch or padded-strike burst. Regain stable posture and base, then fully reset. Stop when output compromises position.

Start in an unfavourable cage relationship. Establish useful inside and head position, turn the partner to reverse the position, gain favourable cage control and stabilise before resetting. Do not slam or throw. Stabilise standing control without converting the turn into takedown completion.

Start near the cage, not fixed against it. The partner gives short striking exchanges, occasional shot or brief tie-up threats, and lateral movement. Strike compactly, stay balanced, use appropriate defence, then angle or reset when position collapses and restore stance and base. The goal is scoring safely, not driving the partner backwards.
Start with 60–90s foam roll across main tension zones, then add 3x15s PNF contract-relax sets. → SPP: progress to dynamic end-range mobility drills (e.g. CARS, banded openers).
Step out of range, pivot off line, then reset stance before re-entry. Moderate hip-rotation and single-side braking cost.
Stick landings. Full reset between reps (max effort)
Strengthen joint control. 3 reps per direction, per joint.
Sub towel hangs if no rope (max effort)

Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist free to move. With the hand empty, raise the wrist in the comfortable range, within any clinician restrictions, then slowly lower over five seconds. Keep the forearm supported. No dumbbell, band, forceful grip, forced end range, speed or automatic increase. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist over the edge and one fixed clinician-selected dumbbell in the hand. Assist the lift with the other hand, then slowly lower within the individually advised range. Do not increase speed or load. This extensor exercise does not apply automatically to medial or posterior elbow pain. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the affected forearm palm-down on a table with the wrist over the edge and one fixed clinician-selected dumbbell in the hand. Use the other hand to assist the lift, then slowly lower the wrist within the individually advised range. Do not force end range or increase weight, speed or volume. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the affected forearm palm-up on a table with the wrist over the edge and one fixed clinician-selected dumbbell. Assist the lift with the other hand, then slowly lower within the individually advised range. Do not force a stretch, increase weight or add faster work. This flexor exercise does not apply automatically to thumb-side tenosynovitis. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the affected hand and gently bend and straighten the injured finger within a comfortable pain-free range. Do not push it with the other hand, pull against a band, tap forcefully or add grip resistance. Follow any clinician-directed protection; do not bend a joint that you have been instructed to keep splinted straight. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the affected hand with the wrist comfortable. Gently bend and straighten the injured finger within a small pain-free range, then relax. Do not force a locked finger, pull it with the other hand, use putty or squeeze a ball. Stop if the finger catches or locks; follow any clinician-directed splint restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Support the affected hand with the wrist comfortable. Start with the fingers straight, gently bend the middle and end joints into a small hook while keeping the knuckles straight, then return. Stay within a comfortable pain-free range; do not force a fist, squeeze a ball or add putty, bands or grip resistance. Stop if a finger catches or locks; follow any clinician-directed splint restrictions. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.

Support the forearm and gently squeeze one soft ball with the wrist comfortable, then relax. Keep pressure fixed; no harder ball or fatigue holds. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the forearm and hold the wrist in comfortable mid-range flexion against a fixed light band, then relax. Do not force end range or lengthen the hold to fatigue. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the forearm on a table with the empty relaxed hand free beyond the edge. Gently move the wrist a small comfortable amount upwards and downwards. No stick, grip, weight, resistance, forced stretch or pressure through the hand. Follow clinician restrictions. Stop if activity makes symptoms worse or causes new symptoms. Seek assessment for persistent or worsening symptoms or reduced everyday function. Get urgent help for major trauma, deformity, inability to use or bear weight, marked or increasing swelling, a hot/red joint, fever or feeling unwell, locking/giving way, altered sensation, progressive weakness or circulation changes. This guidance does not identify the cause, establish healing or provide contact clearance.

Support the forearm on a table with the hand relaxed and free to move beyond the edge. Slowly move the wrist a small amount upwards and downwards within a comfortable non-provoking range. Keep the hand empty and do not grip, stretch with the other hand, press on the bruise or add resistance. Follow individual splint and movement restrictions. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the activity. Seek assessment for increasing or excessive swelling, an expanding lump or hematoma, inability to use or bear weight on the limb, or major loss of function. Seek urgent help for severe pain with tense swelling, compartment syndrome concern, altered sensation, a cold limb or circulation changes, an open wound, or suspected fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions; CALM or RESTORE is not return-to-contact clearance.

Support the forearm with the wrist neutral. Gently resist the other hand without movement, then relax. Use only this fixed neutral position; do not add angles, weight or fatigue holds. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the hand and hold the fingers gently spread against one fixed light mini-band, then relax. Do not force joint range, increase tension or extend holds to fatigue. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the hand and slowly open the fingers against a fixed light band, then release. No flicking, increased tension or fatigue work. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the hand and slowly spread the fingers against one fixed light band, then release. Do not force the injured joint, increase resistance or work to fatigue. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

Support the upper arm and hold the elbow in comfortable mid-flexion against gentle resistance from the other hand, then relax. Keep pressure fixed. No weights, dynamic curls or fatigue progression within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Switch stance in air. Light contact, fast rhythm.
Switch stance to reset lead-leg kicking options and recover a balanced base after a missed or thrown kick. Hip-rotation dominant.
Switch stances every 3 steps while navigating cones.

Take repeated realistic body-kick opportunities. Reduce or stop output if recoil slows, support-leg balance deteriorates, accuracy falls, or stance cannot be restored.
Target surrounding areas without pressing directly on the bruise. May reduce perceived stiffness.
Technical Olympic-lift option for experienced MMA and wrestling athletes during GPP only; use low-volume, crisp reps.
The holder advances lightly. Score with a jab, teep or long kick, recover stance, and exit laterally rather than retreating straight back. Lower the pace if the exit becomes a straight retreat.
The holder advances unpredictably. Intercept only when the entry is genuinely there, recover stance, and take a short angle. Stop if recoil or balance slows.

The holder changes distance without inviting pursuit. Maintain a credible kick-led threat, select a kick suited to the available range, recoil and regain useful position. Reduce feed density if recoil, balance, accuracy or stance recovery deteriorates.
The holder gives one controlled short attack. Cover in a high guard, return 2-4 compact punches, then restore guard and stance. Fully reset; do not trade freely.

The holder gives one controlled short punching action. Smother its punching space, establish brief arm or forearm control, separate into legal punching space, land one or two short punches to the mitts, then reset stance and guard. Stop if control is skipped or live head contact develops.
The holder moves and presents an actual body target. Recognise the opportunity, kick explosively, recoil and restore stance. No target means no kick.

The holder presents a meaningful low, body or high pad target. Read it, select the appropriate kick, recoil and restore stance. Reduce feed density if recoil slows, support-leg balance or accuracy deteriorates, the athlete becomes square, or stance cannot be restored.
The holder presents the open body or head target. Switch levels with 2-4 compact hooks, uppercuts, or short straights, then regain guard and stance. Stop if mechanics deteriorate.

The holder varies body, head, and leg target availability. Build compact 2-4 strike punch-kick exchanges, recoil each kick, and restore stance and guard between exchanges. Read the open target rather than repeating a fixed combination.

The partner advances from just outside scoring range. Make one short lateral or angled escape, recover stance and face the partner at usable range. Do not turn it into a long retreat. Stop and reset if speed, balance or position deteriorates.

The partner applies controlled forward pressure. Escape with a short lateral or angled action, recover stance at usable range, score once, then reset. Do not rely on prolonged straight retreat. Reduce output if the escape no longer restores position.
The partner attempts left and right fence escapes. Deny the route with feet and position before scoring; stop and reset if the athlete reaches, crosses feet or becomes square.

The partner briefly crowds from a safe live position. Use stance, frame, angle or a short intercept to leave before a wrestling connection settles. Regain open space before scoring again. Stop if posture, defence or level-change recognition breaks down.
The partner changes direction throughout. Cut the escape route before throwing and do not follow in a straight line; lower the pace if stance integrity is lost.

The partner changes distance with controlled forward or lateral pressure. Restore preferred range with one short retreat and an angle when needed; do not retreat straight back on consecutive actions. Recover stance before the next cue.

The partner crosses preferred range without a fixed rhythm. Intercept only when the crossing action is clear, then leave the return line and restore range. Stop and reset if timing, stance or positional control deteriorates.
The partner cues a left, right or backward escape. Select the correct cutoff, regain position, then score; no correct position means no forced attack.
The partner enters aggressively from shot range. Intercept with one appropriate long strike and angle out before body contact. Stop the set if reaction speed, stance or defensive shape drops.
The partner escapes left or right; reposition immediately and re-establish pressure before scoring. Cut the route rather than following, then reset fully.

The partner establishes one controlled brief tie-up. Frame and create safe separation, fire a compact 2–3 strike combination on the break, then restore stance and base. Reset if the tie-up becomes prolonged hand fighting.

The partner gives one unpredictable cue: striking advance, genuine level change or no entry. Select an intercept and exit, shot defence, or patient range hold. Do not force an action. Stop if response speed or stance drops.

The partner mixes normal movement with genuine level changes. Maintain range, angle off or move the hips back as needed. Only sprawl when the partner can reach the legs, then restore stance and preferred range.

The partner mixes striking advances, genuine level changes and feints. Identify the threat before choosing range, angle, hip-back defence or a sprawl. Reset at preferred range. Reduce output if recognition becomes late.

The partner presents a kickable target and range, a punching entry or a controlled level-change threat. Choose to kick, reposition or defend; not kicking is a correct repetition. Reduce output if stance recovery, accuracy or threat recognition fades.

The partner repeatedly enters from striking or shot range. Intercept when safe, take an angle and recover open space before the next entry. Do not admire the score. Reduce output if exits become straight or late.

The partner sometimes removes the target or blocks the entry. After a miss, rebuild stance, protect the hips and exit before body contact. Do not chase the failed score. Reduce output if recovery needs more than one step.

The partner unpredictably enters, holds or gives ground. Choose whether to enter, hold range, intercept or exit, then recover stance and preferred range before the next cue. Reduce output if decisions become automatic or position breaks down.

The partner unpredictably presents a short striking exchange, a genuine committed shot, or no shot. Exchange compactly, defend only when necessary, make a brief strike return or safe separation, and restore stance and base before the next exchange.

The partner unpredictably presents a short striking exchange, level change, genuine committed shot, brief tie-up, or disengagement. Choose whether to continue the exchange, defend, frame, create safe separation, strike on the break, reset, or re-engage. Restore stance and base after each action; responses are not pre-called.

The partner unpredictably pummels, frames, changes level, turns, separates, pressures towards the cage, circles away or shows a short-strike opening. Choose to pummel, frame, gain an underhook and head position, stuff the level change, turn, separate, make one controlled pad strike or reconnect. Keep decisions sustainable and recover standing control; responses are not pre-called.

The partner unpredictably ties one arm, squares chest-to-chest, presses inward, begins separating, exposes brief punching space, or smothers offence. Without a pre-called response, choose to frame, regain inside position, turn, smother, separate, or punch the mitts when legal space appears. Restore stance and guard after each exchange and lower resistance if decisions or balance deteriorate.

The partner varies range and posture. Throw one hard low kick only when stance is stable, the target is available and the partner is not entering deeply. Recoil to defensive stance. No safe window means no kick.
Throw 3-4 compact hooks or uppercuts in the pocket. Restore the high guard and stance immediately. Stop if punch mechanics, stance, or guard recovery deteriorate.
Throw a short, compact punch combination in the pocket, then an immediate low or body kick. Recoil the kicking leg and restore stance and guard. Stop if kick recoil, stance recovery, or guard slows.
Throw controlled low or body kicks, recoil cleanly and finish with the hips under the body in a stance ready for a punch or takedown threat. Reduce output if balance, recoil or stance recovery fades.
Throw one maximum-quality rear body or low kick. Recoil fully and restore a balanced defensive stance before resting.
Tire weight 50-70% deadlift 1RM. Drive with the hips, not the low back.
Toss ball forward during jump. 2kg ball max.
Touch all 8 cage sections in sequence.
Touch-speed bag rhythm only; no hard rounds or volume accumulation.
Trace letters with toes while standing on one leg
Train in shortened range away from end-range stretch. Focus on deceleration and reverse control.
Turn the corner off a check-hook pattern and pivot out to an angle. Fight-specific pivot; single-leg pivot loading.
Two-step shuffle on cue, then freeze tall. Keep contacts quiet and volume tiny.

Under higher live resistance, the partner unpredictably creates an underhook battle, cage pin or reversal, frame, level change, separation, short-strike opening, circle-away or takedown-entry opportunity. Choose to pummel, frame, gain head and inside position, defend the level change, turn, separate, make one controlled pad strike, establish an entry position or reconnect. Preserve decisions under fatigue and recover standing control; do not finish takedowns.
Upper body glycolytic work; lower body unloaded
Upper body: reduce waves if shoulder turnover slows.
Upper-focused power work with lower body stability
Use 2–4kg ball. Minimize effort, maximize intent and speed.
Use a basic teep to control range. Retract cleanly, restore stance and regain long range before repeating. Reduce output if recoil, balance or stance quality deteriorates.

Use a clean strike entry to move the partner towards the fence, connect position, then score again. Cut the lateral escape before attacking and reduce output if stance or defensive responsibility collapses.
Use a fixed cue sequence: jab to slip, straight to parry, hook to roll. Add one light counter after each defence, then recover stance and range before the next cue.
Use a light load and full recovery; prioritize jump height and bar speed over load.
Use a light medicine ball and full rest; drive from the hips and transfer force through the torso without chasing fatigue.
Use a marked boundary. Manage the partner and boundary together. Reposition laterally rather than retreating straight on consecutive exchanges, and regain open space before starting again.

Use a marked boundary. Score while protecting open-space position. Circle before the boundary blocks the exit and refuse prolonged backward drift. Reduce output if stance, level-change awareness or boundary checks deteriorate.

Use a marked boundary. The partner mixes passive movement, striking pressure, level changes and boundary cuts. Choose long strikes, patient range holds, angles or shot defence without automatic sprawls. Reduce output if decisions become guessed or cage awareness fades.

Use a marked boundary. The partner repeatedly advances from open range. Escape laterally with movement, a strike or frame, then regain open space before the next exchange. Never retreat straight on consecutive exchanges. Reduce output if cage awareness drops.
Use a split stance, light-to-moderate load, and full rest; drive through the floor and finish fast.

Use a stable wall for support. Rise onto both forefeet on level ground and hold a comfortable heel height, then lower. No external load, single-leg variant or fatigue work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
Use a technically clean, submaximal clean load. End the interval if bar path or burpee mechanics deteriorate.

Use an open-space lane with one edge marked as the limited-space boundary. The partner changes distance and position. Kick only when posture and space allow, then recoil; reposition instead when a kick would weaken stance. Reduce output if stance recovery or decisions fade.

Use an open-space lane with one edge marked as the limited-space boundary. The partner varies usable kick space, compressed range, forward pressure and lateral escape. Choose to kick, reposition, frame or reset without pursuing or wall wrestling. Reduce output if stance or decisions fade.
Use bands or unstable surfaces to challenge joint control and proprioception under minimal load.
Use bands to pull joint into slight instability during slow reps (e.g. banded wall squats). → SPP: progress to reactive reps or light load with control.
Use bands, BOSU, or unstable surfaces. Controlled tempo x 3 sets.
Use bodyweight or a very light load for 3-5 sets of 3 reps with full rest; stop when jump height drops.

Use controlled low or body kicks. Recoil cleanly, regain balance and restore stance before repeating; never rush volume. Reduce or stop output if recoil, support-leg balance, accuracy or stance quality deteriorates.
Use controlled short pocket exchanges with body-head variation, a high guard, and stable head position. Briefly reset between exchanges. Keep a sustainable pace and do not chase across the ring.
Use elastic wrap during movement if needed. Add unloaded full-ROM circles pre-training. → SPP: taper wrap use unless re-aggravation risk is present.
Use jab and teep to halt or redirect the holder’s advance. Recover stance before moving and reset if preferred range is lost.
Use light band tension to open joint space while moving through low-load range of motion.
Use light band tension. Stay upright with fast exchange.
Use light cage-orientation steps. Keep the stance and hips oriented to the opponent while controlling the escape lane; do not chase into open space.

Use light continuous partner resistance. Gain inside hand or forearm position, keep the feet underneath the body and maintain posture as the partner changes arm position. Regain useful connection, then separate under control and restore stance and guard. No takedowns, neck cranking, or extended collar ties.
Use light resistance bands. Emphasize speed over height.
Use long guard, teep feints and lateral steps to escape pressure, then restore preferred range. Do not rely on repeated straight-line retreat.
Use the jab to enter, take a useful forward position and reset stance after each entry. No clear target means no forced attack; circle out and rebuild.
Use the teep only from a measured range. Recover the kicking leg into stance before moving, then circle as the bag returns. Reset if the bag movement pulls the stance out of shape.
Use wall to control inversion angle. (Technical)

Using a fixed light resistance band, slowly raise the arms into a comfortable Y position and lower under control. Do not force overhead range, increase band tension or work to fatigue. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.
WEIGHT: 6-8kg. SPINE RULE: No flexion under load
Walk opponent down at 30-40% effort. Step, feint, angle, reset. No bouncing, no hard pivots, no fatigue chase.

When comfortable movement is possible, lie on your back with both knees bent and feet supported close to your hips. Gently lift into a double-leg bridge and hold briefly at a comfortable height, then lower. Keep the work pain-free and self-paced. Do not walk the feet out, straighten the knees, add resistance or work to fatigue.

When pain no longer prevents comfortable movement, sit with your foot supported on a towel on a smooth floor. Gently slide the foot to bend and straighten the affected knee within a pain-free range. Keep the movement slow and self-paced. Do not force knee flexion, add resistance or increase speed. Stop if movement becomes painful or symptoms worsen.

When pain no longer stops comfortable movement, sit with the foot supported and gently bend and straighten the affected toe within a small pain-free range. Do not pull the toe into a stretch, push off through it, hop or add resistance. Follow any clinician-directed protection; a deformed toe or inability to move it needs assessment. Stop if pain, slipping or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

When pain no longer stops movement, gently move your shoulder and arm through a comfortable range. Go at your own pace and stop before pain prevents movement. Avoid forced chest stretches, resisted chest flies and surgical-repair routines.

When standing and weight bearing are comfortable, practise balancing on the affected leg on firm ground, close to a stable counter for support. Start with a short comfortable attempt and build gradually. Keep support available; do not use a cushion or close your eyes.

When weight bearing and gentle calf movement are comfortable, use a stable support and practise controlled heel lowering as shown in the linked ankle rehabilitation guidance. Work at your own pace, up to 2 sets on alternate days. The source gives no repetition target; stop before symptoms worsen.

Win or maintain useful standing clinch position, take one short controlled punch or knee opportunity on the pad, and immediately recover head and arm position as the partner contests. Reposition, keep awareness of the MMA takedown threat, and strike again only when control allows. A strike that collapses connection is a poor rep.

With a fixed cable load and thick grip attachment, slowly bend and straighten the elbow through a comfortable range. Keep the upper arm still. Do not increase resistance, accelerate the movement or work to fatigue. Demand depends on the individually selected cable load. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With a fixed light mini-band and knees comfortably bent, take slow small sideways steps on level ground. Keep band tension and step size fixed; no faster steps or fatigue work. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With a securely anchored landmine bar and an individually selected fixed load, slowly press through a comfortable range and lower under control. No load, tempo or range progression within this drill. This is resisted loading, not an early movement exercise. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With a securely anchored light resistance band, slowly bring the arms together in front of the chest through a comfortable range, then return under control. Keep resistance and speed fixed. Avoid a forced chest stretch, increased tension or fatigue work. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With one fixed clinician-selected band, raise the affected arm in the scapular plane only to an individually advised comfortable height below shoulder level and hold without movement, then lower. Do not increase height, band tension or hold to fatigue. This does not isolate one tendon. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With the arm at shoulder height only if that position is comfortable, gently press against a stable wall without movement, then relax. Keep pressure fixed. Do not force the position or add resistance. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With the elbow comfortably bent and hand against a stable wall, gently try to straighten the elbow without movement, then relax. Keep pressure fixed. No longer fatigue holds or punching progression within this drill. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With the foot supported on level ground, gently press through the affected forefoot without movement, then relax. Keep pressure fixed; no forced toe extension or explosive push-off. Stop if pain, giving way or symptoms worsen during or after the work.

With your back supported against a stable wall and both feet planted, lower only into a comfortable partial squat and hold, then stand. Keep the knee angle and bodyweight demand fixed.
